ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How moodle create itemid for media files?
ResponsesInList.Text: You'd have to look at the internal code of the Lesson activity to find out exactly where the files are stored. The details you need will be something like: contextid - the activity context component - "mod_lesson" file area - according to https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/master/mod/lesson/lib.php#L1310 the file areas used by lesson are "page_contents", "mediafile", "page_answers", "page_responses", "essay_responses" - so you will need to choose the appropriate area to get the file you want from itemid - that varies based on the file area you are getting details from - take a look at the lesson_pluginfile() function ( https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/master/mod/lesson/lib.php#L1261 ) to see what the different itemids mean

ResponsesInList.Text:
If it's any help, I did an SQL query that pulls in all courses, and then if the blocks.id and blocks.blockname are null then that course needs to have the block added (the left join takes care of that) 
```text
SELECT DISTINCT course.id, course.shortname, course.fullname, blocks.id , blocks.blockname, blocks.parentcontextid  FROM database_name_here.mdl_course as course
	inner join moodle_2015.mdl_context as 
context

    on context.instanceid = course.id
	left join moodle_2015.mdl_block_instances as blocks
    on blocks.blockname = "choose_name_of_block"
       AND context.id = blocks.parentcontextid ;
```
 Note this is pure SQL, if using Moodle to query it will be slightly different Just update the database name and the name of the block to get the results

ResponsesInList.Title: Frankenstyle not required for Activity, still recommended?
ResponsesInList.Text: As written in the exception section of this page , it's not required to use the full Frankenstein naming, when it comes to database tables of acitivies, i.e. the mod_ part can be drop. The wiki page however isn't clear about, whether it's still recommended to use mod_ or whether it would have a side effect for older Moodle versions. Should I add the mod_ prefix to my database tables of my activity plugin?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Frankenstyle not required for Activity, still recommended?
ResponsesInList.Text: It is still good practice to use "mod_" as the prefix for your activity module data tables. The exception is there primarily to allow backward compatibility, but new modules should use that convention. mike

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Frankenstyle not required for Activity, still recommended?
ResponsesInList.Text: But, with the major caveat, that if your plugin is called 'myplugin', the main table (referenced by the 'instance' field in the course module object) must be called 'myplugin' not 'mod_myplugin', or Moodle will be unable to retrieve important data from it (and, given that, I'd probably encourage the rest of the DB tables for the plugin to skip the 'mod_' part as well, in order to keep them together alphabetically).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Frankenstyle not required for Activity, still recommended?
ResponsesInList.Text: Not sure if that made things clearer or added more confusion. :D Should I now prefix my activity database table with mod_ or not? The wiki makes it sound likes it's an option, but doesn't has to be strictly followed.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Frankenstyle not required for Activity, still recommended?
ResponsesInList.Text: Simple answer - if your plugin is called 'myplugin' and you call the database table 'mod_myplugin' you will get a fatal error (unless this has recently changed in Moodle and I haven't noticed), as Moodle won't be able to find the table to extract the activity instance name + (if relevant) the intro fields. You must call this table 'myplugin' (again, I'm willing to be corrected if there's been a recent change to Moodle that allows for 'mod_myplugin' to work). For the rest of the tables that your plugin uses internally (e.g. 'myplugin_pages', 'myplugin_grades', 'myplugin_otherstuff'), you are completely free to name them as you want (but, normally, they'd start 'myplugin_').

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Frankenstyle not required for Activity, still recommended?
ResponsesInList.Text: Okay, thanks for the clarification! Might be useful to update the wiki to not make it sound like it's an optional exception.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Frankenstyle not required for Activity, still recommended?
ResponsesInList.Text: Just to be sure my information wasn't out of date, I've checked the core code (now that I'm back in front of a computer where it was easy to do so): https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/master/course/lib.php#L1122 The above line looks for a table called $rawmods[$seq]->modname, which is the activity name, without the 'mod_' prefix - there is no provision for finding a table with the 'mod_' prefix. You may be able to get around this by using the PLUGINNAME_get_coursemodule_info function in your lib.php, to provide the name + intro data, before that line is reached (but I'd still expect other problems).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Frankenstyle not required for Activity, still recommended?
ResponsesInList.Text: Interesting... Given that, the documentation should reflect that activity modules should not use "mod_" in their database names. I'm going to make those changes. mike

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Frankenstyle not required for Activity, still recommended?
ResponsesInList.Text: For the rest of the tables that your plugin uses internally, you are completely free to name them as you want Is this also true if we plan to get the plugin through the validation process? Because the plugin validation page says the following: The names of all database tables should start with the full ' frankenstyle ' plugin name. For example block_myblock, or auth_paypal. See exceptions for activity modules below. Currently our additional tables are called like: myactivity_anothertable So should we switch to mod_myactivity_anothertable instead?

To clarify, we are specifically studying architectural patterns, rather than design patterns such as the GoF patterns. ResponsesInList.Title: Re-usable activity modules - how can this be done?
ResponsesInList.Text: I am trying to create a new kind of activity module that would enable 'module reuse'. I am interested to hear whether others have had a similar need and how this has been approached. The idea is that a new kind of 'alias' module would allow me to use the content and setup of an existing module. It would then save any grades or other user data with reference to the 'alias' module. The main motivation is to support the DRY principle: If a module is reused in several courses, it is best to maintain one version of it and reuse rather than replicate. In some cases, it also opens up the possibility of better reporting. If 20 feedback modules have the same set-up across different courses, for instance, at present the response analysis has to be done within each module in each course. If it is known that all of the modules feature the same questions, the report could integrate the responses across the whole site. My implementation approach is to have this new activity module linking to the 'target' module. In the target module, all links are changed to include the alias_cmid in the URL parameters. Tables related to user data are changed to the include this alias_cmid and this is inserted when saving user data. Report queries are then adjusted to retrieve records with the alias_cmid if the target module has been accessed through the alias. I have tried implementing this with the SCORM module but found that it was too complex to be workable. There were 40+ links that would have to be changed (to include the new cm_alias ID) and maintained. There were also many different reporting options that would have to be supported. It seemed like it would be too easy to miss something that could lead to bugs and access errors (users being directed to the original SCORM module rather than the alias). I am now making a stab at it for the Feedback module, which seems somewhat more manageable. The biggest issue I can see is that there will be a large maintenance burden for any updates to the module since it has to be changed in so many places to support this. I'm keen to hear whether there's a better approach. Has this been discussed here before?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Re-usable activity modules - how can this be done?
ResponsesInList.Text: Have you looked at the Sharing Cart block? I used it in combination with a "resource course" to keep from having to recreate activities . For instance, I would have a default quiz set up in my resource course and then copy it into the Sharing Cart. In any of my production courses, I could add a Sharing Cart and have access to whatever I had already placed in it. With just a couple of clicks, I could place a copy of the quiz in it's new location. Sharing Cart seems to work with just about any plugin available for Moodle. I did not use the data copy capability but it does seem to be able to copy data from one location to another, too.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Re-usable activity modules - how can this be done?
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks for the suggestion. I've had a play about with it and it looks like a really well put together module. It's a much neater way of using backup/restore functionality in many scenarios. It is not really what I had in mind however since it still depends on *copying* the content of activity modules, whereas I am looking to have one definitive version of the module and have alias modules that *point* to that version. By way of example: I tried using it to share feedback modules between courses and can see that it copies all of the questions used in the feedback. It would be better to be able to use the same questions (i.e. only have one record for each question that is used for all instances of the same feedback). That way, if I have 20 feedbacks in different courses, I can change the question in one place and update all. It also means that I can build reports with the expectation that all feedbacks have exactly the same content and set-up.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Re-usable activity modules - how can this be done?
ResponsesInList.Text: Feedback is probably not a good example of what you want to achieve simply because it can already do what you are describing. If you add a Feedback to the front page (put it in the Main Menu block and then hide the block if you dont want it visible on the front page), you can then map that Feedback to the courses you want it to appear on and add the feedback block itself to those courses so that the activity appears on the course (you can have multiple feedbacks across different courses, or on the same course for different purposes, the block will list any that are mapped to that course). If you know you want feedbacks on every course page, then add it as a 'sticky block'. If you edit the questions on that feedback via the front page, those changes will appear in every mapped course - its just a link to the front page one after all. And when you look at the responses via the front page feedback, you will see that you can report in total, or filtered by courses. I've done this previously with student surveys for teaching programmes and created a feedback tempalte which I then used to create a feedback activity for each department, the department feedback was mapped to all the taught courses and when the students responded the replies could by analysed by taught course or by department (department heads were restricted from seeing the raw results in other departments by using the separate activities), and because all the departments used the same template, exporting and combining the data at a faculty/institution level was then a very simple job too (an sql report from the database or an Excel spreadsheet depending on what you want). If you want to apply that kind of logic to other module activities, actually looking at the feedback module and its back-end code might be a good place to start, because it seems to already do what you are asking about. Richard

ResponsesInList.Title: Wrong character encoding as "combined diacritics" instead of the proper "precomposed characters"
ResponsesInList.Text: Background: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Combining_character https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Precomposed_character Preface: this is a issue in dnduploadlib.php in the course directory and unknown other places. I tried to file an issue in the moodle issue tracker, but as a not that tech savvy person, the obstacles to actually file an issue drove me nuts – so I put the issue here, maybe someone catches it up. *** When uploading a file via dnduploadlib.php, characters with diacritics like german ä, ö, ü in the filename are encoded as so called "composed characters / combining characters": an <ä> is composed out of an <a> combined with an <¨>. In combination with some operatimg systems, browsers and webfonts (OSX, Firefox and Open Sans, for example) these combined characters are faultly interpreted as two separate symbols: <a¨>, which leads to a problem when using things like auto-linking: When I upload a file called "Mäuse.pdf" for example, and autolinking for files is on, then typing the string "Mäuse.pdf" with the keyboard doesn't lead to an autolinked entry because the character "ä" in the filename is encoded as (hex)61CC88, whilst when using the keyboard the character "ä" is encoded as (hex)C3A4. dnduploadlib.php has to be aware of these combined diacritics ((hex)61CC88 for example) and should convert them to the proper precomposed characters ((hex)C3A4 for example). For my special needs, I hacked dnduploadlib.php and replaced the german umlauts. Since I am a frontend developer, that's all I can contribute to this issue, would be great, if a more tech savvy person could find a more radical and generic solution – I've found out, that the same problem occurs on a forum, even when dnduploadlib.php is patched; but I couldn't figure out, what code part is responsible for that.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Insert idnumber into Feedback teacher email
Re: Insert idnumber into Feedback teacher email
ResponsesInList.Text: Please don't encourage the use of get_records_sql in situations like this (especially as it will return an object containing the idnumber, rather than the idnumber) and certainly don't ever hard-code the prefix into the SQL (write {user} not mdl_user) The correct method would be either: $info = $DB->get_record('user', array('id' => $userid), 'idnumber'); $idnumber = $info->idnumber; OR, even better: $idnumber = $DB->get_field('user', 'idnumber', array('id' => $userid));

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Having unoconv issues - won't convert files
ResponsesInList.Text: My steps, for setup from scratch on CentOS 7, with selinux enabled, assuming you have git installed. Unoconv 7 installation: Make sure no existing version currently installed: yum remove libreoffice* Grab a copy of LibreOffice 5.2.2: wget http://download.documentfoundation.org/libreoffice/stable/5.2.2/rpm/x86_64/LibreOffice_5.2.2_Linux_x86-64_rpm.tar.gz Extract: tar -xvf LibreOffice_5.2.2_Linux_x86-64_rpm.tar.gz Install by navigating to the extracted folder / RPMS folder, and run yum localinstall *.rpm Install required Cairo2d library: yum install cairo Get the unoconv script: git clone https://github.com/dagwieers/unoconv.git cp unoconv/unoconv /usr/bin Edit first line of it in /usr/bin/unoconv to be: #!/opt/libreoffice5.2/program/python Configure it to run in listener mode in background via systemctl service: See Installing_unoconv#Run_a_unoconv_listener and follow specific directions bellow vi /etc/systemd/system/unoconv.service And then copy and paste the following configuration into it: [Unit] Description=Unoconv listener for document conversions Documentation= https://github.com/dagwieers/unoconv After=network.target remote-fs.target nss-lookup.target [Service] Type=simple Environment="UNO_PATH=/opt/libreoffice5.2/program" ExecStart=/usr/bin/unoconv --listener [Install] WantedBy=multi-user.target Enable and start the above service: systemctl enable unoconv.service systemctl start unoconv.service It should now be configured for command line use, test via command line: sudo -u apache unoconv -vvv -f pdf /tmp/testdoc.docx The next step is setting home folder of the apache user. Edit /etc/passwd and change in the apache user line the string "/usr/share/httpd" to be "/var/www/moodledata/temp", or some other temporary directory that apache has write access to Then finally SELinux policy tweaks: You will also need to generate and install a policy module. After trying to upload a file, run the following commands: grep python.bin /var/log/audit/audit.log | audit2allow -M unconv-python-policy semodule -i unconv-python-policy.pp Make sure it is properly configured: /admin/search.php?query=unoconv (this will almost always fail unfortunately in my experience) And also on the UI /mod/assign/feedback/editpdf/testunoconv.php Then finally try to upload assignments, and watch the httpd logs for errors (It will almost always seem to generate a PHP Warning:  touch(): Utime failed: Permission denied in ...) even if selinux is set to permissive. Seems to work anyways though.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: custom block doesn't
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear Carlos, From your shared code : public function get_content() { global $CFG; $fichero = file_get_contents($CFG-> dirroot .'/blocks/access_mouse/index.html'); As I understood, you are getting contents and styles of your custom block form this file - $CFG-> dirroot .'/blocks/access_mouse/index.html There might be some css rule that is breaking and causing the break of block's content. My suggestion for you to follow the standard rule of Moodle for creation of block. Put css in a separated file - "styles.css" so that the rule would only be applied on that block's content unless it is to be applied on whole. So, the styles of block access_mouse should be written in file - styles.css (if not, create new one) under directory blocks/access_mouse All styles should be written in this way - .blocks_<block-name> .<style-on-html-file> Example, for block access_mouse, css should be written as - .blocks_access_mouse .buttons{ margin-top: 50px; overflow: hidden; } So, the steps to follow are : On block access_mouse, remove styles from html file and put them on styles.css as mentioned above. Styles of styles.css will automatically be attached with block; so don't worry of attaching of styles.css file on block page. Add file styles.css(if not there) on your custom block too. Follow the same convention of writting css on block. I guess your block name is accesibilidad_raton, then .blocks_ accesibilidad_raton .buttons{ margin-top: 50px; overflow: hidden; } Even you can copy whole styles of " access_mouse ", paste them into your custom block and change the name of block accordingly into the css file Now, You nothing have to change in your custom block. ResponsesInList.Title: What would be a good test that templates do not cause performance problems?
ResponsesInList.Text: This was raised a the last developer meeting: https://docs.moodle.org/dev/Developer_meeting_May_2016 Moodle has a nice new template system (mustache). For what we read, it seem to be pretty fast. However, before we convert all the existing Moodle output to it, we want to be sure that won't cause a huge performance regression. How could we best do that. My suggestion would be to take one or two significant bits of output: e.g. a forum thread, where you have a lot of posts, each of which contains some things like user pictures, buttons and icons. My other suggestion would be outputting a section of the course page, with half a dozen different activities . Then really, just call both the old code, and the new code, in a loop a lot of times to compare the time. The only thing to do is to make sure, as much as possible, that it is a like-for-like comparison. That is, ensure both chunks of code that we are are doing just the work of outputting the HTML, and not doing work of getting data from the database . Does anyone have a better idea? How much work would this be?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What would be a good test that templates do not cause performance problems?
ResponsesInList.Text: Some points about testing this. 1 - We have 2 mustache engines - do we need to compare Mustache.js vs mustache.php ? 2 - There was some limited performance testing of mustache.php on the original issue: https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-49152?focusedCommentId=341909&page=com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.issuetabpanels:comment-tabpanel#comment-341909

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What would be a good test that templates do not cause performance problems?
ResponsesInList.Text: I think Mustache in JS in not really replacing anything else, so less important to profile there. (Also, it only causes problems on the client's computer, not our server , so less of a problem ) So, I think focus on PHP for now. The issue with a lot of the testing done in that bug is that it was done on a developer machine. (Caching off, developer debug, no PHP accelerator.) We only really care about performance a server tuned like a live server such as might be used in production. That is important.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What would be a good test that templates do not cause performance problems?
ResponsesInList.Text: I think Mustache in JS in not really replacing anything else, so less important to profile there. (Also, it only causes problems on the client's computer, not our server, so less of a problem) So, I think you are probably just inventing performance measurement which is probably not going to be the primary concern if everthing moves more client-sidey. In fact we found and fixed a big client-side issue ( MDL-53667 ) with competencies which would give me far more concern than if templates are twice as slow. We Moodle developers need to start taking client side performance a lot more seriously.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What would be a good test that templates do not cause performance problems?
ResponsesInList.Text: Any performance regression that rears its ugly head is serious, and should be taken seriously. MDL-53667 is interesting. I had not seen that before. (I note it came up in Moodle helper code, not the mustache core library.) I am not 'inventing' performance measurement. We do performance measurement at the OU every 3 months, before each of our releases. Sometimes we we are the first to find performance regressions in core, and then we fix them. If templates made page-load times twice as slow, that would be a serious problem, and if that was done throughout core, then it is not something that could be 'fixed' without basically reverting a whole release's worth of changes. Hence my suggestion that we get some measurements before heading too far in one direction. Look, all the signs are the mustache takes performance seriously. However, we are engineers. We should measure and verify.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What would be a good test that templates do not cause performance problems?
ResponsesInList.Text: Any performance regression that rears its ugly head is serious, and should be taken seriously. I agree (and I'm sorry my comment was a bit flippant, bit like your comment about client side performance ). In fact you'll find me banging the drum of us wanting to get us a lot closer to the webkit approach than we already are. While we do have some modest progress towards that, the important thing we need to get better is decent metrics. My point was that I am not sure I entirely agree with you that this metric you are so focused on in isolation is as important as the emphasis you put on it. I expect that mustache templates will be slower, but I feel like we're talking about the microptimisation level and orders of magnitude mean that saving a database query will be far more important for most pages than template cpu degradation. We do performance measurement at the OU every 3 months, before each of our releases. Sometimes we we are the first to find performance regressions in core, and then we fix them. And I/we thank you for that, but how can we as a community get this sort of measurement with decent real world-ish data (from you and other large sites) tested earlier, so you stop having to detect those performance regressions? That is a far more important thing to work on in my view. Finally (and importantly), what are you going to do if you find the 'wrong' answer here - without actual evidence of real world problems I foresee a future of bugs open reporting the problems without a solution. I agree with doing this sort of measurement before something lands and its a shame we didn't get anything more extensive while it was in development - but you know how the world works, people want you to ship, compromises are made, we are all human and some things slip.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: recieving id from nuggets
ResponsesInList.Text: If the URL is [site]/course/view.php?id=XX, then the XX refers to a record in the mdl_course database table. If the URL is [site]/mod/[activitytype]/view.php?id=XX, then the XX refers to a record in the mdl_course_modules table. In that case, the 'module' field in that record will point to an entry in the table mdl_modules (which will have the name '[activitytype]', matching the URL) and the 'instance' field will refer to a record in the table 'mdl_[activitytype]' (again, matching the URL). See https://docs.moodle.org/dev/Course_module for more details.

ResponsesInList.Title: PHPUnit tests fail on DEBUG_DEVELOPER debugging() calls
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm currently working on an internal plugin for moodle, and have discovered that running the PHPunit tests results in errors due to the use of debugging() calls. I've tracked down https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-44339 which infers that any debugging() statement is an error, and as such the Unit tests fail. It appears that the reset_debugging() function in /lib/phpunit/classes/util.php resets the debugging level to DEBUG_DEVELOPER. I'm just wondering if this is a little too aggressive? Currently in the plugin that I'm developing I'm using the DEBUG_DEVELOPER flag to output useful messages that provide information on the process that is being performed, to allow me to see if there is any issue happening or the data is being unexpectedly modified. All of this may be useful information in the future for tracking down any future issues, so hence the DEBUG_DEVELOPER. In normal operation this is of no interest. So this leaves me with a resulting action to do at the end of the development process to remove all of the debugging() calls, which then should I need to find out if the internals are playing funny buggers I would then have to re-add. This is then complicated by the fact that our release processes prohibit me modifying the code running on the live system, hence why the debugging level can be turned up and down as required to investigate any issues. On this basis I'd challenge the notion that debugging is unexpected, and that a debugging message (certainly at DEBUG_DEVELOPER) can be always asserted as being an "error". (I do know that I can use the assertDebuggingCalled(null, DEBUG_DEVELOPER) to check that i *did* output developer level messages but then this also seem to discard *all* debugging messages.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: PHPUnit tests fail on DEBUG_DEVELOPER debugging() calls
ResponsesInList.Text: Why not call getDebuggingMessages in your test, and confirm they contain appropriate content.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: PHPUnit tests fail on DEBUG_DEVELOPER debugging() calls
ResponsesInList.Text: The convention is that debugging output is used to tell the developer that something is not right. The fact that any debug output auto-fails the test is generally a very good thing. So, you have to change your thinking and stop thinking of the like a sort of logDebug or whatever that you might see in other systems. If you want to keep doing what you are doing, then you will need to make your own helper function, to output something if  $CFG->developerdebug is true. However, you don't really want to be running developer debug level on your live servers. The first step with any bug report is to reproduce it on a test server where you can change code.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Use $DB to query neighbor database on same server/connection
ResponsesInList.Text:
Don't mess with the $DB global (you will break things), but you can create an instance of the moodle_database class (or an appropriate subclass like mysqli_native_moodle_database) and use that to query other databases. Perhaps something like this: 
```text
$extdb = new mysql_native_moodle_database(true); // true says that it's an external database, so don't use Moodle's prefix


$extdb->connect($CFG->dbhost, $CFG->dbuser, $CFG->dbpass, 'neighbor', '');
```

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Integration of Moodle using MS Biztalk
ResponsesInList.Text: Add your vote to MDL-28988 . What data do you need to send TO / FROM Moodle? I ended up creating a MSSQL Stored Procedure that exposes the Moodle data that I want BizTalk to consume as xml (a "manual WSDL" if you like). Now each time BizTalk needs the Moodle data the BizTalk client runs that MS SQL stored procedure and it gets the data it wants as xml. This solution gets used hundreds of times a day for over 3 years now... It is a one-direction read-only service though - BizTalk READING Moodle data. I wouldn't ever allow BizTalk to do INSERT/UPDATE operations in the Moodle database . Any INSERT/UPDATE operations need to be done via the Moodle API's in Moodle plugins ... Example: If you wanted to create New Users in Moodle it's not as simple as doing an INSERT in the mdl_user table. Don't do that! There are a LOT of other things that happen in the Moodle database when new users are created (contexts, permissions, roles, etc.)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Integration of Moodle using MS Biztalk
ResponsesInList.Text: You certainly can interoperate with Moodle using SOAP (the protocol that WSDL is part of.) At the OU, we call Moodle webservices from Java and .Net code.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Odd question about $PAGE->set_context()
ResponsesInList.Text: Some things won't work properly if $PAGE->context is not right, so that is why there is a warning if you fail to set it. The point is not really to force you to call require_login. You should know to do that anyway. If that is a side-effect of the warning, then good. It helps developers get their code right. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: how to know whether a user is logged in or not
ResponsesInList.Text: No. It isn't possible to determine whether a user is logged in, because HTTP protocol does not maintain connections; you might still be looking at the website or maybe you've gone somewhere else, who knows. You could implement this by doing a query on the mdl_log table, with the current course id, to get a list of all userids who have made a request in the past 5 minutes (say). Then when drawing your names, check if they are in the list. On busy courses or if the database isn't well-optimised this might be slow because the log table is ginormous, so take care if you have performance concerns. For example I just ran a suitable query now for one reasonably popular course; there were 3 different users in the past 5 minutes, but the first time I asked for this it took a whopping ~450ms to work that out, and even repeated runs took ~150ms. This might be a concern under heavy usage, when you would want to look into caching the information on disk for a minute or something rather than generating it on every user's visit. I don't know if Moodle provides any infrastructure/API to help you with this; not aware of any but I haven't looked. --sam

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: how to know whether a user is logged in or not
ResponsesInList.Text: Exactly as Sam says. Except that in 1.9 and newer you have a table that is probably a better choice than mdl_log: mdl_user_lastaccess. It using user_lastaccess will have much less performance impact.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to translate the custom menu items between languages
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hello Emadof. While the custom menu doesn't support setting multiple languages for an item it does support creating nodes for a sepecific language (thanks to David Mudrak for implementing this in MDL-28168 ). Each custom menu item can contain 4 elements: Text for the item (required) A URL A title to use for the item (if not specified the text is used) The language the item is to be used for (defaults to all) So knowing this the following can be done: 
```text
English only|
http://moodle.com
|English only item|en
German only|
http://moodle.de
|Deutsch|de,de_du,de_kids
```
 In this situation if your current language is english you will see the English only item, if its German you will see the German only node, and finally if its French you won't see either. This system will allow you to create separate menus for different languages. The downside is that you must translate everything you want the user to see. There's no relation between items so you can't say show the English the item if there is no German translation. Make sense? Hope that helps. Cheers Sam

ResponsesInList.Title: Trying to migrate forum posts containing files (images and attachments) by updating the database directly
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello. In the Moodle instance I'm working on, I need to migrate forum posts from one discussion (that has far too many posts now) to several other discussions. While the real solution would have been to organize the discussions efficiently from the beginning, the fact is I'm now stuck with this situation... and as there are a lot of those posts, using any one-at-a-time migration interface command would be a real pain. So I tried to achieve this by modifying the database : bulk-creating new discussions, reaffecting the posts to them - that part works well. The difficulty I'm facing now is how to migrate embedded images and post attachments (images too). While the migrated posts ids have not changed, and the files are directly associated to the posts ("itemid" field in the "files" table), the images don't show... Editing the migrated post shows that the embedded image is referenced in the post (as expected), but appears as a blank square in Atto. What I tried next is modifying the "contextid" field of the "files" table, as it looks responsible for the visibility (or not) of a file in a given context . OK but... how can I compute the contextid of a given forum discussion, without using Moodle PHP code ? Is there a documented mathematical formula to do this ? I tried to create a post in the destination discussion, add a file to it, and examine which contextid it obtained. By copying this contextid into the files records I try to migrate, here's what happens : the images still don't show in the post, but if I edit the post, the images and attachments show in Atto in the edit form ! By saving the post, the images are displayed correctly OK but if I need to edit and save every migrated post, it's not a bulk update anymore... Plus, I noticed that after this operation, the files records in the database had their "pathnamehash" changed.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Trying to migrate forum posts containing files (images and attachments) by updating the database directly
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi again, Partly answering my own question here : the trick is to recompute the "pathnamehash" after updating the "contextid". It is indeed stated in the files table documentation . 
```text
SHA1(CONCAT('/', contextid, '/', component, '/', filearea, '/', itemid, '/', filename))
```
 In my case, all "filepath" values are "/"; unlike the documentation says, the filepath must not be concatenated here or it will result in 3 "/" in a row; be sure to have only one "/" at a time between itemid and filename. One question remains : apart from creating a new file in the desired context to look at its contextid, is there a real good way to compute : guess the contextid for a given activity (in my case a forum) ? Thanks, Mathias

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Trying to migrate forum posts containing files (images and attachments) by updating the database directly
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi, Just in case it helps someone in the future : here's how I achieved the forum posts migration. As Moodle doesn't offer any pagination for posts in a discussion, but does for discussions in a forum, the goal was to convert 1 discussion containing N posts to N discussions containing 1 post. Then displaying the forum "as a blog " does the trick : the posts (in fact the single-post-discussions) are paginated. 1) Create destination forum, write down its id (forum id, not activity id) 2) Create a test discussion in this new forum, add at least 1 file to it. 3) Find this file in the "files" table : 
```text
SELECT * FROM files WHERE component = 'mod_forum' AND filearea IN ('post', 'attachment') AND itemid IN (SELECT fp.id FROM forum_posts fp LEFT JOIN forum_discussions fd ON fp.discussion = fd.id WHERE fd.forum = NEW_FORUM_ID_HERE);
```
 > you get a "contextid" for the file you just sent; write it down. 3b) Delete the discussion you just created. 4) Convert all posts from the source discussion you want to migrate, to new discussions in the new forum 
```text
INSERT INTO forum_discussions SELECT NULL, COURSE_ID_HERE, NEW_FORUM_ID_HERE, subject, id, userid, -1, 0, modified, userid, 0, 0 FROM forum_posts WHERE discussion = ORIGINAL_DISCUSSION_ID_HERE;
```
 5) Define all those posts as the unique post of each corresponding new discussion (update "parent" and "discussion") 
```text
UPDATE forum_posts fp LEFT JOIN forum_discussions fd ON fd.firstpost = fp.id SET parent = 0, discussion = fd.id WHERE fd.forum = NEW_FORUM_ID_HERE;
```
 6) Find all files associated with original posts, and update their "contextid" et "pathnamehash" 
```text
UPDATE files SET contextid = CONTEXTID_YOU_WROTE_DOWN_HERE, pathnamehash = SHA1(CONCAT('/', CONTEXTID_YOU_WROTE_DOWN_HERE, '/', component, '/', filearea, '/', itemid, '/', filename)) WHERE component = 'mod_forum' AND filearea IN ('post', 'attachment') AND itemid IN (SELECT fp.id FROM forum_posts fp LEFT JOIN forum_discussions fd ON fp.discussion = fd.id WHERE fd.forum = NEW_FORUM_ID_HERE);
```
 7) Delete all subscriptions to original discussion 
```text
DELETE FROM forum_discussion_subs WHERE discussion = ORIGINAL_DISCUSSION_ID_HERE;
```
 8) Done ! Unfortunately I couldn't find how to compute the contextid for a given forum, hence the "fake post" trick. Greetings, Mathias

The problem is to "enforce" moodle (somehow) to meet the condition if (!empty($this->config->{'field_map_'.$match[1]}) and $this->config->{$match[0]} === 'onlogin') In my case $key is field_updatelocal_profile_field_nazwagrupy, $match[1] is profile_field_nazwagrupy , $this->config->{$match[0]} is onlogin (all the other fields have value oncreate ). I know this is very detailed question but maybe somehow, someone knows the answer. Regards, Damian

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Custom user field to be updateable during ldap sync
ResponsesInList.Text: The reason is that $auth->sync_users() updates user records by calling $auth->update_user_record(), which in turn calls user_update_user() in user/lib.php. Unfortunately, user_update_user only updates the user record in the mdl_user table - by doing $DB->update_record(). It doesn't load or update the custom profile fields. A way to "enforce" the updating of custom profile fields would be to use update_user_record() in lib/moodlelib.php instead. That function uses update_user_record_by_id(), which in turn loads the custom user profile fields and updates the values via profile_save_data(). So, you have two options (however note the comments marked with '***'): File a bug in the Moodle tracker asking for your issue to be fixed Change your plugin's sync_user() function so it uses update_user_record() in lib/moodlelib.php instead of $auth->update_user_record() *** *** You should avoid changing core Moodle code. For your purposes, you should create a new LDAP plugin that extends the core LDAP plugin, and overload the sync_users() to achieve your desired effect. Good luck!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Odp: Re: Custom user field to be updateable during ldap sync
ResponsesInList.Text: 1/ Yes, the new plugin should extend auth_plugin_ldap, not auth_plugin_base. In addition to overriding sync_users() you'll also need provide the proper constructor (that's where you set the value of $auth->authtype, etc.). And, if your new plugin has settings different from the standard LDAP plugin, you may have to provide a suitable config.html and override the process_config() function in your plugin class. You'll also need a need language file, for your plugin's name and description (and any other special requirements). Take a look at the LDAP Server (Sync Plus) plugin - it's a nice example of customising standard Moodle behaviour without the need to patch it. 2/ Not beside, instead of. Instead of calling $this->update_user_record(), the overridden sync_users() should call update_user_record() in lib/moodlelib.php 3/ Yes, probably best to create your own LDAP plugin and clone it. Actually, extending it might work, but I'm not sure. You can always give it a shot - what do you have to lose, eh 4/ The Sync Plus plugin that I referred to earlier uses a scheduled task to sync users and it may be just what you need.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM packages in Moodle and case-insensitivity file system
ResponsesInList.Text: are you sure it's Moodle that is causing the issues? - Most web servers are also case-sensitive. If the case sensitivity issues are not related to your imsmanifest. xml file then it's more likely that the web server is causing the problems - not Moodle.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM packages in Moodle and case-insensitivity file system
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Rami, the Moodle files pool is case-sensitive regardless the underlying OS: this feature cannot be changed. More details here: https://docs.moodle.org/dev/File_API_internals . It's a bad habit to refer to raw assets (images, media, ...) without taking care of their actual file path and name case, as described in the compressed archive: the SCORM spec is pretty clear and tells that the package must be self-contained and run-able everywhere i.e. you must take care of the case-insensitive file system issue regardless how Moodle stores the files internally. HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM packages in Moodle and case-insensitivity file system
ResponsesInList.Text: As Matteo mentions, even though it's a pain right now, you should really fix the issue in your packages. There's probably a nice find/replace script out there somewhere to help rename files that you might be able to use. Another option could be to use a method of SCORM packaging that does not result in all the SCORM package files sitting in the Moodle file-pool - see the information on using unzipped SCORM in a file system repository in my blog post here: https://danmarsden.com/blog/2013/09/24/managing-scorm-content-in-moodle-2-6/

ResponsesInList.Title: __DIR__ pointing to ftp directory not URL
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, I've installed a copy of Moodle on a site I have to test plugins I'm writing. The __DIR__ constant is supposed to point to the root folder for Moodle (e.g. www.mysite.com/moodle/blocks/ ...) but mine seems to point to the FTP root instead (e.g. home/moodle/blocks/...). Have I installed something wrong, or am I misunderstanding the __DIR__ variable? I can't really use it to point to support files using the FTP path.. Thanks, Miles

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: __DIR__ pointing to ftp directory not URL
ResponsesInList.Text: __DIR__ points to the directory containing the current script file on the server . So, if the file is at /var/moodlesite/local/myplugin/index.php, then __DIR__ will be "/var/moodlesite/local/myplugin". In a Moodle plugin, once you've used __DIR__ (or dirname(__FILE__)) at the top of the file to include the main config.php file (see any existing Moodle plugin for examples), you should not use it again. Assuming config.php has been included, $CFG-> wwwroot will point at the website address of your site and $CFG-> dirroot will point at the root of the directory on the server. So, $CFG->wwwroot.'/blocks/myblock/index.php' will output ' www.mysite.com/moodle/blocks/myblock/index.php' (but, you really should look at using the moodle_url class for doing that stuff anyway).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SQL query to make self-enrolment first option
ResponsesInList.Text:
I'm not sure about doing this with SQL alone but it should be fairly easy to write a CLI script to add it. You can get a list of all the courses that don't have the enrolment plugin by something like this: 
```text
SELECT c.id FROM mdl_course c LEFT JOIN mdl_enrol e ON c.id = e.courseid AND e.enrol = 'self' WHERE e.id IS NULL AND c.id <> :siteid
```
 Then loop through the courses and use $plugin->add_default_instance($courseid) to add it (where $plugin = enrol_get_plugin('self'));

ResponsesInList.Title: Could we make an activity appear more than once in a course?
ResponsesInList.Text: This is something that has been buzzing around in my head. I think from a user's point of view it makes perfect sense, but from a technical point of view it might be impossible to implement without adding insane levels of complexity to Moodle core. Anyway, I want to describe the idea, and discuss it with anyone interested (perhaps at the Hackfest in London?) What teachers might want The idea is that you might sometimes want links to one activity from several different weeks (or sections in another course format). Here are some examples: A workshop activity, where students need to make their submission one week, and then assess other students' submissions the next week. An assignment or quiz where the work is submitted one week, and they want to encourage students to go back to go back and look at the feedback they received a week or two later once the grading is done. A forum, wiki or blog , where students are supposed to write something near the start of the course, then much later on, the teachers wants them to go back and look at what they originally wrote and reflect on it, and may-be write some more as a follow-up. A course using the question practice activity where every few weeks, the teacher wants the student to go back and do a bit more practice. ... and there are lots more ... How you can already do this Simple option: use an ordinary link Something you can already do is to just add a URL resource in the later section, pointing at the original activity. You can give that an appropriate title and description to tell the student what to do. Moodle even supports this to the extent that if you backup and restore the course, the link is updated to work in the restored course. If you are happy to use manual activity completion, students can have a separate completion check-box by the second activity. Moodle does not really support this, because several things don't work fully. Easy set-up: you have to manually copy and paste the URL of the original activity. Access restrictions: If you hide the original activity (or add a conditional availability rule) but not the link, then students have a link which, when they click it, gives an error. Extra info on the course page: E.g. if you link to a forum, you won't get the notification that tells you if the forum contains unread posts. Deletion risk: If you delete the original activity, there is no warning that something else links here that you are about to break. Completion: You can't have different automatic completion rules for the original activity, and the link to it. (Think about the Workshop example above.) Navigation: Once you have followed the link, the navigation shows you being in the place where the original activity is. Option 2: use a custom plugin This is something we have done at the OU. We have something called mod_repeatactivity, it really just automates manually creating the link, but because it is a plugin we can solve some of the issue above. When you add a repeat activity, it gives you a nice selector to pick the activity you want to repeat. By default the repeat copies the name and description of the original activity, though you can customise them if you like. It automatically copies the visibility setting and activity completion rules form the original activity. And if the settings on the original are changed later, the changes are automatically mirrored to the repeat using an event handler. It also displays the right automated notifications like for unread forum posts on a repeat of a forum. When you turn editing on, activities that have been repeated elsewhere get the word "repeated" displayed next to them as a warning. However, this requires a renderer hack in our theme. If the original activity is deleted. Any repeats are deleted using an event handler. This is where it starts go wrong. The repeat activity can only have a manual completion checkbox. And we don't have a solution to the navigation issue at all, though we are being asked to develop one in our new theme, which is going to be a really horrible renderer hack. Because of the need for renderer hacks, we have not shared this plugin with the community. Could we do better So, really, my question is: if we did this in Moodle core, rather than in a hacky plugin, could we do better? In particular, would there be a nice way to solve the navigation issue, and to allow the two links to the same activity to have different automatic completion rules? What does anybody think?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Could we make an activity appear more than once in a course?
ResponsesInList.Text: There's also a related (but more complex) situation that at least one customer of ours has wanted - having a group of activities that are shared between multiple courses - e.g. a survey/questionnaire that users of multiple courses all need to fill in or a forum shared between multiple courses (whether a news forum or a discussion forum). We've solved this using a block which lists the content of the other course that holds these shared activities and a redirect script on the links that silently enrols users onto this course. There are also some core & renderer hacks to hide this course from 'My courses' and to rewrite the breadcrumb trail to make it look like the user is still in their original course. Having the ability to completely decouple activities from the course that contains them, is probably getting a bit too far outside the scope of what you were proposing (although, moving outside of Moodle, the VLE software Ilias does support something like that).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Could we make an activity appear more than once in a course?
ResponsesInList.Text: The OU's Forum NG has the ability to have a shared forum that is used in multiple courses, but that is also a bit of a hack. I am not suggesting that we completely decouple activities from courses. For example, when you think about working out roles and permissions, the actual activity must be in one place in the tree of contexts, and that is what controls access permissions, or it just becomes too difficult (I think). I think I am just proposing a sort of smart pointer referring to an activity elsewhere. However, no reason that other activity cannot be in a different course. Then, the link to it can check the permissions before making the link visible to a particular student.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Could we make an activity appear more than once in a course?
ResponsesInList.Text: Respect your cautious approach Tim, However, some thoughts to stimulate the buzz in your head from someone similarly buzzed: An activity in Moodle is many things thrown together: Content to be delivered usually created by teacher or a similar role; Settings that control the availability or interaction with the content like hiding it, availability dates etc; Participation by the end users including the completion state and grade besides the content generated by them; If we could decouple these three, we should be able to gain a lot more flexibility. For example, the content could belong in a repository with its own access control and publishing / approval workflow. The published items in this repository should be available for a teacher to include in her course by either linking to it or making a copy of it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Could we make an activity appear more than once in a course?
ResponsesInList.Text: If some developer guru could come up with a solution I for one would be extremely happy. Coincidentally, a couple of days ago we had to look for a solution to a use case and it looks like we'll be going with your "simple option" above with an addition of using the correct icon via a Generico template and actually using links to orphaned activities. Our use case that has led us to trying to find the best solution: A linear 17 block course (a block being 8 days) where each new block is revealed on the 8 day cycle Two courses run at the same time but a block or two apart For analytical and data retention reasons we want all cohorts that go through to use the same assignments, quizzes etc. Due to lack of equipment for some of the practical components, the "blocks" have to be juggled a little half way through for even numbered courses so the blocks are out of order (i.e. instead of blocks 1-17 they do blocks 1-6, 10, 11, 7-9 then 12-17) Due to having to juggle blocks for even numbered courses we keep hitting issues with activities ending up having to be moved around as they are not always in blocks the even numbered courses actually have access to. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Could we make an activity appear more than once in a course?
ResponsesInList.Text: I can think of two approaches the won't "beak" Moodle. One solution, as mentioned before, is a block. A block not that different from the activities block, where the major difference will be that the activities are manages manually. Additional permissions checks can be added to make sure only selected users will view selected activities in the block. Another solution is creating a new type of activity that I call a 'reference activity'. This activity has little to no content of its own, but will act as a, let's call it a smart link, to another activity in the course. This way, you can set several reference activities in the course and each activity can have its own completion status. Furthermore, a new capability can be created that will block users from accessing an activity directly and they can do it only from the reference activity.

ResponsesInList.Title: Share same live instance of activities across Courses
ResponsesInList.Text: Hey Moodlers, We would like to share an activity / resource e.g. a forum, database , quiz across courses easily. This currently seems impossible without copying the activities to the other courses. However, copying the activity to the other course is not sufficient as the interaction of the users i.e. forum posts, database entries, quiz grades also need to be shared. Does anybody else also feel that this is worthwhile. Please read on if you do. I have a requirement where groups are being used to segregate the users participating in an activity with the condition that the groups can be from across courses. Also, the groups that do not want others to see them also cannot see others. However, the ones that want to see others can also see the other groups. Have had multiple people approach us with similar requirement whose core is - it should be possible to build a repository of activities and assign them in various courses. Thereafter, all the users / user groups should be able to see other users / groups attempting this activity. I think this would only be possible if we decouple activities from courses as well as from the user content being generated  with them. We may have to additionally also decouple some of the fields in the create / edit activity interface to provide more flexibility with regard to their accessibility etc. in different courses. While a teacher should be able to use an activity in the activity repository, she should also be able to publish the activities she creates to the activity repository which might be promoted to the common activity repository after an approval workflow. Does this make sense? Besides your experience and view on if you have come across such a requirement and how desirable this would be, we would love to know how complex would this be to implement and how deep the architectural changes will need to be.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Individualized Course administration
ResponsesInList.Text: The other alternative, which I have done in the past is, rather than creating a new block, override the renderer for the custom menu in the theme and add a menu drop down that is hard coded to those functions but wrap it inside a conditional such as if (isadmin()){ your drop down code here} There are a number of themes that have renderer overrides for the custommenu that you could check out to see how to achieve this. A menu item would also get around the need to add a block to whatever page and the possibility of altering the layout/page look and feel for something which is only related to a few admin functions. The other issue (probably actually the first and most important step) is sorting out the role you want to give these users as something more than 'teacher' but less than 'manager' or 'admin' so you will need to create a role with the relevant permissions and capabilities you want them to have. In which case you may need to change my suggestion above and not use isadmin() but the better and more specifically targetted has_capability function. Once you know the capabilities you want them to have (from your survey you mention perhaps) and assuming these capabilities exist at the granular level you want them, then the rest of the project is actually not that difficult. I realise you said that survey comes at a later stage - I would suggest its the most important part to determine and should come first, because its from there that you can determine if these are already functions that a teacher would have and you just need to provide links to the relevant pages, or whether they are separate capabilities that can be built into a new 'extended teacher' role, or whether they are a necessary part of the manager/admin role that cannot easily be split out (e.g. if a theme provides an 'alert' setting, that cannot be separated out from the ability to manage the site settings as a whole as there is not a capability permission that is at the level of granularity). So you really need to determine what the requirements are before knowing how best to progress, because there may be alternative solutions depending on those requirements. Richard

ResponsesInList.Title: Re-apply capabilities from db/access.php
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I've already got my block installed and the default capabilities were set on install against the role archetypes from what I had in the db/access.php However, now I've made changes to that access.php file, as I decided some capabilities should be PREVENTED for certain roles. Is there anyway to re-apply what's in that file, instead of going through manually and changing all the capabilities for each role in the Users -> permissions section? Cheers.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Re-apply capabilities from db/access.php
ResponsesInList.Text: No, because Moodle has no way of knowing which differences (between the defaults in the file and the configuration in the database ) are due to local configuration changes and which are due to changes in the defaults. You could, in theory, write an upgrade step that directly alters the role capabilities in the DB (or via an API call), but that could be bad if the site admin has already customised the role capabilities to their liking.

ResponsesInList.Title: How to implement non-permanent application cache
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi, I'm developing plugin for Moodle 2.6 and I have an application variable that checks if an instance of RabbitMQ consumer is started or not, so it doesn't start another one. Right now, I have something like this: 
```text
$cache 
= cache::
make_from_params
(cache_store::
MODE_APPLICATION
, 
'local_morph'
, 
'rabbitmqconsumer'
);


$cache
->set(
'enabled'
,
'true'
);


$enabled
=
$cache
->get(
'enabled'
);
```
 It works, but the problem is that this variable is permanent, and in case of apache restart I need to clean the cache in order to return variable to default state. Is it possible to make this variable non-permanent, without installing memcache data store? Thanks, Zoran

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to implement non-permanent application cache
ResponsesInList.Text: No. And I do not see how would memcached help you here since it runs in separate process unrelated to web server . The appropriate way to deal with this issue would be to detect when did web server start (on LAMP that can be determined by examining pid file timestamp) and encode that information into cache value (key name etc.). Upon every execution you compare the key timestamp with server timestamp. When they differ it is time for reset. Of course this is not the most fortunate way of doing this. Ideally it might be possible to use apache SetEnv to define env variable pointing to pid file so as to avoid hardcoding.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to implement non-permanent application cache

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to implement non-permanent application cache
ResponsesInList.Text: Of course it is possible but I have no idea how to do it. Process management is completely different in Windows. Perhaps a more portable solution would be to use APC and it's cache store. http://php.net/manual/en/ref.apc.php Of course that would not work if PHP is installed as php-fpm.

ResponsesInList.Title: file_get_contents fails randomly
ResponsesInList.Text: ﻿ Not exactly a Moodle question but perhaps someone can help. This is on a Linux system: How can I find out why a call to file_get_contents is failing (in a Moodle enrollment plugin I wrote)? I have a list of courses, and for each one I use file_get_contents to ask an external system for some information. The call fails randomly, even when I loop through the same exact list; sometimes it fails on the 100th entry, sometimes on the 13th, sometimes on the 76th, and so on. I verified that the external system never receives the GET request when this fails, but I don't know where to look to tell what the problem is, connectivity or a resource or what. What I suspect is that the Linux server is occasionally running out of "something" and failing to send the request, but I have no idea what or where to look. I do know it's not the PHP limits on "execution time" or "input time" since we set them crazy high just to test this. Has anyone had experience with this sort of problem? Thanks for any constructive reactions. (I know it is slightly off-topic.)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: file_get_contents fails randomly
ResponsesInList.Text: If it's external then it involves networking ... networking comes before application. Is the 'talking' between Moodle server and this external thing on a certain port or IP address? One could install a thing called iptraf ... ncurses tool ... realtime monitoring ... on the Moodle server.   When launched one could set to watch any traffic on a NIC or a protcol ... and I think a specific IP.   It could be set to save a log on each launch and will stop logging when one exits. See: http://www.tecmint.com/real-time-interactive-ip-lan-monitoring-with-iptraf-tool/ for page that describes. One could open two terminal windows for the Moodle server.   1 has iptaf running and set to watch the traffic however configured.  The 2nd terminal window running something like multitail ... which will show the logs of other services - like messages log, secure log, etc. Something like what you've described would be difficult to pin down ... ramdomness.   Not sure if I know of any single monitoring tool that would help easily pin point the issue. Is the Moodle system in/on a virtualized environment ... like VMWare or other?   If it is, you won't see anything on or in Moodle that indicates the issue.   Had a Moodle on a VMWare box once and another Guest OS had been configured to use all the resources of the virtual server itself for certain timed jobs of some sort.   Moodle wouldn't respond to any client request and appeared to users as being down ... but it wasn't.  It was hard to convince the Virtual Server admin that it wasn't an issue with the guest OS upon which Moodle was hosted ... nor Moodle code, Good luck! 'spirit  of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What plugin type modifies every page?
ResponsesInList.Text: As far as I know, the only "right" way to do the kind of thing you're talking about is using a Theme, overriding one of the core renders that's used on every page like footer().  It's possible to do with other plugin types, but hacky.  In this case, a local plugin is as good a choice as any.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What plugin type modifies every page?
ResponsesInList.Text: Basically, you're right.  It is possible for themes to inherit from each other, so it could be possible for someone to build a theme based on yours, but if they want to use a different 3rd-party theme it's trickier.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What plugin type modifies every page?
ResponsesInList.Text: It will help to hear more about the intended features. I saw some local plugins trying to inject HTML/JS into every page by having such code in the global scope of lib.php and hacks like that. It often has side effects - e.g. CLI scripts and AJAX response break etc. In one particular case, it turned out that what those guys actually needed, was a block. Blocks can exist on almost all pages in Moodle even if they are not actually displayed as blocks. They have opportunity to inject into the page nicely and cleanly. They can be aware of the page context and customise things according to that. Typical use case is a contact form, 24/7 live support chat window and things like that.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What plugin type modifies every page?
ResponsesInList.Text: Blocks can exist on almost all pages in Moodle even if they are not actually displayed as blocks. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What plugin type modifies every page?
ResponsesInList.Text: I meant that the block's `get_content()` method can return empty content so the block is not displayed at all. Even if it exists on the page. And it still has a chance to inject and execute the javascript via `$this->page->requires` which in turn can modify HTML etc. Such a block can be configured to appear across the whole site. As a result, you can embed your JS into almost every page in Moodle.

I've found is really increases the productivity of myself and the other Learning Technologists in my team. One of the goals of my little UI was to not touch the page layout at all (hence a floating UI) so that when testing the site during upgrades or theme changes, we know it's not going to skew the effect as seen by someone not using the extension. Unlike a block, it is also fixed to the corner of the screen so no scrolling to access it! I have a lot of experience with PHP, JS etc but am only 6 months into my job here working with Moodle so I appreciate the help understanding how to correctly integrate to it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What plugin type modifies every page?
ResponsesInList.Text: Blocks and other plugins can have their own style. css file and if you prefix all of the styles with one id or class that wraps your entire content, then it would only be overridden by a theme if the theme designer specifically targets it. The problem comes if you are trying to get your block/plugin to override theme css after the theme has been added, simply because that's not how the css inheritance works (core -> plugins -> themes). It sounds like you might need a local plugin - and you may want to look at adminer. That has a kind of floating UI for database management and has its own self contained css, so may be a useful starting point. Richard

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What plugin type modifies every page?
ResponsesInList.Text: See my other post where I describe how to use the block `get_content()` and simply use the block as a widget to execute your JS.

ResponsesInList.Text: Blocks need to be put on the page, or someone to add them as a 'sticky' block across the site. Adding the functionality to a local plugin should remove that requirement as it would always be available in the same way as something like adminer. That said, it may be that you want this to float over the current page (adminer does open its own in the background) in which case maybe a block is better. To be perfectly honest, where you have written blocks before, I have written quite a few themes, so I would have been tempted to build this functionality into a theme - but again, if your institution needs to use multiple themes, that may not be appropriate either As far as I can tell, the need to add the block to the page(s) is the only way it would affect behaviour/usability that I can think of and that could be an advantage in terms of controlling where it appears (or doesn't). ResponsesInList.Title: Moodle core development workflow by merging fixes with git
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm curious about the process of how bug fixes are applied to Moodle core. The core development instructions at https://docs.moodle.org/dev/Process#Develop_your_change_using_git say: You will need to push one commit for each branch the fix needs to be applied to. Why are the changes not merged directly from lower branch (e.g. MOODLE_30_STABLE) to higher branch (e.g. MOODLE_31_STABLE) using " git merge lower_branch"? Why go through the trouble of doing the same changes manually to multiple different branches? I've been using the merging workflow for a long time and even with very large and complex frameworks. Many people who try it are surprised how well git actually handles stuff like this (but after all that's what git was designed for in the first place). Has Moodle HQ ever considered moving to this workflow? Has it been tried? Are there any current plans/discussion related to it? I just think it would save a lot of time and trouble and would make it easier to work with Moodle core.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle core development workflow by merging fixes with git
ResponsesInList.Text: As I understand the logic, the idea is that the integrator shouldn't have to worry about merge conflicts etc. when applying a fix to a given branch.  By having the developer prepare a commit for each branch, they will (should have) already have done the work to take into account any divergence between the branches for the code they are changing. In practice, I generally create the fix once for the branch I'm running, then cherry-pick it on the other branches I'm submitting a fix for, and do any necessary tweaks for each branch as I do.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle core development workflow by merging fixes with git
ResponsesInList.Text: Cherry-pick is indeed one way to move fixes from branch to another. The drawback with it however is that it always creates a completely new commit (the commit hash does not match the original one). This causes the history of the two branches to become incompatible, which makes it impossible to use some tools that git provide. However when using `git merge`, the commits are identical copies across branches.

ResponsesInList.Title: MUC identifiers, proposed change to implementation
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, During my implementation of MDL-53213 it realised that MUC identifiers can change the cache pointer of an existing cache eg; $properties = array('dbfamily' => 'pg sql '); $cache = cache::make('core', 'databasemeta', $properties); Then; $properties = array('dbfamily' => ' mysql '); $cache2 = cache::make('core', 'databasemeta', $properties); This will result in $cache = $cache2, which is not what I would have expected as a developer.  It feels dangerous and counter intuitive. Proposal: Identifiers and Sharing options be added to the definition_hash. Identifiers would not be able to be changed once a cache::make has been called.  You will need to complete a second cache::make if you need a different cache option set. Remove multikeyprefix.  This would be handled by the store as the singlekeyprefix along with the definition hash if that was interesting to the store.  Some may need it for keys, others may not as definition hashes will have separated it. This will then uniquely identify a cache by those things and the code above would result in two separate instances.  It also has a benefit of allowing developers to purge a cache based on that new definition.  So in the databasemeta case, I would just purge the pgsql cache, and not all of them.  Developers can then use this function to make identifiers like smaller sub-caches for certain use cases.  I've had a couple where I want the identifier to be a userid or forumid and manage it as a separate cache. Generate singlekeyprefix would then not be required, the singlekeyprefix is the definition hash. Then the way definition hash and key hash are handled should be pushed downwards into the store.  A reason for this is something like; Redis can uses hashes for each of the definitions. A filestore can do the same thing. Memcached would need to use a different strategy of prefixing the definition hash before the key_hash in a single key.  But it has to do that now.  It will still have all the same purge problems.  But other caches would no longer suffer from purging all versions of identifiers and sharing options when a cache is purged. There is currently very little documentation about the usefulness of identifiers and it's original intended use.  I have spend quite some time working on the caching code and still don't understand the purpose they were made for.  My idea above is much clearer to me. Possible future direction is also to push the calculation of the key into the store rather than the loader.  The store is the one that needs to handle restriction on the keyspace.  Whether it's size or character options available.  Each store could determine the best rules for it.  This coupled with the definition hash change would let a store decide how it indexes the content we send to it.  File stores can have directories, redis can have hashes, mongodb can do the same kind of thing.  Memory caches can just use keys as-is and memcached could put the keys together as it can't ensure unique keys without that. I would like feedback on whether others think this is a move in the right direction and if there are any objections or ideas around this proposal.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: MUC identifiers, proposed change to implementation
ResponsesInList.Text: There has been not feedback on this over a reasonable amount of time.  I'm bumping this for a couple of reasons; 1. See if there can be any buy-in to the idea or comments on it. 2. It has come to my attention through MDL-53875 that session cache is broken and a perfect case for the use of identifiers. To try to explain 2 a little more; Session cache for users is just a set of elements split by session_id().  That is the same as a set of elements split by an identifier.  With the capability of the proposal above, you get session caches to be much more like application caches in terms of code and management.  In my view it would reduce the complexity of the code and provide more consistent interface for users.  As MDL-53875 shows, there isn't any testing around session cache that ensures it cleans up correctly or can find the right sessions to destroy.  Work on MDL-55604 also showed there is no testing around identifiers at this time and the reliability of them is only tested by some use of them in the databasemeta cache.  Some small amount of testing was added in MDL-55604 , however it is a complicated area.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: MUC identifiers, proposed change to implementation
ResponsesInList.Text: I don't have the depth of experience with this to by able to offer much, other than saying what you are proposing sounds reasonable and safer, so I encourage you to go forward with it. On a general off topic note about MUC - since you seem to be working the most in this area, my personal feeling (without actual technical analysis) is that if we should be doing anything, we should actually be reducing the feature set of MUC and only allowing developers to do very performant operations with it. Anecdotally it seems there is so much functionality that many people don't know how to use and too often we are coming across MUC uses which are utilising its 'flexibility' at the cost of performance (e.g. serialisation impact). On reflection I think it would've been better to restrict the way which data which can be stored in MUC so it was as fast as possible rather than as flexible as possible.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Problem insert_record() and special chars
ResponsesInList.Text: Most likely your PHP source file is not saved in UTF8 encoding which is a must for any Moodle development. UTF8 contains ASCII as it's subset so anything written in English is fine. Spanish on the other hand breaks that limitation and hence the characters ó and ñ are most likely incorrectly encoded (probably saved as latin1). Make sure to use correct encoding when creating/editing PHP files for moodle.
