The only time it's enabled is when looking at upgrades for PHP .   Have to do that via command line switch to yum command: --enable-repo=webtatic.   Since I'm limiting the yum search, etc. to just PHP tends to avoid other potential conflicts.   When it comes to PHP and webtatic repo I always do yum without the -y option to see what will be added/replaced, etc.. so that I can 'chicken out'.   Then reissue the command with --exclude=blah to see the results.  One could also check into 'priorities' of yum and set certain repos to 'rule the roost', so to speak.   Time consuming sometimes but .... ResponsesInList.Title: Should we drop MyISAM, so we can finally rely on transactions?
ResponsesInList.Text: At the moment, Moodle has an API for database transactions, but you are not allowed to rely on it because we have to support MySQL with MyISAM storage engine. It occurs to me that since we have just released a long-term support release, then if we are going to drop support ofr MyISAM, now might be the best time to do it. What do other people think? If there is enough support for the idea, I will make a tracker issue.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Should we drop MyISAM, so we can finally rely on transactions?
Re: Should we drop MyISAM, so we can finally rely on transactions?
ResponsesInList.Text: +1 But bear in mind this will not solve some of the developer difficulty with transactions - the ONLY thing it will solve is that there are a few places in core where we do 'if something fails, then delete all the other stuff we've done up until now', which we no longer need (if in a transaction and you throw an error this happens automatically). In particular it won't mean that we are able to rollback transactions as part of normal operation (i.e. normally you will only be able to do a rollback by throwing an error to cancel the entire page). This is because of nested transactions, which cannot be rolled back. I.e. you can't make a function that relies on rollback working just within that function, because whoever called the function might have already started a transaction, and then you can't rollback the inner transaction on its own. Tim knows this already, but just saying for public benefit or something. There's nothing stopping us doing this already, but this change might possibly also be an impetus to add transactions to a few more bits of Moodle that might currently be missing them, to improve database integrity (&, slightly, performance), which would be good. And transactions could be included as a requirement in the coding standards (i.e. any action which includes more than one related database write should be wrapped in a transaction). --sam

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Should we drop MyISAM, so we can finally rely on transactions?
ResponsesInList.Text: +1 to Sam's post! Not to mention the Files API too, where rolling back means rolling a transaction on the database and an action on the "file system", wherever the pool is stored. The design of the pool hosted in the file system can live with files no more referenced in the logic representation within the database but not always the opposite: the Files API implementation is quite mature and stable but it could be useful to review that code too. HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Should we drop MyISAM, so we can finally rely on transactions?
ResponsesInList.Text: 1. The main questions are still "Will this change allow for faster processing speeds for data requests?" and "Will this change reduce immediate resource demands?" One may be able to offset the other, but if both are true, then why not? 2. Support for MariaDB certainly seems to be growing recently, and as MyISAM is no longer the default driver for MySQL then it will become increasingly problematic as a useful tool in any app that uses older versions MySQL. Users will have to update their DB at some point and as we have seen with the demands on updating PHP in the transition from v1.9 to v2.0 this is not always easily accomplished- usually by Users on shared servers. 3. While hdd space is marvelously cheap, and is still declining, devs should still be mindful of it. My understanding is that deletes in MyISAM are left as blank spaces until the DB is optimized, which takes time and processing power. As Moodles do not get smaller over time, this can become somewhat problematic if an overnight cron is not properly set up- which leads to yet another problem with MyISAM. 4. MyISAM may be OK for organizations that have large numbers of reads and smaller numbers of writes, like schools and the like, but increasingly, the peaks and valleys of demand that traditionally flow with the day/night cycle are slowly being eroded by the nature of the changing learning world. I am certain that international enrollments, say at something like the OU for example, are increasing, so the time window when the optimize code can be run to refresh the db is, without significant impact on User experience, becoming smaller. This may not be an issue today, but I strongly suggest it will in the not too distant future. Internationalized MOOCs may or may not be becoming more popular, but Moodle should be able to accommodate them so can it do so while retaining support for MyISAM? Please Note: I don't know if any of this is relevant to Moodle, not being a dev it is hard for me to say, but these are the sorts of issues that I would be considering I suspect, if for no other reason that to ensure that my app is remaining constant, or consistent, with identifiable technical, social, financial developments that will impact upon my app.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Overriding custom question type renderer
ResponsesInList.Text: The answer to that question is rather subtle. The short answer is that for this question type, the display is identical to the standard multiple choice question type, so this question type does not need to privide its own renderer. qtype_multichoice_multi_renderer, defined in question/type/multichoice/renderer.php is used. But, to fully understand, you then need to ask, how does Moodle know to use that class from qtype_multichoice? Well, to get the renderer, the question engine calls $question->get_renderer(). class qtype_multichoiceset_question extends qtype_multichoice_multi_question does not override that method, so the implementation from qtype_multichoice_multi_question is used. (Normally, you don't need to override this method, because the base class provides a sensible default implemenation: https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/master/question/type/questionbase.php#L271 )

ResponsesInList.Title: Best practice for making core customisations
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all. I see a lot of posts on here asking, "How can I change this core functionality?", and many replies saying "just change this line in this file!". This is quick and easy. But once a system has more than a few of these "minor" changes, it becomes a technical debt of sorts. I have spent plenty of time debugging client code that had been previously modified, with undocumented and unexpected effects. Making upgrades to newer Moodle versions easy is also important. Piles of git conflicts to resolve due to custom code is never fun! The best way I have found so far to minimize these issues is to do the following: Add a local plugin, e.g. local/clientname For every core customisation, make a local/clientname setting, with the default being the standard Moodle behaviour In the core code being tweaked, add a check for the relevant setting One advantage is that any changes to standard behaviour can be accounted for on a single settings page, and can be enabled or disabled at will. This helps with figuring out conflicts and regressions. Hopefully this example is explained better with actual code - here's a diff https://gist.github.com/PeloNZ/92c4e4bf99645f773ffd I'd like to know what other devs do for this sort of thing. What tips and tricks do you have? Cheers, Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Best practice for making core customisations
ResponsesInList.Text: If you have customisations in the code, it is best to have them on a separate branch in git. For doing the merge, this technique can minimise merge conflicts: http://tjhunt.blogspot.co.uk/2014/01/moving-ou-moodle-code-to-moodle-261.html

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Best practice for making core customisations
ResponsesInList.Text: I just wanted to point out that what you are doing manually here is the basics of what git would do for you. That is: Keep multiple copies With names so you know what they are (branch names, commit comments) However git gives you lots more if you want or need it an easy way to copy the files from computer to computer (git push / pull / checkout) with a way that verifies that copy is exact, with not file missed or corrupted (git status). an easy way to compare any two versions (git diff). ways to copy specific changes from one copy to another (git cherry-pick / rebase) Git uses an efficient storage format. Most versions of the code you are keeping are very, very similar. For example the current Moodle code is just over 200MB. Git stores the History of all 72,000+ versions of Moodle in 320MB! There is only really one down-side to using git: You have to learn how to use it Some useful links: https://docs.moodle.org/28/en/Git_for_Administrators https://docs.moodle.org/dev/Git_for_developers http://tom.preston-werner.com/2009/05/19/the-git-parable.html http://git-scm.com/book/

ResponsesInList.Title: University (software engineering) senior project collaboration?
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm a university professor who supervises senior projects in software engineering. Some of my students are looking for challenging real-world projects (representing roughly 100 hours of work in a 4-month period). They can be either individual projects or team-oriented. These are engineering students who must show proof of an analysis, a design and of course a working implementation (preferably with tests). Moodle has a set of undeveloped features and certainly needs developers. Obviously nothing stops students from forging ahead blindly and trying to develop features on their own, but I'm wondering if there's a track record of this kind of collaboration and how it has best worked in the past. Would senior Moodle developers be interested in a coordinated kind of collaboration? I'd like to discuss it with them (perhaps offline, if appropriate).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: University (software engineering) senior project collaboration?
ResponsesInList.Text: Have you heard of Google summar-of-code? Moodle has participated in that with very mixed results. Also, there have been a very few occasions in the past where teachers have tried to get their students to contribute, with even more mixed results. Things may be better these days since We have tools like codechecker to make it easier for students to check their own work for the basics. There is better documentation. I agree that in principle, getting students to do real work is a good concept. The biggest difficulty is proably that most university courses teach students to write code, whereas the most important skill is to read code.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: University (software engineering) senior project collaboration?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Cris, Mentoring students on a development project can be a big commitment - Google Summer of Code is good because it allows the Mentor to choose a student that they would be willing to mentor on a project they are interested in. In my experience working with University projects this is a bit harder to get right. If you could match your project timeline with GSOC it could help a lot - from what I understand the GSOC guidelines allow this: http://www.google-melange.com/gsoc/document/show/gsoc_program/google/gsoc2012/faqs#course_credit I do have an interest in mentoring students on development projects but I don't have a lot of available time - you could reach out to some of the local Moodle Partners in your area who may be interested in partnering with you - they may even be interested in hiring students after graduation!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: University (software engineering) senior project collaboration?
ResponsesInList.Text: Dan, etc., Thanks for your replies. The GSOC angle and getting credit is interesting, but not what I was aiming for. I should explain more how our senior projects work: mandatory one semester project (4 months, 135 hours, but at least 20 go to preparing a summary report and presentation for the course grade) students are at the end of a software engineering bachelor's degree (capstone project, aka senior project) they already have a professor mentor (e.g., me) they usually already have an idea for a project, but often it's not feasible and they need a backup (e.g., a Moodle feature, such as TAG search for questions) they must do analysis and design as well as coding (e.g., a conceptual UML model of relationships between questions and non-hierarchical keywords, a class design showing PHP elements and database elements in the solution, a working solution). they must develop iteratively (2-3 week iterations where they demo their result to a "client" and get feedback to drive the next iteration) they must track risks and mitigations (e.g., search algorithm XYZ used to find questions is not optimal and may have bad performance with large question banks, perform tests with huge question banks). Iterative projects (I avoid the word agile because it means different things to different people) don't have firm commitments as to what will completely work at the end. In one semester, students get at most 4 iterations (usually only 3) and so I hope they can get 2-3 important features working well. Sometimes, it's easier than they imagined and they get more working. The idea is to start with a set of related features that are sufficiently complex, but prioritizing them in the development so that the most important (risky) ones get working as soon as possible. The angle I'm looking for from Moodle's developing community is an eventual commitment to a project schedule for collaboration (not managing, but mentoring is always great). That is, some senior Moodle developers could give suggest features that are needed urgently, provide feedback at the end of iterations, provide input into design decisions and code revues (not mandatory, but would be awesome), etc. It's the prof's responsibility to supervise the academic engineering part of the project, but it's way more useful if the "problem domain " part has input from an expert community. I only tried once to use an open-source project with a senior project a few years back (there were only two developers on the project). There was really very little input from them, but I suspect there were several reasons: 1) the project was not as active as Moodle, 2) they weren't very interested in the extension the student had chosen. Regardless, the project was a success and the little input from the open-source developers was better than a virtual project with no collaboration. To maximize the benefit, it would be good to get input on what features are priorities at Moodle and which ones can easily be broken into iterative chunks for a student. I'm aware of the tracker site, but not sure how it can be browsed to find those answers. That's probably where senior Moodle developers can help to provide that kind of advice. Having that "prioritized feature list," I can suggest it to students who are at the choice-phase (before the semester starts).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: University (software engineering) senior project collaboration?
ResponsesInList.Text: Cris, many small (100 hours) but important and highly desirable enhancements can be packaged in Moodle plugins such as blocks, locals etc. Your students' projects can be designed and developed as such. In the requirement analysis students can justify the importance by referencing tracker issues and forum discussions. You can install these plugins in your local environment and evaluate them for grades. Then they can be contributed to the community via the Moodle plugin repository or git . And some of these enhancements may some day find their way to core in a controlled way. Everybody wins.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: University (software engineering) senior project collaboration?
ResponsesInList.Text: Cris: Your description of these languishing tracker items as purgatory is quite apt!!  I wonder what Anthony will think of this term.  Theologically it may be accurate.  A staging place on the way to a better place. There are a large number of items that are core to the basic way user manage a Moodle site that Moodle has just not bothered about.  There are a range of reasons why which are not really pertinent here.  I have been banging on at this question now for 5 years, but there are still a lot of issues languishing in the tracker. There has been more of a push to make Moodle plugable rather than sort some of these things.  Martin's latest statement recently is this: " I try to get myself and my small company involved with the many parts of Moodle as much as I can, but mostly we focus on making a stable core platform for the community to build on and share code via moodle.org/plugins etc" - so effort in your students in plugins is a good place to start as someone has said. There is a list here which I wrote: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=245531 which is a few enhancements I think would be very valuable to a typical admin/teacher.  Moodle really has not a good track record in picking off even the low hanging fruit here.  As far as I can see there are almost none of these requests in either 2.6 or 2.7.  These are some tracker items worth looking at. IMO , an opinion of one. By the way, as of last month, this plugin lacks a maintainer: https://moodle.org/plugins/view.php?plugin=mod_certificate As to supervision, there are probably issues with senior developers getting involved in terms of time.  And there is another issue written up here: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=180865#p788945 , the language barrier. However, I believe if you work on a problem in Moodle, of which there are many great problems to choose from in my list (and believe me I can expand it by another 15-20) you will get a lot of help in the forums from non-HQ developers.  Many of them are too busy coding to post here anyway. BUT: caution your students.  Coming here and saying "I have a masters project to do, plez help me, cheers" never endears anyone. Just my opinion. -Derek

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: University (software engineering) senior project collaboration?
ResponsesInList.Text: "2) they weren't very interested in the extension the student had chosen" This will still be an issue when working with Moodle devs - not many Moodle devs would be willing to commit to your project schedule as volunteers and those that do are likely to have a very limited field of interest. This is one strong point of the GSOC model - The moodle devs that are willing to mentor develop a list of projects they are interested in and students can apply to work on those projects. If you could develop a relationship with your local Moodle Partner this might still work - they may have more motivation to help the local university and the bigger partners might have enough staff to be able to cover a wide range of Moodle code. I work for a Moodle Partner and we have a range of initiatives working with students from local universities/colleges on various projects.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Link to file every downloading
ResponsesInList.Text: Almost any file served through pluginfile.php is forced for download regardless of the forcedownload parameter. Only course category, course, course section, backup and few others honor forcedownload param. You should revert to static file. For details look into file_plugin_file function in lib/filelib.php.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Adhoc Tasks are not firing
ResponsesInList.Text: Bryan Debugging ad-hoc tasks is really tricky. I think you won't get anything in the apache logs, because the task is run via cron . Which brings up the first thing to check, is cron running? You can just hit it with: [MYSITE]/admin/cron.php and cron will run, and you should see some output for your ad hoc task in there. If there is nothing there, not even an error, then your task is not being picked up. Possibly the namespace is wrong? For scheduled tasks you can run them from the command line. See here: https://docs.moodle.org/27/en/Cron#Debugging_Scheduled_Tasks If there was a trick like this for ad hoc tasks it would be good.

ResponsesInList.Text: question/type/multichoice is the multiple choice question type. (Where the right answer can either involve selecting one, or many, choice. question/type/multianswer is called the Embedded answer (Cloze) question type in the user interface.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Question about question types - multianswer / multichoice
ResponsesInList.Text: The simplest option is to just create the questions in Moodle. That will work, but will get a bit boring. Probably the simplest way to automate it a bit it to use Export and Import in the question bank. Create one question in Moodle with all the answers you want. Export it to a file (Moodle XML or GIFT). Edit that file in your text editor, and make many copies of the question. Change the question text in each copy, but leave the rest the same. Import the edited file. An even more advanced option would be to create a custom question type plugin, but that is probably overkill.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re:  Theme CSS Not Updating

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: javascript in moodle and then non javascript version...
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Ryan, As Tim says, this is no longer a requirements within Moodle. Screen readers have caught up with standards and are now able to process changes through JavaScript. Furthermore, we no longer require a non-JS version of code in Moodle (we used to). We have also removed the "Screenreader" and " AJAX " settings within Moodle and expect all code to return the same output. There is one class on the body which we still insert - ` jsenabled `. This is added by a piece of Javascript during the page load and historically was used to allow theming based on whether the browser supported JavaScript. See the CSS for action-menu as an example of how this has been typically used. Most browsers these days make it much harder to turn off JavaScript. For Firefox you must go under the hood and disable it in the settings registry. There really isn't a good reason that I'm aware of to disable JS. I'm also unaware of any way to detect when a user has opened a new tab, window, etc. Some browsers may give browser window lost clues, but as far as I'm aware, these are non-standard. With screenreaders, there is no need to play any sound to alert the user that a page has done something, or has finished loading, etc. The correct use of ARIA attributes such as aria-live, aria-describedby, etc. will ensure that things are announced. In addition to all of the above, I'm not aware of any way to reliably detect the presence of a screenreader (in fact, I'm not aware of any at all). Doing so could be argued to be a breach of user privacy (e.g. user tracking, advertising etc.), and both users and screenreader developers argue that the same content should be provided to both sighted, and non-sighted users and should have the correct markup. With regards your third point, I'm not aware of anything in Moodle core which does this at present anyway. What are the options for sighted and non-deaf users there? The content should be accessible to all, regardless of abilities. Either way, you would need to look at a community plugin for this functionality. Best wishes, Andrew

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Ryan, 1) Ad blockers should not disable JavaScript. If Admins disable it, they need to be educated. We're in 2015. The days of disabling JS for funsies have left us. I don't know of any ad blockers, firewall, or AV checker which disables JS. 2) That's hardly a use-case. We are supporting real users. Real users do not run with the developer tools continuously open. 3) There are browser extensions for colour blind folk, and all themes are designed to be high colour contrast. There are so many different types of colour blindness, we cannot cater to all. 4) You could care less about this, but the screen reader's developers and users do. They *DO NOT* make this information available to us and, in my opinion, nor should they. 5) Yes - but that is intrusive and not necessarily helpful. If you want to do this on your system, then you can write a local plugin. Often people have multiple windows open, and want to be able to view both at the same time - reading from one, writing notes or looking at references in another. Not-focused != not in use. It drives me nuts when Facebook pauses a Video I'm watching in one window while I have something else open. I have multiple monitors - let me use them! 6) You will have to look at the JS yourself here - it's not a part of core Moodle Q1: AFAIK , it's good ARIA. I haven't looked at it in any great detail Q2: "drop down section menus"? What are these? If you mean the expanding forms, then I believe that they are good for accessibility . In fact, I was chatting to a blind user on Friday who uses NVDA who started the conversation by telling me how much he loves them and how they work really well with the screen readers he was using (NVDA, Jaws, and VoiceOver). Q3: Define okay? I doubt whether many blind users will use any of the drag/drop functionality. We don't actually recommend it for them. Drag/drop file upload is largely beyond our control; and we provide an alternative method for moving resources because drag/drop is *very* hard for screen readers. I suggest that you take a look at the ARIA specification , the authoring practices , and other documentation at http://www.w3.org/WAI/intro/aria.php Andrew

ResponsesInList.Title: Safer delete for course modules (aka Recycle Bin)
ResponsesInList.Text: We keep on running into issues every now and then about a user complaining that they deleted a file or course module and wants the data recovered. The process often involves us taking a recent snapshot of the database , load it up another another server . If files are involved we rsync the file system to another server and "hope" that the deleted files aren't yet purged from the file cleanup cron. Then we do a backup/restore of the single course module. This process is not always smooth and is such a hassle that involves hours of manual intervention. What if we had a "deleted" flag in the course module data that acts like a super "visible" flag. So that the content doesn't show up for any user. Or we can overload the "visible" flag for a third state of "deleted"? Then we have a weekly or so cron that will clean up course modules that are flagged as deleted if the flag was set at a certain time interval? Seems like a possible simple concept that would save people from shooting themselves in the foot. We would have a report that can allow users to "undelete" deleted course modules. This is a past discussion: Undelete or recycler for all deleted items? It was also mentioned in the Perth Hackfest years ago , but nothing seemed to come out of it. I hope to drum up interest and I wonder if my proposed approach is along the right way or not. I created a tracker issue for this: https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-48012

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Safer delete for course modules (aka Recycle Bin)
ResponsesInList.Text: Just to say +1 to the idea - the general principle of making actions reversible is a UX concept I feel we should be trying to apply more widely across Moodle. Petr has commented on your issue concerned that this will be complex to implement - its unwise to take Petr's comments lightly ;) but i'm little a bit more optimistic about this. I've seen a lot of the course module handling improved and refactored into manageable pieces in recent releases - particularly with things like conditional availability causing change. Problem area I'd immediately think of is the gradebook..

ResponsesInList.Title: DMARC Causing tons of bounces
ResponsesInList.Text: My Version: Moodle 2.4.9 It seems that Yahoo!, Comcast, and AOL have been busy over the weekend and have issued a new more restricted DMARC policy on their email domains, causing students and instructors with these email addresses to no longer receive notifications from Moodle. This is because Moodle inserts the student/instructor email address into the FROM header, and sends the email on behalf of that person. See example header from bounced message below. In this example, it seems to be effecting anything using a Yahoo address as sending or receiving. ------------------------------------------------------------------ 550-5.7.1 Unauthenticated email from yahoo.com is not accepted due to domain 's 550-5.7.1 DMARC policy. Please contact administrator of yahoo.com domain if 550-5.7.1 this was a legitimate mail. Please visit 550-5.7.1 http://support.google.com/mail/answer/2451690 to learn about DMARC 550 5.7.1 initiative. m6si942994qay.218 - gsmtp (in reply to end of DATA command) Final-Recipient: rfc822; email@gmail.com Original-Recipient: rfc822;email@gmail.com Action: failed Status: 5.7.1 Remote-MTA: dns; gmail-smtp-in.l.google.com Diagnostic-Code: smtp ; 550-5.7.1 Unauthenticated email from yahoo.com is not ---------- Forwarded message ---------- From: "Joe Smith" <joesmith@yahoo.com> To: "Jane Doe" <Janedoe@gmail.com> Cc: Date: Tue, 8 Apr 2014 11:00:24 -0400 Subject: Course Subject ----------------------------------- There has been a bunch of uproar this week from it, mentioned here http://www.theregister.co.uk/2014/04/08/yahoo_breaks_every_mailing_list_in_the_world_says_email_guru/ John Levine talks about the impact this has and what he has been doing to address it - such as telling people to change their email address. In Moodle, there hasn't been any discussion on this. There is no place in the administration interface to edit email headers so I have been trying to figure out how to do it in the lib/moodlelib.php file but haven't had any luck. What needs to be done, seeing in this section at the DMARC website http://www.dmarc.org/faq.html#s_22 , is to change the FROM address to be the same as the No-Reply address or the email for the domain, and then set the REPLY TO as the student/instructor email address. Though I am not sure how to do this and I want to bring this up to the community for review and to hopefully get some help.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: DMARC Causing tons of bounces
ResponsesInList.Text: Fixed! Below is a copy of my code. The change needs to be made in the lib/moodlelib.php file. I am in terminal right now so I can't tell what line I am on but search for the following and you will find it. if ( is_string( $from)) { // So we can pass whatever we want if there is need $mail->From     = $CFG->noreplyaddress; $mail->FromName = $from; } else if ($usetrueaddress and $from->maildisplay) { // Changing this due to new DMARC policy requirements //$mail->From     = $from->email; $mail->From     = $CFG->noreplyaddress; $mail->FromName = fullname( $from); } else { $mail->From     = $CFG->noreplyaddress; $mail->FromName = fullname( $from); if ( empty( $replyto)) { $tempreplyto[] = array( $CFG->noreplyaddress, get_string( 'noreplyname')); } } Of course you could also remove the part of the else statement and it would still work as well. Also of note I did not change anything with the Reply To, as it is really not needed since the message body tends to include links to interact with the notification by pointing the recipient back to Moodle. This is a temporary solution which hopefully will be addressed in future Moodle patches.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Capabilities to Delete Activities (Prevent Deleting of Assignments with Submissions)
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Tim, I've been burrowing through the code this afternoon to figure out the simplest way of achieving a 'Recycle Bin' . One of the simplest ways that I can think of achieving this (who doesn't prefer simple solutions) is to extend the existing logic for deleting a course module (course/lib.php course_delete_module). My idea is as follows, add a 'deleted' tag to the course_modules table, that will be 0 for not deleted, and when it's set as deleted it would be a timestamp of when. When the delete function is called, it checks to see what this value is, if it's got a timestamp then actually run the delete process. If it hasn't, then set the value to the current timestamp. This then allows for the function that loads course modules for viewing in a course to be changed, to ignore anything with a value set in deleted (We don't want them to appear on a course anymore as they should now be found in the recycle bin). Then we can create a page that loads all the course modules that have a value in a new page called 'Recycle Bin', allowing users to permanently delete this or to restore it. The benefits of this flag and timestamp, is it's simple to restore content back to where it was. And with the timestamp we can empty the recycle bin every x days. There would be backups, and this isn't meant to become a permanent store of information. I'm not sure what others thoughts are on this?

ResponsesInList.Title: Event Handling documentation issue
ResponsesInList.Text: The event handling documentation states The handler function accepts one parameter (the event data object) and should return a boolean. Returning false indicates that there was an error and the event will be left in the event queue. We have run into issues with the Turnitin Plagiarism plugin in that it returns false here if the TII EULA hasn't been agreed. What seems to actually happen is that if the handler function returns false this gets bubbled back up the chain of event handling code (events_dispath, events_process_queued_handler, events_cron) and in the events_process_queued_handler() event it updates the event_queue_handler status with a +1 and returns a false. In events_cron if the returned status === false, then entire handler function is disabled and nothing subsequently gets processed! So here is the crux of the post: the statement at the top is wrong. Yes the event is left in the queue, but nothing else in the queue that is being dealt by that handler with will get processed until this event is cleared! The documentation seems to imply that if you have an event but your handler decides that it wants to defer processing until later, it can just return false. But it can't because if it does, any subsequent events that are in the queue for that handler that may not want to be deferred won't run

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Event Handling documentation issue
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Michael, I've come across this issue before. The documentation isn't clear as you say. I think that basically events must return true , regardless of what happens in the event code, to avoid the queuing situation you describe. Updating the documentation is easy enough, writing the above so it makes sense, on the other hand...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SQL query for Obtaining userid, questionid, response, correct response for a particular question attempt
ResponsesInList.Text:
This works 
```text
SELECT
upper(u.username),
FROM_UNIXTIME(qas.timecreated), 
qa.rightanswer,
qa.responsesummary,
q.name as question,
u.id

FROM mdl_quiz_attempts quiza
JOIN mdl_question_usages qu ON qu.id = quiza.uniqueid
JOIN mdl_question_attempts qa ON qa.questionusageid = qu.id
JOIN mdl_question q ON qa.questionid = q.id
JOIN mdl_question_attempt_steps qas ON qas.questionattemptid = qa.id
JOIN mdl_user u ON qas.userid = u.id
LEFT JOIN mdl_question_attempt_step_data qasd ON qasd.attemptstepid = qas.id

WHERE quiza.id in (SELECT id FROM mdl_quiz_attempts WHERE quiz = (select instance from mdl_course_modules where id = 1))

Is there any way to configure Moodle so all emails sent out by the application would use the same email address?    If not, how do you get around sending emails from the server that the Moodle site is hosted on and emails going out using other email addresses like the students or even the teachers, such as blahblah@yahoo.com?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Email Sending Problem
ResponsesInList.Text: In site admin menu, search for 'replyto'.  What search returns will point to two settings that are related to your question. Think the recommendation is to use an SMTP server through which to relay mail.  SMTP servers generally have the appropriate SPF or DKIM records in the DNS zone for that domain and have less issues with other systems and their spam checkers/filters.  Or, if you have control of the DNS zone in which the Moodle server resides and access to the DNS records, you could create your own SPF/DKIM records for the Moodle server itself. IF your moodle server is not part of the same domain as the SMTP server domain, then one has to allow relay from the moodle server through the SMTP server.   That is not done via Moodle, but, rather, the config of the SMTP server.   The only thing Moodle config of SMTP does is to send all mail to an address on the SMTP: server using appropriate/authorized login credentials. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: using Git with Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle HQ use something similar for maintaining the code for all Moodle community sites (such as this moodle.org). Our model is slightly different from what the Open University uses and seems to work well for us, too. Basically, we have a clone of moodle.git. In a certain and well defined point (best identified by some upstream tag), we create our own tag that acts as a base point for the whole site composition. Let us say this base tag is called `ourmoodle-2.8-base` and it matches the commit tagged as `v2.8.0` . The basic idea of our model is that every single local hack/customization and every single additional plugin goes into its own "feature" branch. All these branches are created off the base tag. We have certain rules on naming these branches, which helps to administer it all. Let us say there is a branch `ourmoodle-2.8-theme` where the site theme plugin is committed (we commit just snapshots of additional plugins, they have their own development history in their native repositories) and another branch called `ourmoodle-2.8-login-page-hack` with some customization. We create a branch called `ourmoodle-2.8-test` and we merge all feature branches ourmoodle-2.8-* as well as upstream MOODLE_28_STABLE branch to it. This -test branch can be deployed on our notebooks and the test server and it helps us to be sure that we all share 100% same version of the code. Once we are happy with testing, the -test branch is again merged to another `ourmoodle-2.8-deploy` branch that is then deployed to the production site. When a new 2.8 stable version is available, we simply merge MOODLE_28_STABLE into the `ourmoodle-2.8-test` branch (and then, after testing the upgrade etc), we merge that into `ourmoodle-2.8-deploy` again. This can be done easily for every weekly build, if we want to. When doing the major version upgrade, say from 2.8 to 2.9 in this example, we principally use `git rebase --onto` . We are aware of every single modification done in our 2.8 site (because they all are tracked on separate branches) so we can re-create ("replant") these feature branches in the new version. In other words, we create a new base tag `ourmoodle-2.9-base` and we create a new branch `ourmoodle-2.9-login-page-hack` from it. We know that all the commits in the range `ourmoodle-2.8-base..ourmoodle-2.8-login-page-hack` need to be re-applied to this new branch. We usually use git-rebase, git-cherry-pick or git-format-patch && git-am to do that. If there is a conflict, we know that upstream has changed and we need to investigate further. Even if the patches apply without the conflict, testing is still needed as there might be some change elsewhere that does not allow the customization work any more.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: using Git with Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Having experimented a lot with the different ways of doing this, David's way is the best in my opinion. I wrote a blog post on this strategy 18 months ago ( http://thamblings.blogspot.com.au/2013/07/upgrading-moodle-from-git.html ), and I know that the people that I used to work with still use it. The strategy was developed largely from the ideas of several core Moodle Developers, and based on the experiences of other organisations (including the Open University). I'd highly recommend looking into this. Things to note: David mentions the base branch. It should always be based on the .0 tag (e.g. 2.8.0; 2.7.0; 2.6.0). It should never be a point release (e.g. 2.8.1; 2.7.3). David discovered that using a forward-slash as a separator between the instance+version and the feature name is much more powerful (e.g. instead of ourmoodle-2.8-login-page-hack, use ourmoodle-2.8/login-page-hack). This allows you to do such magic as git push myrepo/ourmoodle-2.8/* I'd also recommend that you create a task in your project's bug tracker for the next release. E.g. If you are running 2.8 now, then your next major release will be 2.9. Under that project, create a sub-task for every feature branch that you merge (e.g. Merge login-page-hack branch). When it comes to your upgrade time, you can then go through that list and tick them off, one-by-one. If you no longer need your login page hack, then you can comment on the subtask to say why and you have a record for future reference. As I say, I would highly recommend this approach. Andrew

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: using Git with Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Hittesh, The reason that I would really recommend always basing on the .0 release is because it makes your life much easier in the long run. In my experience, most of the feature branches you're creating are for plugins which you want installed. These do not need to be based on a point release. The other frequent type are the inclusion of hot-fixes before they are included in a point release. The less-frequent type are for the inclusion of hacks to Moodle core. In all of these cases, there is no real benefit to basing on a point release, and doing so can complicate things at upgrade time. By basing on the major release tag, when it comes to the next release; you can simply do: 
```text
# Fetch from our upstreams
git fetch ourprivaterepo
git fetch origin

# Checkout the feature branch for the current version of Moodle
git checkout ourmoodle-2.8/some-feature-branch

# Create and checkout a branch for our intended version
git checkout -b ourmoodle-2.9/some-feature-branch

# Rebase on that release
git rebase v2.9.0

# Push it back to our repository
git push ourprivaterpo ourmoodle-2.9/some-feature-branch
```
 As you can imagine, the above can easily be scripted to take three things and automate this. the source tag (v2.8.0); the target tag (v2.9.0); and a list of branches to try and rebase. The alternative would be to use rebase --onto as David discusses. Both ways are fine, but with major tags it is generally much easier for 99% of situations, and is also much faster to do. The way that rebase --onto essentially works is to rollback each commit from the point release to the shared point (e.g. v2.8.0), and then replay all of the commits between v2.8.0 and v2.9.0. There will be some situations where you have to base your branch on top of a point release (e.g. because your change conflicts with a change in a point release), but for the majority of situations this way is much less confusing and is generally easier and faster to update with. Generally the occasions where you're basing on a point release are more likely to require manual intervention because of conflicts. Andrew

ResponsesInList.Title: use of external libraries with a YUI module wrapper
ResponsesInList.Text: Hey, I'm currently working on a street map block plugin with some additional geolocation functionality (push latest geolocation via ajax to server and safe it in the $USER session variable). By the way is there a better way to wrap leaflet with YUI rather than explicit call 'load' and use the slightly ugly callback after Y.Get finished? ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Git query, sort of loosely Moodleish :)
ResponsesInList.Text: Instead of deleting your repository, could you just rename it instead?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Git query, sort of loosely Moodleish :)
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Mat, Rather than deleting it, you can: 
```text
cd filter/oembed
git remote remove origin
git remote add origin git://github.com/MSOpenTech/moodle-filter_oembed
git remote add public git://github.com/grum1975/moodle-filter_oembed
```
 This will change where your repository points to. Rather than pointing to your own repository (originally origin), it now points to the MSOpenTech repository as the 'origin'. The third line adds your repository back as a repository called 'public'. You can now update your copy. Assuming you have no changes in your repository you currently wish to push: 
```text
# Checkout your old master and rename it:
git checkout master
git branch -M old_master

# Get the latest changes from MSOpenTech
git fetch origin

# Checkout the latest copy from MSOpenTech
git checkout origin/master

# Now push the MSOpentech master to your master
git push --force public master
```
 Now, to push any of your changes: 
```text
# Checkout a new branch for this set of changes:
git checkout -b some_feature_branch

# Make your changes

# Add and commit your changes:
git add .
git commit 

# Now push it to your branch
git push public some_feature_branch

# Then go to github and submit a pull request.
```
 Hope this helps, Andrew

Content creator may specify an instance of a field to be "read-only", in which case student's previously-entered value will just show up (in that activity) as inline text, not as a text entry box. Student may edit the values in the text fields at any time (except in activities where they're marked as read-only). ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Seeking a "show/save aribtrary input data" plugin
ResponsesInList.Text: I don't know of any activity like this. However, you may want to consider creating a Moodle filter instead of an activity. A filter is basically a way to do search/replace on any input before it is output, for example in the contents of a page resource, but it will work anywhere. For example there are several filters running here. If I type [ [Debugging] ] without the spaces, that will get replaced with a link ```text Debugging ``` (but without the extra spaces, which I have added to stop another filter, one which looks for anything like a URL and turns it into a clickable link. If I just type https://docs.moodle.org/en/Debugging then that will become a link without me doing anything. So, if you want, you could make a filter that looks something like {{name=inputid|width=30}} or {{name=inputid|width=20|readonly}} in the text, and replaces it with a text box. You would probably then also need some JavaScript / Ajax code to handle putting in the value, and saving it when it changes. See https://docs.moodle.org/dev/Filters for docs. This approach is probably simpler than building an activity, but is not without its issues. E.g. How do you stop students typing that sort of thing into a forum? (The answer might be https://docs.moodle.org/28/en/Managing_filters - only enable the filter in the places you need it.)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Including js file in plugin page
ResponsesInList.Text: I battled with this when I was first writing Moodle plugins too. Actually once you get the hang of it though, Moodle loads up all your javascript nicely. If you just output the script tags in the middle of the page, the sky won't fall in. And it will work. If you need to load Js/ css files in the head of the page you can add the script tags in the additional html section of site administration->appearance. But the recommended way to do it is as Damyon stated, and it works pretty well. Basically: i) you load JS files using $PAGE->requires->js ii) you put all your javascript functions etc inside a file called module.js in your plugin. iii) you call $PAGE->requires->js_init_call('[YOUR FUNCTION NAME]', $YOURPARAMS); (you can add two more params to this function call that will load some YUI libraries etc, but that optional) Then Moodle will load your required JS , and after that load your module.js and call your function(s). The best way is to look at a simple plugin that does all this. Anything will do, but this is a template I use when making my plugins: https://github.com/justinhunt/moodle-mod_newmodule see view.php and module.js

ResponsesInList.Title: How should we organise less in a plugin
ResponsesInList.Text:
There are a lot of advantages to less over CSS , and its adoption into the Moodle core themes has been well received.
As a plugin developer I want to be able to use less in my plugins, I am particularly keen on the organisation it provides as I believe it better conveys my design intentions during development. Of course I am well aware that I can use less within my own plugin any which way I want.
The purpose of this post is to perhaps generate a bit of discussion about how it could best be done so that we can ask Moodle HQ to include it in the coding style docs as a convention. Personally I think its really important that we don't start discussing whether less should be automatically compiled into styles.css or anything along those lines as at that point there are a lot of questions and technical discussions. I think the focus should be on simply where to put it so that we can start including it with confidence. At present Moodle has no conventions for including less within a plugin. This means that: No less can be added to any core plugin. Without a properly discussed and documented convention that would be a hard sell. I can't be sure how to add less to our own plugins because we want to take Moodles approach so as to have consistency of knowledge. Personally I think that we should use a less directory within the plugin root directory that contains any less the plugin has and most importantly a styles.less file that is the build point for all of the plugins less. If a plugin wishes to have theme specific styles then there should also be styles_themename.less to generate the corresponding styles_themename.css. There should be no importation of less from outside of the plugin. This could not be considered safe as it adds dependencies for the plugin. As mentioned above I don't think plugin less files should be automatically compiled by Moodle when generating the full CSS. This can be discussed on MDL-45482 . Mitigating the risk of an unknowning developer/designer modifying the styles.css file for a plugin with less I think is an important consideration. My feeling on it are that compiling in the same way Moodle compiles the bootstrap less is going to be enough as the compressed CSS should be a giveaway that there is a build process. From there we would just rely on institutional knowledge that if a less directory exists the CSS is generated. That raising one more point, under no circumstances should a plugin use less to generate part only part of the CSS. It should be all less generated or not. Cheers Sam

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How should we organise less in a plugin
ResponsesInList.Text: For reference my interest in this came about through MDL-36296 wherein I have reorganised the CSS in the navigation block making it simpler and fixing a few bugs. I did so using less, that will will not land to core because of a lack of convention. I feel this won't be the last time it comes up and would like to see a convention established for the future.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How should we organise less in a plugin
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Sam, In general I like the idea, but there are some potential issues with IE . IE9 and below will only support 4095 selectors per file (and I expect some of the sites with a large number of plugins are likely to come across this issue - I'm not opposed to dropping support of IE9 :D), whereas IE10 and up support 65534 selectors per file (possible, but highly unlikely to exceeded). The source for this is at http://blogs.msdn.com/b/ieinternals/archive/2011/05/14/internet-explorer-stylesheet-rule-selector-import-sheet-limit-maximum.aspx As an extension to this, it's been crossing my mind whether it is worth using less in our themes, but haven't devoted too much time to it as it appears that Moodle combines and minifies them anyway when in production mode.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How should we organise less in a plugin
ResponsesInList.Text: An interesting thought is that if we go for grunt I think that we would be able to support this kind of thing quite nicely with the use of distributed gruntfiles (assuming you can do that!) for relevant plugins. I think this would work well for core - because we would be able to verify programmatically  if someone modified the built file but not the source file.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Use Annotate PDF beyond assessments
ResponsesInList.Text: This sounds like a good idea, but something that would take a while to implement. Whilst much of the front-end could be reused, a lot of the back-end code for PDF annotation is fairly firmly connected to the assignment code. I would have thought that, like the PDF annotation code, this would be best developed initially as a 3rd-part plugin. Once this has been tried out and any practical issues around it have been worked out in real situations, then it could be put forward for (possible) integration into Moodle core. The question is, do you have any kind of budget to cover this development? Alternatively you could consider seeing if there was enough interest for a group of people to crowd-fund it? Or maybe you will be lucky and a developer will offer to take it on as a pet project? I'd estimate that a developer, who knew what they were doing, would need to spend 3 or 4 days to put together such a plugin.

ResponsesInList.Title: A one-time moodle developers problem
ResponsesInList.Text: It is happened that I often become a coach for the one-time Moodle developers. People come, fix the issue they are interested in and go, often to never return to the Moodle development. I find current JIRA settings tricky for them, since they not belongs to the "developers" group. They coudn't fill "testing instructions" and pull repository/pull branch/pull diff field as they don't have permissions to edit issues. They could only post info to the comments, from where I (or someone else) should copy it to the issue fields. Worse, no one can't set them as a righful issue assignee as this field seems limited to the developers, no simple jira-users can be placed there. They coudn't send code for peer review either, but this may be not so bad as an extra check is always good for the new developers code. What is supposed process for such people? Should they apply for jira developer status even if they do just one issue? Or could you propose another way to work with them?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: A one-time moodle developers problem
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks Oleg for raising this. I am going to ping Marina Glancy (our development process officer) to join this discussion. The current JIRA setup is a result of the continuous tweaking to make it acceptable for most involved developers. From what I understand (to be confirmed by Marina) is that these "hitchhikers" should ideally leave a Git patch file or git-pull details in the comment. And the assignee is to be set to moodle.com. We have a policy to try hard and record the credit for the original author of the patch. Such reported patches should be detected properly during the triage - see https://docs.moodle.org/dev/Bug_triage#Labels Related information is probably https://docs.moodle.org/dev/Peer_reviewing#External_peer_review It seems that the https://docs.moodle.org/dev/Process might be more specific about this case.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: A one-time moodle developers problem
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks for detailed answer, David. I wonder what may be wrong with allowing all users in assignee field. moodle.com seems to be the last entity representing such "hitchhickers". AFAIK been set as assignee just recognizes user's work on the issue and doesn't give him any privileges simple users may exploit.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: A one-time moodle developers problem
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Oleg We can not give more permissions to the general users for the simple reason that we would not be able to revoke them if they are misused, don'tforget that registration on the tracker is open to everybody. Unfortunately jira is very unflexible with permissions and we can't give permission to edit one field without giving permission to edit all fields. Currently the process is the following: User can recommend a patch by commenting on any issue. They can include git repo, branch, diff and testing instructions in their comment. component lead or I will spot it and submit the issue for peer review. All components are watched by anybody, even if they don't have an assigned component lead, so commenting on the issue will send an email to all watchers. peer reviewer will fill the necessary fields on the issue from the comment and leave Assignee field empty or put moodle.com there. Peer reviewer will also suggest developer the changes in the patch if necessary. peer reviewer will send the issue for integration if integrator is happy with the issue and integrates it, he will add the developer to the jira-developer group and put his name in the "Assignee" field Sometimes we spot people who are actively working on several issues and add them to jira-developers group even when none of their issues was integrated yet. But generally the requirement is to have at least one patch in the form of git branch that was accepted in integration. I'll be happy to hear your suggestions on how we can improve or change this process.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: A one-time moodle developers problem
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, Marina. I agree with you about permissions on the tracker. But AFAIK been an assignee of an issue doesn't give you any particular permission. So I wonder why ability to be assignee is limited to jira-developers only and can't be allowed to just any jira-user.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: A one-time moodle developers problem
ResponsesInList.Text: This is a good question. Let me redirect it back to you: when would we need to set assignee as somebody who is not a developer? And also we would like to encourage users to submit the patches as git branches, and being listed as Assignee becomes a reward for putting an effort in complying with the Moodle process.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: A one-time moodle developers problem
ResponsesInList.Text: Marina wrote " when would we need to set assignee as somebody who is not a developer? " Not a jira-developer memeber you mean. Just one-time moodle developer. Well, the asnwer is in my first post of this discussion (and it's name partially).  You could look on examples in MDL-23545 and MDL-6340 . They submit patches as git branches, They comply with the process as far as their rights allows. But they can't be listed as Assignee because this is their first patch for the Moodle. And - as far as I know them - the last for many, so I see no sense in adding them to jira-developer. Still, I guess they deserve been listed as Assignee.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: A one-time moodle developers problem
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Oleg, first of all, thank you for mentoring the developers and contributing to Moodle. We appreciate it very much. As for those two issues (and similar to them), as I already said above - they will be added to jira-developers group once the issue is integrated. It's better to set assignee to moodle.com when you push such issues for peer review, this way it will be more clear to the integrator that the actual developer does not yet have all permissions. Thanks again!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: multiple schools on a single mooodle install?
ResponsesInList.Text: The bit about several different Moodles running on one server is just a standard feature of web servers. For example you can configure one server running Apache to provide different web sites, e.g. several of the sites moodle.org, download .moodle.org, docs.moodle.org and tracker.moodle.org are on the same server, although I can't remember the details. Anyway, that is a web server configuration issue, not really a Moodle-specific one. Another example is my desktop computer where I do development, I have 5 different versions of Moodle installed: localhost/moodle/, localhost/1.9/, localhost/1.8/, localhost/1.7/ and localhost/1.6/. Then there is the question of managing users. If you want the same set of users in several different Moodles, you first have to ask, "where will the master data be?". That is, you want to be just editing the list of users in one place, and then have all the other places use that master list. The answer may either be one particular Moodle site, or a database outside Moodle. Once you know the answer to that question, you can then look at the various authentication plugins . Alternatively, you might find that Moodle Network is what you want.

ResponsesInList.Text: Getting a Moodle to behave like a "moodle farm" should be possible, by modifying config.php. I didn't try this: if it breaks, you get to keep both pieces. Normal precautions apply (backup, don't test on your production site, etc.). Drupal has a generic way of doing this, could be some inspiration for you: have a look at http://cvs.drupal.org/viewvc.py/drupal/drupal/includes/bootstrap.inc?annotate=1.206.2.2&pathrev=DRUPAL-6#l192 I would create a config.SUBDOMAIN.php for each of your site, and modify config.php to load the right one based on the URL . My tests here seems to indicate a problem with themes and with https logins... so this is not a one-liner. Obviously, you still need one data directory per site, and when upgrading the files, you still need to run the upgrade procedure on each site too. Running only one code base saves disc space and make upgrades a bit faster, but you need to run the same version on all sites, all the time. As disc space is cheap, it might be easier to write a few shell scripts to make it faster to upgrade each installation separately than making Moodle run out of a single codebase.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: multiple schools on a single mooodle install?
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm using a single codebase for nearly 600 moodle installs and use this idea. Each school has a separate config.php file which is chosen based on the domain name served. This config file points them to their own data directory and seperate database etc. It works perfectly. The limitations of this are: * No one line-hacks can be done on a per-school basis * No modules can be installed on a per-school basis * Themes available for one school are visible for all schools Two out of three of those limitations are advantages for us as upgrading and supporting 600 moodles is difficult enough as it is without code-disparity. And there is a solution to the theme problem! Variables exist to specify a custom theme directory, see $CFG->themedir and $CFG->themewww [ Docs: Theme Directory Guide ]. I did a presentation at the last UK moot large-scale vhosting, the slides are available online and might contain more pointers than my current jetlagged explanations!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Multiple accounts with same username
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle does not support the user scheme you mention. The base assumption in Moodle is that every different users has unique username and email. You could try creating custom authentication plugin which could permit the login using the same username and different passwords and behind the curtain create different user accounts. This would also mean that you can not store username and email in the standard profile fields but instead use custom profile fields for this. For example let us assume you have username foo and email foo@foo.com this is how the user table would look for 2 different accounts: User table username email login username login email foo1 foo1@foo.com foo foo@foo.com foo2 foo2@foo.com foo foo@foo.com So when user enters username and password you need to check against login username custom profile field and password to determine which one user is in question etc. You should also use email provider that behaves like gmail where everything after + is ignored so you can effectively have different emails pointing to the same address (foo@foo.com, foo+1@foo.com etc.)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Multiple accounts with same username
ResponsesInList.Text: ummm Russell, what you are describing seems to be somewhat --um--um -- dark sidish... Moodle does not treat users in that way. Basically what happens is: At the Front Page you have no role, per se, until you log in. After Login, you have the default Front Page Role usually "Authenticated User" [however, I use the derived Role of "Staff" for staff members, which only has the ability to view hidden files different from "Authenticated User"] These are the only Roles I assign at the Front Page - except obviously, Admins. Manager and Course Creator Roles are assigned only at Category Level. No overlap between Categories. Teacher and Student Roles are only assigned at Course Level. Simple as that. This is a fundamental in Moodle, so would not be difficult to change, but more likely impossible without an almost complete rewrite. Besides, a User can be an Authenticated User anywhere in the Moodle, but a Student, in one course, while a Teacher in another course, and Yes, I have done that in one organization I was working for. Worked in that instance, unlikely to do it again though. While this system may seem a little outdated I would offer that it is probably the most secure approach, even if it does mean calculating permissions at every page. The least desirable thing I would suggest is that to reassign usernames as an alias is creating a circumstance where the trolling of the database will slow things down so much that it becomes untenable. Adding a non-alphanumeric character, the @, is just going to add to the congestion I would think. Recalculating permissions plus reestablishing the alias credential is not, for me, workable.

The BCU branch has some minor changes for our needs, e.g. we have a consistent javascript banner accross all of our sites instead of using the moodle header etc. The problem is, I do all of my work in feature branches, that are then merged down to master and to the BCU branch. However, ocassionally the BCU branch looses it's custom changes. What's a better way of managing this? ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Git issues
ResponsesInList.Text:
What you are doing sounds sensible, except for the " occasionally the BCU branch looses it's custom changes". The trouble is, that is too vague to know what is going wrong. You need to get more exact in formation. On what occasions did the changes 'disappear'? Obviously they won't disappear on their own. Something must have caused that, so what were the last few commands executed in that git repo before they 'disappeared'? So, really, this comes down to carefully tracking whether the difference between the master and the bcu branches are what you expect at all times. I suggest you get into the habit of regularly running git diff master bcu , (or possibly git diff --stat master bcu ). One other thing. How are you doing the " feature branches, that are then merged down to master and to the BCU branch" bit. I would probably do it like this: 
```text
$ git status
On branch feature7, working directory is clean.
$ git checkout master
$ git cherry-pick feature7
$ git branch -D feature7
$ git checkout bcu
$ git merge master
```

ResponsesInList.Title: Behat + hidden elements
ResponsesInList.Text: One scenario that has hit me a number of times in writing behat tests is hidden elements on the page getting matched before the visible element I was expecting to click on. For example, in Totara (and apologies if you're not familiar with Totara, but the example should be fairly clear anyway), there is an 'assign position' dialogue. The following tests succeed (assuming you've already navigated to the correct page): And I click on "Assign position" And I click on "Position 1"  (in the pop-up dialogue that appears) And I press "Close" This also works: And I click on "Assign organisation" And I click on "Organisation 1"  (in the pop-up dialogue that appears) And I press "Close" This, however, fails: And I click on "Assign position" And I click on "Position 1"  (in the pop-up dialogue that appears) And I press "Close" And I click on "Assign organisation" And I click on "Organisation 1"  (in the pop-up dialogue that appears) And I press "Close" As the second 'I press "Close"' matches the 'Close' button in the 'Position' dialogue box, rather than the one in the 'Organisation' box. Behat then complains that the 'Close' button is not visible, rather than trying to click on the visible 'Close' button on the page. Now, as a developer, I can spend some time writing a more specific test that uses CSS selectors or xpath descriptors of the dialogue box to make sure the correct one is clicked on, but it would be a lot more straightforward to be able to assume that any visible elements will be tried before the test fails due to the element being hidden. Also, if we want more non-developers writing Behat tests, then 'And I press "Close"' is a lot more friendly than 'And I click on the "Close" "link_or_button" in the "div.somethingorother" "css_element"' (assuming there is even a suitable CSS class to match, and I don't have to start resorting to even more contortions to select it).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: mdl_files itemid relation to an activity
ResponsesInList.Text: the itemid is the field that specifies, to which activity/resource instance the file is related to No. It's actually up to your activity module how to interpret the itemid. More precisely, the `xxx_pluginfile()` function of your mod_xxx gets file area and itemid among parameters and it is supposed to decide how to handle that. So itemid helps to identify the particular file within the given file area. For example, in the Workshop module, the file area `instructauthors` does not use the itemid at all as there is only one "Instruction for authors" in the given module context. For file areas `submission_content` and `submission_attachment` the itemid is interpreted as the submission record id. But again, it's up to your module how to work with this value. Note this applies at both places - when serving the files as well as when generating the links to them. The File API docs page has some information and you may also want to study how other modules do the thing. Good luck, I personally found the file API an amazing land to be explored in the moodleverse.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: mdl_files itemid relation to an activity
ResponsesInList.Text: The answers to this question can all be found in the Moodle code, if you look through it. But, to get you started: You have not specified whether you are attempting to get the files via Moodle code, or via a database lookup. Your question implies you are trying to do something external to Moodle itself, as you are asking about database tables, so I'll explain the underlying database tables, rather than the files API (which is what you should always use if you are working inside Moodle). Files are stored within file areas (within each file area, each file has a path + filename). File areas are uniquely identified by 4 values: contextid component name file area name itemid The contextid is the id of the relevant entry in the table mdl_context. In the case of an activity module, to find this, you need to look up the moduleid in the table mdl_modules (the id of the row with name = 'resource', in this case). You then look up the cmid in the table mdl_course_modules (the id of the row with module = moduleid and instance = the id of the mdl_resource table). Once you have the cmid , you can find the contextid from the table mdl_context (the id of the row with contextlevel = 70 (CONTEXT_MODULE) and instance = cmid ). The component name is the ' frankenstyle ' name of the plugin (in this case, 'mod_resource'). The file area name is chosen by the particular plugin (in the case of the mod_resource main file area, it is 'content'; if, however, you are wanting the files stored in the description for the resource, then it would be 'intro'). The itemid is relevant when there are multiple areas which have not already been uniquely identified by the above items (e.g. a forum has multiple posts, each of which has attachments stored in a separate file area), in the case of the resource activity, the itemid is not relevant.

(From memory, the resource code may do something to the itemid to avoid browser caching, but that shouldn't be an issue here). If you're really not sure, just look at the code within mdl_resource to see how that retrieves the files - that should be a lot quicker and more accurate than asking on the forums.

ResponsesInList.Title: Activity completion "Require view" meaningless for some activities?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all, Further to this discussion in the Lesson forum: " Prerequisite Lesson vs Conditional activities ", I would like to share my view of the "Require view" condition in the "Activity completion settings" for some activities . For resources such as Book, Page or activities such as Forum, Glossary, etc. it can make sense that simply "viewing" the resource or activity can count for completion. On the other hand, for any activity that requires the student to answer questions, e.g. Quiz, Lesson, Survey, Questionnaire, etc. simply viewing the activity without participating can not , in my opinion, count for completion. Those activities can only be considered "completed" when they have been submitted . Therefore I suggest removing the case FEATURE_COMPLETION_TRACKS_VIEWS:   return true; from the mod_supports($feature) function for those activities (Quiz, Lesson, etc.) as I have done for my own case from the Questionnaire plugin. Actually, to push things a little further, it does not make much sense either for those activities to offer the choice for students to mark them manually as completed. And that option could/should be removed from the settings as well. Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Activity completion "Require view" meaningless for some activities?
ResponsesInList.Text: I disagree. I certainly see your point. But people use Moodle in all sorts of places for all sorts of purposes. Removing flexibility would have to have a better justification than "it is not what I would call completion." Imagine a scenario where a company trusts their workers to move through a series of learning tasks based on on their own assessment of whether they know the subject matter or not. Or a course which people have paid for, and it is deemed the students have a right to access all the material, albeit with a mild nudge to go through the course sequentially. (Not to mention the fact that it is a whole lot easier to peg conditions onto the "must view to complete" than to make new conditions when hacking around)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Activity completion "Require view" meaningless for some activities?
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks for your reply, Justin. I too see your point. It is not my intention to remove flexibility from the Completion feature. And of course nothing obliges a teacher to use the "View activity" as a condition for completion, I am just saying it is meaningless and therefore useless. I maintain my view that simply "viewing" an activity which asks questions to be answered without answering any of those questions can be counted as "activity completion" (*). I am waiting for strong counter-arguments. Joseph (*) The Lesson activity is a special case, as it can consist entirely of so-called "Content pages", without any questions to be answered.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Activity completion "Require view" meaningless for some activities?
ResponsesInList.Text: Is there some reason that there is no option in the Quiz Activity Completion for submitting the quiz like there is for Assignments? Being able to restrict based on submission would be very valuable to most of us, especially those who deal with asynchronous courses where students are submitting assignments and taking their quizzes at different times. Right now the only options are viewing the quiz (which is not helpful at all for us) and getting a grade (which prevents our students from going on to their next module assignment while they are waiting for a grade). We want our students to complete their assignments and quizzes in a specific order. In several of our courses, the authors are using a "quiz" as a module assignment. In this case, we cannot guarantee that the "assignment" has been submitted prior to the student going forward. We do use the "view" option in cases where we require that students read some information but are not required to actually complete or submit anything. It is one way that keeps students from saying they did not "see" the information. While there is no guarantee that they really read the information, requiring them to "view" the content before proceeding to an assignment or quiz makes it easier for us to justify that the item marked as "required reading" with a "view" restriction is something they are responsible for reading. I have attached copies of the Activity Completion options for Assignments and Quizzes for reference. I would assume that this would be a relatively easy fix since it has already been developed for assignments. It would be greatly appreciated if the options could be the same in both cases. Are there any plans for this in the future? Image 1: Quiz Activity Completion options Image 2:  Assignment Activity Completion options

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: extend sessiontimeout
ResponsesInList.Text:
Noting that it certainly can be considered a security risk (but I'll leave that up to you to determine the risk and what you/your institution are willing to accept), the way to do it is this: Edit config.php, and add the following: 
```text
$CFG->sessiontimeout = 31557600;
```
 The value above is the time in seconds that you wish the session to be alive for, my example above is 365 days - I would suggest reducing this to a much lower value in a production system. I have this set on my development workstation for the reasons you have mentioned, I prefer to never be logged out. I would definitely not suggest using this value on a production system.
