ResponsesInList.Title: Adding a variable in a serialized object
ResponsesInList.Text: During the week-end I was bored and decided to fix some of the lesson module tracker issues (Yes I know it's a strange idea !) One thing I want to do is permit teachers when they grade an essay question to have a decent editor (currently it's just a textarea) see MDL-43387 . I have not decided yet if I will add a filepicker too. The problem is that teacher comment is member of an object (it's $essayinfo->response) and that object is serialized and stored in a single field useranswer of the lesson_attempts table I don't know what is the best method to add a new member to the object ($essayinfo->responseformat) in order to store the format associated with the teacher comment in $essayinfo->response. More precisely I don't know how to handle: upgrade step (having to get all records in the table, unserialize that field add the format, serialize again and store the modified value in the table will have a huge impact on big sites) backup and restore ... other foreseeable problems... Can you give me some advices ?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Adding a variable in a serialized object
ResponsesInList.Text: I suggest that you don't try to do DB upgrade. Instead, make any code that tries to access ->responseformat first check if it is present, and if it is not add in the backwards compatible value. I can think of two ways to do that. First, if there is only one place where that data is un-serlialised, then do it when you unserialise. Otherwise, you will been to make a function call add_responseformat_if_needed($essayinfo) and call what everywhere that you try to access ->responseformat. If you do it that way, then you don't need to do anything on upgrade, or on backup/restore.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Adding a variable in a serialized object
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks Tim, It helps a lot And yes I will definitely need the add_responseformat_if_needed function given how badly structured the lesson module code is ! For instance there are 10 places where essayinfo is unserialized

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Adding a variable in a serialized object
ResponsesInList.Text: Well, if you can think briefly about refactoring, you might be able to improve thing. For example, are there also 10 places where we do the get_record call that loads the data that needs to be unserialsed? If there are fewer DB class, then move the unserialise there and you can reduce the duplication. Or, if the DB call is duplicated 10 times as well, then perhaps you can extract a better function than lesson_add_responseformat_if_needed. It could be lesson_load_XXX that does the DB query and the unserialise. (But be careful with that approach, because it makes it hard to combine DB queries for efficiency.)

ResponsesInList.Text: This topic has already been done to death on these forums, yet here we are - our monthly rant against the Events API Really, is it that much work? It shouldn't take you more than a couple of minutes as you already seem to have figured out what you need to do...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Just catching up with add_to_log() replacement - Seriously?
ResponsesInList.Text: I think the basic idea is that, if it's interesting enough to add to the Moodle logs, then there's a chance that someone will want to trigger something else when it happens. Given that, it's helpful for all 'log' entries to also be events that can be hooked in to (I have come across many situations, writing Moodle plugins , whereby hooking into an 'add_to_log' call would have been an ideal way of avoiding modifying core code or forking a 3rd-party plugin).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Just catching up with add_to_log() replacement - Seriously?
ResponsesInList.Text: Yep - I guess that's what we are being asked to buy into. "You WILL create events!!!". But... people are lazy. If it's not about getting the job done on time/budget then devs won't bother. (Almost) no specifications for third-party plugins will have "must create events" in them. Devs will just leave out the logging/events because it becomes something else to go wrong. If that's what was expected then it should have been *much* simpler so there is little effort required.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Just catching up with add_to_log() replacement - Seriously?
ResponsesInList.Text: It's not like third-party plugins already had proper logging even when it was just an add_to_log call. Hell, core Moodle doesn't have proper logging - in fact the most critical instances (the type where a member of staff has broken a website by changing some setting and you need to find out who it is so they don't break it again after it is fixed) tend to be missing. And when I'm slagging off third-party plugins above, I'm largely referring to OU internal ones that we developed. Unless somebody paid particular attention, we very often forgot to add logging, even though we have quite good compliance with code guidelines and suchlike overall. Anyhow: I don't think the new API is a particular problem for developing new code. It doesn't take long to do and it's an opportunity to think about what you need to log (for example do you want two different log events, or the same event with different parameters). Also it means the log events are properly document (i.e. look in /classes/event, you can see them all - vs look in db/log.php to find it doesn't exist or hasn't been updated and contains incorrect information anyhow). It is tedious for existing code, though. I have probably migrated more than 20 events now so I should know... Good news is that in some theoretical future when we're not all far too busy, we might be able to use the new log API to improve logging performance. I think writing log entries to database is one of the biggest bottlenecks to Moodle scalability, because it's one of the biggest causes of database writes, and db writes are really the key limit to scaling in most setups. --sam

I personally see big benefits of the new events driven model that can be used for plugins interoperability. And I already saw some plugins making use of it in very elegant way.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Just catching up with add_to_log() replacement - Seriously?
ResponsesInList.Text: I think one of the complications with the current system is that it is not suitable for plugin interoperability in general - it's basically only suitable for reacting to user actions. For general plugin communication you'd want things like being able to communicate very efficiently between plugins in a manner which is *not* logged (because it doesn't correspond to a user action and you might make hundreds of such calls in a request). So far as I know there isn't a good generic mechanism for that yet; it's MDL-44078 and related discussion. But the current system does have some good possibilities for plugins to observe log events - or would do if we had more events in useful places. For example, I have some situations where I need the system to do something after a restore finishes to fix specific details - unfortunately there isn't a 'restore complete' event yet (afaik). --sam

As I was adding events, I obviously started with the legacy ones. Then I added some extra ones here and there, where I thought they might be useful/needed. But some admin or teacher using a plugin might think differently. They might a) never use some events I decided to include or b) need to log other events which I did not envisage. Of course, for case a), it would be possible to put the list of events in the plugin settings (at site level) where an admin would then be able to decide which events in the list they want to be used. Does any core or add-on plugin does that at the moment? Case b) is not so easy or maybe just not feasible. Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Just catching up with add_to_log() replacement - Seriously?
ResponsesInList.Text: I don't think this is a good way of thinking about this. Neither admin nor teacher "use" the event. If the event has no subscribers, it is simply logged and done. If those making reports are not interested in it, they will just not include it in the report. There is no need to give up on data just because we think we will never use it. Events data are too valuable, or may be in the future. The sooner you start gathering them, the higher value your database has.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Data API Query
ResponsesInList.Text: I've seen your note that the actual query is more complex than demonstrated, so I won't suggest using get_record() instead ... I think what you're asking for is something like this: $userid = required_param('userid', PARAM_INT); // Retrieve the POSTed 'userid' param. $user = $DB->get_record_sql('SELECT * FROM {user} WHERE id = ?', array($userid), MUST_EXIST); OR (often clearer and more maintainable, if you have more than one param in the query) $userid = required_param('userid', PARAM_INT); // Retrieve the POSTed 'userid' param. $user = $DB->get_record_sql('SELECT * FROM {user} WHERE id = :userid', array('userid' => $userid), MUST_EXIST); Note the MUST_EXIST is optional, but, unless it is valid for the user record to not exist, it is a good way to stop the code immediately, before it starts trying to operate on a non-existent record.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: siteidentifier what is its general purpose
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Mark. The general purpose of that is to uniquely identify the site once and forever. The value can be used everywhere where possibly multiple Moodle instances share the same data space (caching for example) or when the site is to be registered etc. It could also be used to identify if the data is originating at the same site or not - although backup/restore and question bank export/import seem to use their own ways of this check. ResponsesInList.Title: Database server slows down because of moodle session renewals and checks
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, I made a previous post about a query that runs a couple of times every hour dealing with 'siteidentifier' slowing down the mySQL server rendering all moodle installs unable to communicate with the DB. This brings down all of our sites. We have 130+ websites that communicate with a very large my SQL database (32 cores, 128 gigs ram, 5TB storage), and our DB settings are perfect for a server of that size. It should not have any issues with handling any set of queries that are being thrown at it and most of the time things are great. However, after investigating quite a bit I noticed a 3 or 4 stage set of queries dealing with mdl_sessions. First is a request for a user lock that looks like this: <pid> <dbusername> <connection source ip> <dbname> Query <time elapsed> User lock SELECT GET_LOCK('<dbname>-mdl_-session-68804', 120) Then it will do this: <pid> <dbusername> <connection source ip> <dbname> Query <time elapsed> Opening Tables SELECT id FROM mdl_sessions WHERE sid = '<sid>'; Then this: <pid> <dbusername> <connection source ip> <dbname> Query <time elapsed> query end UPDATE mdl_sessions SET state = '0',sid = '<sid>',userid = '<uid>',timecreated = '1412669850',timemodified = '1412674008',firstip = '<user ip>',lastip = '<user ip>',sessdata = '' WHERE id='<session id pulled from previous query>' BTW , the "sessdata" this query can be like 1000-2000 lines, which is massive and I'm unsure if this is actually necessary. Anyway, these queries will take about 5 minutes to perform, where the database is flooded with these requests (hundreds of them) and then the database becomes unresponsive. These are all very slow queries. Things I've done to fix: reschedule crons to give reasonable time for completion and no overlap and ensure cronlocks are being used move intensive crons/queries to run during night instead of during business hours moved sessions handling from DB to moodledata (I thought this would help but it didn't, and it still talks to the DB for the rest of the session data even though it's no longer doing the "USER LOCK" request) Confirmed that the database settings are ok. Even after all this, it's still coming down from 02-07 after the hour and 27-32 after the hour. Any help would be appreciated. This is a beast of a problem.

ResponsesInList.Text: I'm still trying to find out the implications of adjusting this setting, but I suspect it's relatively safe. $CFG->session_update_timemodified_frequency = 20; That is the default in seconds to update the table with session update information.  If your session is 2 hours, my current understanding is the above is the amount of error you could have in session overrun if the user continues to use the system after their session is supposed to have expired.  If that is of little concern to you, you could try a figure of 300 or 600 and see what it does to the load on the server.  Depending on the timeout risk, you could bump it up to 30-45 minutes.  If a user gets to 1.5 hours, then doesn't update the session even though the user starts using it.  So the longer update time basically puts the session end window into a state of real session_timeout - session_modified_update_frequency.  Depending on your use-case you may wish to just increase the update frequency and the session timeout by the same amount.  It will only produce a small set of cases where the user would stay logged in with the longer session timeout.  If I thought harder about it, I could probably work that out.  But that's not for now. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle destroys my sessions - make it stop
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle initialises and makes use of the PHP $_SESSION variable itself, so, unless you are wanting to rewrite many major parts of Moodle, you should not be touching $_SESSION at all. Moodle does have a variable called $SESSION, which it uses to store session data. You may have some success with including the Moodle config.php file, then adding values to $SESSION, if you want to pass them on to other code you have running within Moodle itself.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Error: Database Connection Failed
ResponsesInList.Text: Know that you are using postgres ... my suggestion is for MySQL but imagine postgres has something similar.  MySQL has a default of 151 for maximum connections - the odd number (ie, the 151st connection) is reserved for only the 'superuser' to connect once there are 150 connections. Solution for me was to increase max_connections to 201. But, you might read this: http://blog.endpoint.com/2013/12/increasing-mysql-55-maxconnections-on.html Again, that's for MySQL.  Surely there is something similar for postgress. 'spirit of thinkering', Ken

After some serious online reading a few weeks back I made the following changes: Set the max_connections = 200 in the postgresql .config, and Increased the SHMMAX value to 4GB for the OS in sysctl.conf (which is 1/4 of installed memory). This was done on September 17th, 2 days before a 2 week school holiday, during which we had a power outage for about 4 days because no-one was around to reset the server room breaker after it tripped during some wild weather. Suffice to say that there has only been minimal traffic through Moodle and the problem has not recurred after being back at school for 2 days. Early stages yet - but we'll see. Fingers x'd. Any other suggestions? Thanks again. Craig.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Error: Database Connection Failed
ResponsesInList.Text: Altering SHMMAX by itself will not improve the amount of memory PostgreSQL has available to it.  You will also need to change shared_buffers to something that approaches the SHMMAX number you set.  4G for shared buffers should be sufficient and will give a significant speed boost. Connections running out can be a problem, but it's usually a symptom of slow queries.  On sites with 1000 users logged in at the same time (1000 page views a minute), Only 200-400 postgresql connections remain open.  So you will need to do more reading on PostgreSQL performance tuning and especially logging of slow queries.  If you log your slow queries you can find out if all queries are slow or just some.  If write queries are slow or commits are slow, your disk could be not performing as well as you might like.  But you need more data to be able to determine that. More shared_buffers means PostgreSQL can manage an entire query in its own memory space without asking the OS for pages, that will make it much much faster.  work_mem can be useful to increase slightly on a large server if you are getting lots of large sorts happening in queries. Hopefully that's enough to think about for today Regards Russell

"Cloud" itself is just a buzzword, and in the sense it is being applied here it is to mean an FTP storage site. If you can, could your system support its own FTP  storage system. You would have full control over every aspect of the process and the materials, and they could be made available for future reference where needed. The only issue may be that you will have to set up a repository plugin yourself. ResponsesInList.Title: Enhancement to the Scheduled Tasks API to support 'random' time values
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Everyone, In MDL-47221 i've submitted a patch I am hoping to make into Moodle 2.8 to support random syntax in the scheduled task time definition. This is so you could put : 
```text
$tasks = array(
    array(
        'classname' => 'tool_langimport\task\update_langpacks_task',
        'blocking' => 0,
        'minute' => 'R',
        'hour' => '4',
        'day' => '*',
        'month' => '*',
        'dayofweek' => '*'
    )
);
```
 And then the minute will be chosen at random at install time. The point of this feature is so that you can create scheduled tasks which will not all run at the exact same time across different installs - its useful to stop overloading web-services. I intentionally restricted this syntax to time values, because I don't think it makes too much sense elsewhere (and also is tricky to compute :D). I'd appreciate any comments/support/criticism of this patch on here or the issue! cheers, Dan

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Problem with javascript-static.js
ResponsesInList.Text: Try clearing your cache. The path is changed for this static file to improve cacheability. javascript.php ensures that various headers are set to try and ensure that the browser caches the file, and is designed such that subsequent calls for the same file where the browser provides a Last-Modified header just result in a 304 not changed. javascript.php also minifies the files on the fly. The timestamp is to ensure that when you upgrade Moodle, the timestamp is reset, thus changing the URL , and a browser will re-request a different file. If you clear your cache, this will remove the existing server cache of the minified file, reset the timestamp in the URL, and this should mean that you get the file served. Most likely, something has caused the cache to be incorrect somehow - this may happen if your storage is flaky for example, or something odd happened the first time the file was requested and a dodgy copy was stored. This shouldn't happen, so if know the cause, it may be worth raising an issue so that we can prevent similar things happening again. Andrew

ResponsesInList.Title: Assignment assignsubmission_mahara plugin
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, Ruslan Kabalin has updated the old Assignment (2.2) subtype for Mahara to a new Assignment (2.3+) submission plugin (assignsubmission_mahara). I'm just taking over the plugin from him to finish it off now and pondering how best to handle page locking. The way that this plugin works, when a user submits their Page (formerly View) to Moodle, that page must be locked in Mahara to prevent any further changes to the Page prior to (or during) marking. There are two options for how we can do this, and I'd appreciate some feedback on how users would expect this to work. In writing this up, I'm already rubber-ducking and making my mind up, but I'd appreciate some user feedback too. One way would be to Lock the Mahara Page as soon as it is submitted to Moodle. The Page is released when a different Mahara page is selected and the assignment resubmitted. We could also theoretically allow the user to release the Page in the Moodle submission screen by some other mechanism to allow them to make changes to that Page before the submission date (unsubmitting their work essentially). The other way of handling the page locking would be to only lock the Mahara Page when the assignment submission is locked in Moodle. When an administrator unlocks the assignment submission, the page is unlocked in Mahara. We would prevent any marking of the page until it has been locked in Moodle. Ideally a task would run to lock all pages in Moodle (and thus Mahara) at the submission deadline. In talking this through, I feel that the first option is the 'best' and most appropriate option, but would appreciate some validation of my thoughts. My feeling is that Locking of assignment submissions in Moodle is the wrong approach to take and is really intended for different purposes. Additionally, I'm just wondering what should happen to that page once the assignment has been marked. My gut feeling is that it should not be released... ever - imagine the scenario where the Page is used as evidence and sent to an external examiner at a later date. It therefore must not be modified in any way between being marked initially, and then subsequently marked by the external examiner. Again, I'd appreciate any views others may have in this regard. For those familiar with Mahara, you will of course be aware that even when a Page has been locked, some of it's content can still be changed as it is essentially just a view of other content. As a result, content such as Blog Posts which are displayed within the Page can still be edited, so this is not foolproof. Thank you in advance for any thoughts and suggestions, Andrew Nicols

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Assignment assignsubmission_mahara plugin
ResponsesInList.Text: I've been discussing this Ruslan and others a little more and it appears that my rubber ducking does not necessarily agree with theirs. I thought I'd add some more of the background to my reasoning here: As it stands, whilst we can lock the pages in Mahara when an tutor in Moodle locks that assignment submission, there is currently no way to automatically lock the page in mahara when the deadline for the assignment in moodle passes. We cannot rely on cron as there is no guarantee on the timeliness or frequency of cron and therefore we could get into a situation where users are able to edit their pages after they have been submitted, and after the deadline but before marking/locking has taken place. I'm also concerned that the model for this breaks somewhat if users are able to submit a page, and yet still make changes. If users are not 100% aware that this is the case, they could submit a page to Moodle but it not be locked, and then continue making changes (or even delete that page) without realising that their changes do indeed affect their submission. We've seen similar usability issues with the 'Submit for grading' button whereby users upload their work, Save their changes, but do not Submit for grading. They assume that because they have uploaded their content, Moodle will do the right thing at the right time. My concern is that users could make the same assumption here - that their page has been snapshotted in it's current state and therefore that they can make any changes they like to it for another purpose. Cheers, Andrew

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Assignment assignsubmission_mahara plugin
ResponsesInList.Text: To elaborate a bit, my suggestion is: 1. When the student submits their Page, within Mahara we create a non-editable, non-deletable copy of the page (using basically the same mechanism as the existing "Copy a Page" button). We'll call this a "Snapshot". 2. We send the URL for that Snapshot to Moodle. I discussed some of the implementation complexities in this later comment: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=231356#p1006613 I think the best thing about this solution is that it solves the perennial problem of people not wanting to "lose" their original Page by getting it permanently locked when they submit it to an assignment. Also, by creating a "Snapshot" API, we'd be laying the groundwork for my dream of adding a Page versioning system to Mahara. In this scenario, there would be no such thing as a "draft" submission, really. However a student could potentially go in to the assignment and change their submission to a different Snapshot. There is also nothing we need to do on the Mahara side when the submission deadline happens. Cheers, Aaron

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Assignment assignsubmission_mahara plugin
ResponsesInList.Text: Just would like to clarify how updated version works at the moment. If user is required to click submit button to declare submission is final (defined in assignment settings): On final submission, the submitted Page will be locked in Mahara and submission editing will not be possible in Moodle. To make an edit, teacher should release submission to draft. This sounds reasonable and it works the same way for any submission type (file or onlinetext). If user is NOT required to click submit button to declare submission is final (defined in assignment settings): On submission, the submitted Page will not be locked in Mahara and submission editing will be possible in Moodle. The reasoning here is simple - since submission editing is possible in Moodle why it should be locked in Mahara? To actually grade submission that has not been declared as final, teacher should Lock it in Moodle (select "prevent further changes" for single submission or lock them all), this will result in locking submissions in Mahara as well.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Assignment assignsubmission_mahara plugin
ResponsesInList.Text: I think Aaron's approach is the best, in fact that is what I thought was going to happen. I would wager we are one of the biggest users of Mahara assignment submission in Moodle and have been speaking with Kristina Hoeppner about funding development work on this. For us assignment submission to Moodle is one of the most important features, but it has never worked as it should. What I have never seen are any use cases for this feature which I think would be useful. There are a couple that cause us problems: 1) Students incorrectly submitting assignments. This happens where there are multiple assignments and relating Mahara pages in a single Moodle space. It is not uncommon for students to "mis match" the Mahara pages with the assignments and subsequently re-submit the correct ones. In this instance the first submission is never graded and remains locked. Sumbission as final / draft or any other complexities are irrelevant. We are talking about human error. If a student believes they are submitting the correct assignment they will (do) follow the entire process through to locking. 2) We have a number of cases where students on work placement (6-12 months) are asked to maintain a journal / work diary in Mahara and submit it for weeky / bi weekly review by the lecturer. These form part of the assessment and are a good way for lecturers to maintain contact with the student. Currently this just does not work. Students need to maintain access to their pages / journals as they are "living documents". Lecturers on the other hand want to see measurable weekly updates and progress. Lecturers also want to be able to leave feedback in the Mahara comments. 3) Moodle 2.5 allows for assignment re-submission, I am not sure what the impact of this would be? Another point is in the past we have had issues with "inheritance" in locking, for example embedded blog / journal posts were not locked with the page and could be edited by proxy. It seems to me that locking of new Mahara features will always be an afterthought and every new content type added to Mahara would need more code adding to the "Mahoodle" interface. Also I do not think some of the above comments take account of the way lecturers work, or the fact that most do not have the time nor the inclination to get into the complexities of such a system, in my opinion processes: "If user is required to click submit button to declare submission is final (defined in assignment settings)" "If user is NOT required to click submit button to declare submission is final (defined in assignment settings)" It is too much to expect each and every lecturer to understand the implications of this in Mahara. It is a huge task to keep everyone up to date with core Moodle features, trying to get the implications of Mahara locking / unlocking across to them just wont work. There can be large gaps between training lectures and them actually coming to use the system and most lecturers / teachers are not technically minded, and why should they be! "To actually grade submission that has not been declared as final, teacher should Lock it in Moodle (select "prevent further changes" for single submission or lock them all), this will result in locking submissions in Mahara as well" Again, way too complex. Lecturers already have a process for this, it is the assignment deadline set in Moodle . That should be all they need to do. Often lecturers do not get round to grading for some time. They teach, they also have many assignments submitted on different courses in the same couple of weeks. They are sometimes off sick, attending conferences, on holiday / vacation etc. Also consider we are (in our case) talking about formal assessment of degree courses where there are strict rules regarding deadlines that need to be adhered to. The idea that the process becomes reliant on this kind of manual intervention is a very bad idea. Lecturers and Students regularly make mistakes (as we all do). We should be designing a process that is as resilient to human error as possible, one that requires a minimal amount of training / knowledge / understanding to use successfully. Another point is that the process of "archiving" is complex and expensive, but according to this process is only made use of in a tiny minority of cases, whilst in parallel we continue trying to work with an increasingly complex set of rules for locking / unlocking which has been nothing but trouble since its inception. My suggestion is that you stop trying to fix an already over complex and problematic process with additional layers of complexity take a serious look at Aaron's suggestion of using the "snapshot", and perhaps try and gather some more use cases. Finally, I am sorry if this sounds overly critical particularly where I have taken and responded to quotes or complained about the existing process, I am just trying to make these points as clearly as I can but am aware this may seem blunt. We are all very grateful for the great work you guys do! Regards, Jez

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Assignment assignsubmission_mahara plugin
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jez, "Snapshots" of any sort have their own complexities to deal with too, unfortunately. First, you have to decide what you mean by "snapshot". In my comment, I was thinking of it as a variant on the same functionality as when you click the "Copy a page" button. In other words, we'd make a new in-Mahara copy of the page, maybe with some metadata that says which Page it was copied from and when, and we'd permanently lock that "snapshot" copy. The alternative definition of "snapshot", which is more resource intensive and is probably the one that was referred to as being done in batches, would be to export a LEAP2A (or flat HTML) archive of the Page, and store that somewhere, perhaps in Moodle. This idea has some advantages, the main one being that it's more permanent. Even if your Mahara site goes away, you'll still have that archive file to compare with the grade. On the downside, not all types of artefacts work great when run through the archive/dearchive process. With my in-Mahara "snapshot" page copies, I think the main complexities you run up against are: 1. It still relies on locking, so you still have the "Locking inheritance" issues you mentioned. You could work around this in a couple of ways. First off, you'd want to make actual copies of all the artefacts rather than just link to the originals. Second, you could just disable all editing on Pages that are earmarked as a "snapshot" (though potentially it could be trickier to block editing of the Pages' artefacts). 2. Since these snapshots are permanent and can't be deleted, there's the potential for some storage bloat issues. But maybe you could let admins manually delete individual Snapshot pages. 3. Feedback comments on the snapshot page. If the teacher roams over into the page from Moodle, should they see a comment/feedback thread for the snapshot page itself? Or should they see the comment/feedback thread for the original page? Or should they see a frozen snapshot of the original page's feedback thread? 4. There would also be some UI fiddliness about coming up with ways for people to see and manage their snapshots. Like, should they show up on the list of "Your pages"? How do you display snapshots of pages where the source page has since been deleted? Do you put a notice at the top of the Snapshot page linking back to its source page? Can you set separate permissions for snapshots than for their source page? etc. 5. And there may be some further complications once you get into the idea of Collection snapshots. Although... in principle I think you could just make one by taking a snapshot of each of its component Pages. Cheers, Aaron

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Assignment assignsubmission_mahara plugin
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Aaron, Yes I am sure its a tricky process. I was referring to a "Mahara Export Procedure" described in a Catalyst document titled "Solution Design for Mahara and Moodle Integration" (June 2013) which said: "A submitted page or collection will be archived under certain conditions, e.g. when an institution using Moodle decides to use the LTI assignment and / or when page submissions to groups are made and the archiving setting has been activated. The Mahara export process needs to be able to archive submitted pages / collections after the tutor / teacher finishes grading either in Moodle or in a group that allows submissions." If that process were implemented, then could the archive not be taken at the point of submission rather than the point of grading / release? If so then the pages / collections could immediately be released back to the student. Regards your points above: 1) Artifacts / file access would be an issue, probably the biggest hurdle. 2) When Kristina described this process to me (prior to me seeing the document) the concept of "retention periods" was mentioned so that files would clear down after a given period of time. 3) I envisaged feedback being left on the live copy not the snapshot. The purpose of locking / taking snapshots is to enforce an assignment deadline. Staff have a number of ways to give feedback, I think most use Moodle assignment feedback but in the case of ongoing weekly journals they like to leave feedback on the Mahara pages / journal entries. 4) I would imagine those issues would come under the scope of the project to develop these features (again referring to the Catalyst document I saw). I don't know how well this process would work / how reliable it would be. The document I saw has concepts for admin screens showing "failed exports" etc. I do think it is worthy of further consideration though, especially as development of these features already seems to have been planned. Again, if this process is implemented and does work, why not take the snapshot on submission as opposed to grading? Regards, Jez

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Assignment assignsubmission_mahara plugin
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jez, Just to be clear, I wasn't trying to say that we shouldn't go the Mahara-page-copy "snapshot" route. I just wanted to define what I meant when I used the term "snapshot" in my forum post here, as well as try to use the wisdom of the community to figure out the best answers to some of the questions it poses. My idea of using in-Mahara copies of the Page as the "snapshots" is different from what is in the Solution Design document you referred to. It's actually an idea I had relatively recently while I was discussing this issue with Kristina. So, this would sort of be an alternative to that document. I'll confess to not being super familiar with the contents of that Solution Design, as it was written by one of my colleagues, not me. I think it boils down to: 1) replace mnet with LTI for web services (which is purely a back-end change not directly visible to users) 2) create a Leap2A archive of each submitted Page, and hold on to that as a permanent backup of the submission. In all other ways, it remains the same as the old Mahara assignment plugin, including the idea that it would lock the user's submitted Mahara page, and that the teacher would look at the locked, original, Page. I believe it's item #2 there which would include the "failed exports" and "retention periods" you were talking about. This would also be the bit you mentioned, that can't be done in realtime, because creating leap2a exports is resource-intensive. Indeed, that seems to be the part the document goes into the most detail about. I do think adding a file export of each submission, as a permanent record even if the Mahara instance goes away, is probably a good idea. I've heard from institutions that need a permanent audit record like that. Although, for the teacher who is grading the submission, they're going to want to be able to view the Page easily, in something like its original form, and so my idea of creating a copy of the page in Mahara is a good answer to that, I think. Cheers, Aaron

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Getting Record from database
ResponsesInList.Text: If that code's going to be running on a Moodle site, then you should use the $DB API, instead of mysql_query. See any DB access within Moodle for examples, or read the documentation online at: https://docs.moodle.org/dev/Data_manipulation_API However, in this case, you really should use get_fast_modinfo($courseid) to get the information. e.g. $modinfo = get_fast_modinfo($courseid); $modnames = $modinfo->get_used_module_names(); (I'm assuming get_used_module_names is the function you want, as your original query appears to be retrieving a list of all the activities used in the course).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Getting Record from database
ResponsesInList.Text:
If you wish to extract associative array you can do it using $DB->get_records_sql_menu($sql, array $params=null, $limitfrom=0, $limitnum=0) function. You need to declare global $DB variable before running the command. 
```text
$sql=' SELECT mdl_activitysetmodule.course as course, mdl_modules.id as id, mdl_modules.name as name
FROM mdl_course_modules, mdl_modules, mdl_course, mdl_activitysetmodule
WHERE mdl_activitysetmodule.course = mdl_course_modules.course
AND mdl_activitysetmodule.course = mdl_course.id
AND mdl_course_modules.module = mdl_modules.id
AND mdl_course_modules.course = 3 ';

$query_result = $DB->get_records_sql_menu($sql);
```
 When using notation like this you should put table names in curly braces because table prefix maybe won't be mdl_ on every system. Btw did you run this query on your DB to check it?

ResponsesInList.Title: Quiz: Mystery slow/bottlenecked updates
ResponsesInList.Text:
(This is fairly development-oriented, after a bit of mulling, posted here. Could move it to quiz forum...) On a heavily loaded M2.6.x running on MariaDB 5.5.x. Bouncing between innotop's view of Locks and Queries, I see that this setup gets hit by queries following this format 
```text
UPDATE mdl_question_attempts 
    SET maxmark = 2 
WHERE 
   questionusageid IN (
        SELECT quiza.uniqueid 
        FROM mdl_quiz_attempts quiza 
        WHERE quiza.quiz = '23440') 
   AND slot = '1'
```
 these queries can take 5~10 minutes to complete. They hold on to a table-wide lock, so nobody can touch mdl_question_attempts. To make things more colorful the subselect yields an empty result set. I feel like this: To illustrate, checking for empty results like this makes the query take less than 10ms 
```text
UPDATE mdl_question_attempts 
SET maxmark = 2 
WHERE
     (   SELECT COUNT(quiza.uniqueid) 
         FROM mdl_quiz_attempts quiza 
         WHERE quiza.quiz = '23441') > 0  
    AND questionusageid IN (
        SELECT quiza.uniqueid 
        FROM mdl_quiz_attempts quiza 
        WHERE quiza.quiz = '23441') 
    AND slot = '2' ;
```
 Clearly MariaDB is being rather stupid. Following the code around, qubaids_for_quiz::__construct() has bits of the subselect, and quiz_update_question_instance() calls it thus: 
```text
    question_engine::set_max_mark_in_attempts(new qubaids_for_quiz($quiz->id),
            $slot, $grade);
```
 so I think I found the code path that leads to that SQL . However... we see a lot these updates.
Are there code paths or uses cases that run over this in a loop? All I see seems to come from the quiz edit form, which I'd say edits one quiz at a time...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Quiz: Mystery slow/bottlenecked updates
ResponsesInList.Text: In case you have not found it, the source of this query is when you go to the Edit quiz page, and change the Max mark for one of the questions in the quiz. ( https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/272fec367fba2957cb0818460c31d10d09352bca/question/engine/datalib.php#L1078 ) The particular MySQL /MariaDB stupidity that is killing us here is that these databases don't understand that there is such a thing as a non-correlated subquery, so it is probably re-evaluating (the fast and well-indexed) sub-query for every row of the very large question-attempts table. As you say: moron! We were promised a fix for this obvious query optimiser bug in MySQL 6. Don't know about the corresponding timeline for MariaDB. I am afraid this is a known issue: MDL-32616 . The short story for why this is not fixed is We know the query that is a problem. But, it is an UPDATE statement, with a subquery, and the only way to fix it would be to change to to be and UPDATE ... JOIN. Unfortunately, the SQL for that is different between all databases. So we need a $BD method $DB->update_join(...) or something, but no-one can work out the right abstraction to make that work. So it has just been sitting there (not helped by the fact the OU uses postgres , so I have not personal itch here). If you want to break the deadlock, we may have to resort to a MySQL-specific hack, like we did once before: https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/272fec367fba2957cb0818460c31d10d09352bca/question/engine/datalib.php#L932 . Obviously much better to avoid that, but if you want a quick win, that is probably the way. I don't particularly like your rewritten query. It only fixes one case (the one where the subquery returns no rows. A more typical case is that it returns one row for each attempt at the quiz, and that will still perform terribly.) Also, surely it should be EXISTS, not COUNT > 0 if you want efficiency. As I say, look at an UPDATE ... JOIN for MySQL only.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Quiz: Mystery slow/bottlenecked updates
ResponsesInList.Text:
I was thinking about this cycling in to work, but was then too busy to write it up. How about this for an API ... ... ah, while researching options, I just found the horrible mess in quiz_update_open_attempts . That is a useful case-study. ... $DB->set_field_join($table, $alias, $newfield, $newvaluesql, $joins, $wheres, $params); Example calls In the quiz_update_open_attempts example, we would have 
```text
$table:       'quiz_attempts'


$alias:       'quiza'


$newfield:    'timecheckstate'


$newvaluesql: $timecheckstatesql


$joins:       '{quiz} quiz ON quiz.id = quiza.quiz


                        JOIN ( $quizausersql ) quizauser ON quizauser.id = quiza.id'


$wheres:      $attemptselect
```
 In the query from this thread, we would have 
```text
$table:       'question_attempts'


$alias:       'qa'


$newfield:    'maxmark'
```
 Example SQL (I really don't trust the Oracle case here, and don't have a test DB.) Postgres 
```text
UPDATE {$table} $alias


SET $newfield = $newvaluesql


FROM $joins


WHERE $where
```
 MySQL 
```text
UPDATE {$table} $alias


JOIN $joins


SET $alias.$newfield = $newvaluesql


WHERE $where
```
 MSSQL 
```text
UPDATE $alias


SET $newfield = $newvaluesql


FROM {$table} $alias


JOIN $joins


WHERE $where
```
 Oracle 
```text
UPDATE {$table} $alias


SET $newfield = (


    SELECT $newvaluesql


    FROM $joins


)


WHERE $where
```

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Quiz: Mystery slow/bottlenecked updates
ResponsesInList.Text: Come on Martín, you can do better than that. If you look at the other hack I linked to: https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/272fec367fba2957cb0818460c31d10d09352bca/mod/quiz/locallib.php#L969 you will see that you can write this sort of query as a single UPDATE ... JOIN in a way that MySQL optimiser can cope with. Do that, even, if you have to do it as a special case in this code with if ( $dbfamily == 'mysql' ) { , and not as a general solution in the DB library. As for the indirection, I don't think it is complicated. There are just two components involved here: the quiz, and the question engine. They each own their own database tables, and so the quiz should not poke around directly in the question tables if there is a higher-level API provided. In order to make that work, there is a single abstraction, the qubaid_condition class, to let the quiz pass the quiz-specific bits of SQL (SELECT a list of IDs that the question engine needs). That is used throughout the question engine, when bulk operations are involved, and it works quite nicely. (Though i realise I sat that as the person who invented it, so of course I would think that.) If you cannot work it out well enough to do your own good patch, then I will do you a deal: if you write some unit tests for quiz_update_slot_maxmark , then I will code an implementation that works well in MySQL and passes your tests. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Database migration from moodle 2.6 to moodle2.7
ResponsesInList.Text: As previously - you cannot put a 2.6 database onto a system which already has 2.7 installed. 1. Create a clone of your 2.6 site on your system2 - this includes copying the moodle code, the database and the moodledata folder. You will need to edit the config.php to point at the new locations for the database and moodledata folder. Given that your previous efforts have not worked - please make sure you are doing this with a completely fresh database etc. Do NOT try to duplicate the existing database from your system1 onto an existing moodle database wich may by now be a mix up between 2.6 and 2.7. 2. Go into the new clone version and check everything is working as expected. If you have any plugins, update them. 3. Remove the 2.6 code (except the config.php) and replace with the 2.7 code 4. Go back to the site and run through the upgrade process which should start automatically. From Vivanath's question, it looks like you are doing both - migrating to a new server and upgrading. Follow the links he has given, but do them one at a time. Either migrate (clone) your site to your new server, make sure it works and then upgrade, OR upgrade in place, make sure it works and then migrate/clone. It seems like you are trying to do both processes at once.

ResponsesInList.Title: Moodle 2.6.x - Sessions _always_ stored in DB table?
ResponsesInList.Text: I am debugging performance problems in a Moodle 2.6.x site; and I see MariaDB v5.5.x with extremely high contention over several tables. One of them is mdl_sessions. We have db sessions disabled, so I go looking and I find that there is now a table to track metadata about sessions. I think I understand the intent -- GC is easier and more reliable -- but this just adds a very nasty bottleneck. There are strategies to run GC without it, doing it "out of band" (in cron, for example), sidestepping impact on creating/updating sessions. This bottleneck is unnecessary. We have a bunch of jobs that are a very bad fit for an ACID DB. Simplifying things: tables that need to be written to on every request are just a very bad match with a "real" DB, and it's been a while since we've used MyISAM. We are in the territory of ACID DBs and they just put too much effort in ensuring the ACIDity of every data manipulation. All those assurances are expensive, and they are not needed, we can mark a session is recent with much cheaper methods (touching the file for instance).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 2.6.x - Sessions _always_ stored in DB table?
ResponsesInList.Text:
From git log lib/classes/session/manager.php: 
```text
commit d79d5ac2760b7c5508aca8a7b319543ce08e1b17
Author: Petr Škoda <commits@skodak.org>
Date:   Sun Sep 8 08:38:52 2013 +0200

    
MDL-31501
 rework user session architecture

    List of changes:
     * New OOP API using PHP namespace \core\session\.
     * All handlers now update the sessions table consistently.
```
 For some "handlers" updating the sessions table is a waste of expensive resources. Some 'caches' have built-in TTLs/expire, and do their on GC. Others, such as filesystems, store created and edit timestamp efficiently for you. This makes code consistent...ly bottleneck everywhere...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 2.6.x - Sessions _always_ stored in DB table?
ResponsesInList.Text: Checkout the comments in https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-31501 you will see that you are not the only one who had issues with this implementation.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Help a Behat newbie
ResponsesInList.Text:
Selecting text by the editor id does work. I guess you're running tests with firefox in which case you'd better switch to chrome. The selenium firefox webdriver seems to have serious issues finding elements with recent versions of firefox. To run selenium with chrome you need to add to config.php something like: 
```text
$CFG->behat_config = array(


   'default' => array(


       'extensions' => array(


           'Behat\MinkExtension\Extension' => array(


               'selenium2' => array(


                   'browser' => 'chrome',


               )


           )


       )


   ),
```
 You also need to download the chrome webdriver from https://code.google.com/p/selenium/wiki/ChromeDriver Init behat for the new config to take effect. And to run selenium: 
```text
java
 -jar path-to-your-selenium-jar/selenium-
server
-standalone.jar -Dwebdriver.chrome.driver=path-to-your-driver/chromedriver.exe
```
 See https://docs.moodle.org/dev/Acceptance_testing/Browsers for some more details. As for verifying that the img is displayed, try something like: 
```text
And "//img[contains(@src, \'pluginfile.php\')]" "xpath_element" should exist in the ".some_css_class_of_a_container_element" "css_element"


And "//img[contains(@src, \'moodle_logo.jpg\')]" "xpath_element" should exist in the ".some_css_class_of_a_container_element" "css_element"
```
 These steps verify that an img with src with pluginfile.php and the image name exists. There may be a way to use regular expression for the contained value in which case one step could do the trick. hth

ResponsesInList.Title: Mandatory Description Fields, can they be made non-mandatory?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all, we're running Moodle 2.6.4, just wondered whether anyone has ever thought of or carried out, making the description field in resources and activities non-mandatory? It is an annoyance for users, and often gets bypassed with Drag/drop of file and folder resources anyway. would it be a setting in all the activity mods or an overarching config setting somewhere? Many thanks,

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Mandatory Description Fields, can they be made non-mandatory?
ResponsesInList.Text: Nope. You have to live with it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Mandatory Description Fields, can they be made non-mandatory?
ResponsesInList.Text: If you go to the global settings page for any given activity/resource type, then there should be an option to make the description field optional. This doesn't apply to 'assignment' activities, as an assignment should always have a description, otherwise students won't know what they're supposed to be submitting.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Mandatory Description Fields, can they be made non-mandatory?
ResponsesInList.Text: Yes, that assignment descriptions must be required seems to be a common misconception (our teachers are certainly annoyed by the required field). For some years now I've been carrying on a local "hack" to Moodle Core that makes the assignment intro field optional.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Mandatory Description Fields, can they be made non-mandatory?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Chris-yes - what Davo says about going to each item's settings page, for example Site administration>Plugins>Activity modules>Page It's such an oft-requested thing that I included it in a "Moodle tip" post a while ago which might be useful to you: 3 Teacher time-saver tips in Moodle .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Something a little odd in the /course/lib.php file....

ResponsesInList.Title: Controlling standard pages layout from theme

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Controlling standard pages layout from theme
ResponsesInList.Text: Once you're familiar with the constraints of a theme just customising it via CSS, you then are probably going to step up and create a custom theme yourself. This is where you can specify more layout internals than CSS can provide. You probably want to start by reading https://docs.moodle.org/dev/Creating_a_theme which tells you the basics of what can be changed. Essentially there's some specific folder names you have to use, and some specific files you have to have, and these tell Moodle which php pages to use for various areas in Moodle (e.g. the front page , or a course, or a report). But you really have to get in and start editing php files in order to understand what's going on. If you're using Moodle 2.7, you might like to try this: Open up your moodle folder and clone the /theme/bootstrapbase folder. Name it something you like (I'll use "adventuretime"). Open that folder Inside the lang / en folder rename theme_bootstrapbase.php to theme_adventuretime.php and open it in your php editor Change the $string['pluginname'] to have your theme name, and empty out $string['choosereadme'] for now. Save that. In the theme folder, open up version.php and change "$plugin->version" to todays day and time, as numbers (e.g. 201409162100), and change "$plugin->component" to be "theme_adventuretime" Log onto moodle as an admin and go to site admin -> notifications. It should prompt you to install the new theme, so do that. Go to site admin > appearance > themes > theme settings and make sure theme designer is ticked (so you can see your edits as you make them without having to flush caches all the time). Now you have a place to try out changes to files and css. The css files for the theme will be stored in the themes "style" folder, and the php files that "draw" the layouts will be in the "layout" folder. Say you want a radically different design for the front page. You could do this: In the "layout" folder, make a copy of the file "columns1.php" and call the new file "frontpage.php" Open up "config.php" in the theme folder Look for the line that starts with "$THEME->layouts = array( ..." and read down until you see the "frontpage" item - change 'file' => 'columns3.php' to 'file' => 'frontpage.php' and save the file. open up layouts / frontpage.php and implement the most fantastic design ever, adding styles in the style / moodle.css file as required. Other theme designers have done things like have extra columns (e.g. 5 column layouts), or over-ridden core functions that affect how things like custom menus or the catalogue search page are actually generated! It's pretty amazing how much custom control you have over moodle just through the theme. Load up themes from older versions of Moodle (e.g. 2.6) since in the latest version a large number of them were removed. There's a number of interesting tricks to be studied in themes built for older moodles. I hope this (and https://docs.moodle.org/dev/Themes ) gives you some ideas on where to go from here. welcome to the world of theming moodle!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Controlling standard pages layout from theme
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Ashish, The main page layout changes can be achieved by adding block regions.  See; https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=160466 for details on adding a block region. Regions don't need to be just on the right and left as they are in the default theme.  Open2Study for example has them on the top, right and a set of tabbed regions where you see the discussions and extra reading materials.  You can see that by viewing the source of the page and seeing where Moodle adds the region classes to the markup. Progress information must be calculated from completion data.  The basic idea is that you understand lib/completionlib.php and you can use that to work out how to calculate progress.  Using the data from completion lets you determine what's completed and what's not.  You then have the ability to calculate a progress bar. After that it's just about rendering that information into a nice progress bar. Using the single activity course_format available in 2.7 will give you a good idea how to get Moodle to direct students away from the main course display page and use a certain activity.  You just need some rules to pick where to direct students to. completion data and get_fast_modinfo() will likely be helpful. For creating a block to display navigation in a different way than normal.  You really want to understand how get_fast_modinfo() works.  That is the basis for any block that deals with the structure of a course. Regards Russell

ResponsesInList.Title: Automatic clearing of classloader cache?
ResponsesInList.Text: I was just wondering if there was any benefit in automatically resetting the classloader cache if a class is not found? I've hit a number of situations when deploying code that I have been working on, whereby (as far as I can make out) Moodle hits code that relies on the automatic class loading, before it reaches the point where an admin can login and run the upgrade process (giving a fatal error, preventing the admin from logging in to run the upgrade). This usually means a command-line upgrade (or cache purge) is needed, before the site works again. Would there be any downside to just automatically rebuilding the cached version of the classmap, at the point when a class is requested which cannot be located. As far as I understand it this would only ever happen if: The class has not already been loaded into memory via an include/require line AND the class is newly-added and not yet in the classmap cache OR the class does not exist at all in the system In the first case, rebuilding the classmap to find it would be very helpful. In the second case, you would appear to have a fairly serious bug in the code, so the performance hit of rebuilding the cache is probably the least of your worries. Or am I missing something here?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Automatic clearing of classloader cache?
ResponsesInList.Text: If we did this, I would suggest: Ensure it never did it more that once per page-load. Only did it in developer debug mode. You could try making a patch, to see how ugly or otherwise it came out.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Automatic clearing of classloader cache?
ResponsesInList.Text: Tim, to respond to your suggestions: Ensure it never did it more that once per page-load - yes a sensible precaution (even though it could never run more than twice in a page load anyway) Only did it in developer debug mode - this would probably defeat the purpose of this proposal in most of the situations where it is currently an issue. On a developer site, it is usually fairly straightforward to fix the problem anyway. On a live site, it is more tricky, if the class loading error is getting in the way of an admin reaching the upgrade / purge caches page to fix the issue. I'll put together an issue + patch and see what happens.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Automatic clearing of classloader cache?
ResponsesInList.Text: Nope, I was wrong. There's a lot of places where the classloader function is triggered by a call to 'class_exists'. Unless we're going to start messing around with using debug_backtrace to distinguish between calls generated by class instantiation and 'class_exists' calls, I can't think of an obvious way to spot the use case of 'this code really believes this class should exist, so let's try extra hard to find it, before PHP gives up and shows an error message'.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Automatic clearing of classloader cache?
ResponsesInList.Text: This would probably require setting up a global flag to *not* reset cache on miss every time class_exists() is used. I'm not sure if it's worth doing it but maybe... I've hit the same issue few times. Tomek

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Automatic clearing of classloader cache?
ResponsesInList.Text: Wrong - do not try to login before upgrade, go directly to http://yoursite.com/admin/ - the classloader and opcache is reset there automatically, all other caching is disabled there and upgrade does not need login anyway (unless you use buggy addons of course). This is nothing new, admins were always required to visit admin/index.php after any code change going back to early Moodle 1.x ...

ResponsesInList.Text: On reflection, this last post of mine was a silly post.  Did not move us forward. Detail: Here below is a grid I have used for a number of years when teaching about online interaction in the context of reflection, forums and even in class F2F activities .  My premise is that reflection is hard, often not intuitive (Students are NOT naturally metacognitive) but reflection can be learned to some extent.  (Include critical thinking etc etc) TRUST is involved.   "Am I safe?" So communication and activities are needed in all quadrants. Lets say you are having a discussion online.  LIKE is a quick public feedback. Lets say you have a "Required post".  This should be deeper, and is public. Lets say you have a semi private journal.  Maybe you, your three group members and the tutor. etc You stuff things up if you force too deep an interaction when students are not ready. etc Sometimes it is helpful to consider these activities as to how they start, finish in terms of pubic-ness or not.  (etc)  Obviously they slide around the page.  But how and when they slide can be an intentional learning pathway to help the student. Student<>Tutor interaction In the process of all this, it is often helpful to add in a personal Student to Tutor interaction.  If course you an use email.  But something inside Moodle will add another tool to the toolkit of the tutor. I am aware of the dangers. Care of use, technical, ethics, idiots using it  etc.  My worry was that this could be implemented in a silly way.  Partly the UI question.  Which was Micheal's concern, and he is right.  And the problem also is that if we make it idiot proof, the universe then decides to make an improved version of 'idiot'. My argument FOR your request. I'ts also an argument for several other forum enhancements. Like/Me to button Subscribe at the thread level Ability for tutor to push a notification to all students regardless of forum subscriptions Edit in place Two pane page (doc on the left, forum on the right) -Derek

ResponsesInList.Text: Your server connects to Moodle.org directly (not via your browser) to collect the plugin, when you install that way. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: PayPal users can't re-enroll in course.
ResponsesInList.Text: If you need users to enroll themselves again you would need to unenroll them first from that course. Of course that also removes any user information from the course itself (grades etc.). To do that you can configure "Enrolment expiration action" in the PayPal settings page and set it to "Unenroll user from course". That way they could reenrole again. If you need to keep user information always than you need to hire somebody to make you a custom version of paypal plugin that does not have this limitation. (You can also sumbit a feature request to the Moodle tracker but I doubt anybody will act on it.)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can't get contextid only for some users!?
ResponsesInList.Text:
It probably doesn't make any difference, but it's not a good idea to use $mysqli directly in Moodle code, a much better way to write this would be: $users = $DB->get_records('user', array('deleted' => 0), 'id', 'id, auth, deleted'); foreach ($users as $user) { $context = context_user::instance($user, IGNORE_MISSING); echo "{$user->id} {$context->id} {$user->auth} {$user->deleted}
"; } The next thing to check would be a query like this: $contextrecord = $DB->get_record('context', array('contextlevel' => CONTEXT_USER, 'instanceid' => 895); var_dump($contextrecord); (Or you could just look this up directly in the database, using Adminer or PHPMyAdmin - CONTEXT_USER has the value '30'). The strange thing is that the internal code for context_user::instance will automatically create a context record for the user, as long as the 'mdl_user' record exists. Maybe you could also try purging your site caches, (Site admin > Development > Purge all caches), just in case there is bad data stored in there (although, I think the contexts are only cached in a static variable, so should not persist over different web calls).

ResponsesInList.Title: Database Write Error Using DML
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all, I'm in the process of developing a plugin that will index courses, topics, and modules for a Google Search Appliance (GSA) XML feed (one that I eventually hope to feed back to the community, once I've gotten everything ironed out). However, I am having some challenges. To use a GSA feed in the most efficient manner, the manual suggests using an incremental feed that only submits data that has changed since the last feed. Doing this will also cut down on overhead, since items that haven't been updated won't be sent. After a bit of research, I determined that the most efficient way to keep track of this information is by building my own database table, and then referencing that database table with each crawl to determine what has and hasn't changed. I'm currently having some difficulty, though. All of the documentation I've read on using the Moodle DML to read from and write to the database suggests that when inserting a record or updating a record, the only field that is absolutely necessary is 'id', such that: $record->id=0 //or some integer: So, for each course, topic, and module, I am using the unique ID that the database employs (so $cm->id, $topic->id, or $get_fast_modinfo->get_course()->id). However, when it gets down to the method: insert_record_raw(), the id of the object is somehow set to 0. So naturally, when trying to insert another record (as the script has to do), it tries to insert where id = 0, and since the record is already defined, it hits an error. I'm also including the script below that I've used to create the databases, to see if it's a configuration issue. $table_gsa_module = new xmldb_table('gsa_module'); $table_gsa_topic = new xmldb_table('gsa_topic'); $table_gsa_course = new xmldb_table('gsa_course'); //Defining our fields. $field_id = new xmldb_field('id',XMLDB_TYPE_INTEGER,'10',null,XMLDB_NOTNULL,null,'0',null); $field_name = new xmldb_field('name',XMLDB_TYPE_TEXT,'255',null,XMLDB_NOTNULL,null,null,null); $field_audience = new xmldb_field('audience',XMLDB_TYPE_TEXT,'64',null,XMLDB_NOTNULL,null,null,null); $field_url = new xmldb_field('url',XMLDB_TYPE_TEXT,'255',null,XMLDB_NOTNULL,null,null,null); $field_updated = new xmldb_field('updated',XMLDB_TYPE_INTEGER,'10',null,XMLDB_NOTNULL,null,'0',null); $field_courseid = new xmldb_field('courseid',XMLDB_TYPE_INTEGER,'10',null,XMLDB_NOTNULL,null,'1',null); $field_content = new xmldb_field('content',XMLDB_TYPE_TEXT,'2048',null,XMLDB_NOTNULL,null,null,null); //Defining our key (we only care about sorting the DB by id, since it is used universally). $key = new xmldb_key('primary','primary','id'); $key->set_attributes(XMLDB_KEY_UNIQUE, array('id')); //Defining our indices. We're using ID and courseid to make searching by those //fields easier. $index_courseid = new xmldb_index('courseid'); $index_courseid->set_attributes(XMLDB_INDEX_NOTUNIQUE,array('courseid')); $index_updated = new xmldb_index('updated'); $index_updated->set_attributes(XMLDB_INDEX_NOTUNIQUE,array('updated')); //Only add the fields, keys, and indices to the table if the table doesn't //already exist in the DB. $table->addField($field_id); $table->addField($field_name); $table->addField($field_audience); $table->addField($field_url); $table->addField($field_updated); $table->addField($field_courseid); $table->addField($field_content); $table->addKey($key); $table->addIndex($index_courseid); $table->addIndex($index_updated); //And then write the table to the DB. $dbman->create_table($table); I'm trying to insert a record using $DB->insert_record() with the following object: $record = new stdClass; $record->id = (int) //some number; $record->name= (string) //shortname; $record->audience= (string) //the most-visible cohort - used for security purposes; $record->url= (string) //Moodle URL ; $record->updated= (int) //last updated timestamp; $record->courseid= (int) //id of the containing course; $record->content= (string) //some descriptive string of what the course, topic, or module contains; So, does anyone have any ideas as to what I could be doing wrong?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Database Write Error Using DML
ResponsesInList.Text: So for those curious, I figured the problem out. $DB->insert_record() assumes that you want the system to handle the ID field. It actually winds up dropping the ID field entirely and passing the rest of the object, with some cleaning, to $DB->insert_record_raw(). $DB->insert_record_raw(), on the other hand, is the function to use when you want to define the ID yourself. Since I switched over to the insert_record_raw() method, I've had tremendous success.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Database Write Error Using DML
ResponsesInList.Text: You have reached the wrong conclusion. When you create your DB table, you must create the id column as an INT(10) AUTOINCREMENT. Then insert_records works. (You don't set $obj->id before calling insert_records.) You should use XMLDB to generate the install.xml file and the necessary upgrade code, and it will do this for you.

ResponsesInList.Title: Course completion: "activities to be completed" not as stated, inconsistent
ResponsesInList.Text: This is a bug fix / improvement that I think should be done, and I can do it (very easily), but it's a change from how part of Moodle used to work.  Therefore I wanted to get some feedback on how to make the adjustment with minimal surprise to any users who may be relying on the old behavior.  Maybe we put a setting somewhere.  Some users think the new / corrected behavior is what one would expect, so no setting is needed - just make it do what it says it does. Activities can have four possible completion states: INCOMPLETE:           The student has not completed the activity. COMPLETE_PASSED The student has not completed the activity. Also, the student achieved a passing grade on the activity. COMPLETE_FAILED (optional) The student has not completed the activity. Also, the student had a failing grade on the activity. COMPLETE_COMPLETED The activity has been completed. No passing grade was set. For most (all?) activities, the user can choose to not allow COMPLETE_FAILED by requiring a passing grade in order to mark it complete (ie quiz) or requiring a specific grade (ie scorm ). So complete_failed is generally optional - the user can choose settings to only allow completion if it's passed. Within "conditional activities", criteria work as the language indicates: requiring an activity to be completed before another is visible means it's not visible if the prerequisite is still INCOMPLETE, it becomes visible when the prerequisite is marked COMPLETE_*, when it's completed, regardless of what the grade was. In conditional activities, if you want to require that it's completed and passed, you simply either set the prerequisite to not be completed unless it's passed, or set a specific grade to be required. Course completion, on the other hand, does not work as one might expect. If a course requires that the student complete the pretest, study module, and final, it does not mark the course as complete when those three activities are marked as complete. Instead, the course will only be marked complete if the student both completes the pretest and also achieves a passing grade.  This means that in the completion report, the teacher may see that all of the required activities are marked complete, but the course isn't marked complete. I propose that course completion should work like activity completion does. "Require these activities to be complete" should mean that when those activities are marked as complete, the course is marked complete. This would be a very simple one-line fix. Note again, if a user wants the old behavior of requiring that an activity be passed in order to be considered complete, they still have that option.  I'm not suggesting anything be removed. I'm proposing that we not force / override that in the course completion aggregation code, but rather honor the setting that was set on the activities completion settings. Is anyone relying on the old behavior of course completion, of "completed" really meaning "both completed and also have a passing grade"?  Are there any suggestions for how to make this improvement without affecting users who may be relying on the old behavior?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course completion: "activities to be completed" not as stated, inconsistent
ResponsesInList.Text: There is a typo in the above. The word "not" should not appear in the description of complete_passed and complete_failed.  it should be: INCOMPLETE:           The student has not completed the activity. COMPLETE_PASSED The student has completed the activity. Also, the student achieved a passing grade on the activity. COMPLETE_FAILED (optional) The student has completed the activity. Also, the student had a failing grade on the activity. COMPLETE_COMPLETED The activity has been completed. No passing grade was set. A tracker issue for this now exists here: https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-47232

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: HTMLPurifier to all input fields
ResponsesInList.Text: This first thing to check is if the javascript is being allowed via the 'trustcontent' capability ( https://docs.moodle.org/en/Capabilities/moodle/site:trustcontent ). This is specifically to allow trusted users to add javascript (and any other potentially unsafe content) to text areas within Moodle (see the above link for one situation in which this is desirable). It is, however, entirely possible that this is a text area that has just been missed in terms of being cleaned at all. In which case, it should be reported as a bug in Moodle tracker.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: HTMLPurifier to all input fields
ResponsesInList.Text: trustcontent is not the only mechanism. Generally speaking, anywhere in Moodle where only teachers can input content, JavaScript is allowed through on the grounds that There are useful educational things you can do using snippets of JavaScript; and you trust your teachers. It is a compromise, but a reasonable one. Of course, in Moodle there is not necessarily any such thing as a 'Teacher' becuase roles can be re-defined. On the define roles page, you will see 'risk' icons next to each capability. One of those icons is 'Risk XSS'. It is the 'Risk XSS' capabilities that let you input JavaScript.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: how to change the module instances' names
ResponsesInList.Text: You need to call the Moodle function rebuild_course_cache(). This can be done for a single course (rebuild_course_cache($courseid)) or for all courses on the site (leave out the courseid parameter). Alternatively, for Moodle 2.5 (or below), you can clear the 'modinfo' and 'sectioncache' fields in mdl_course. For Moodle 2.6 (or above), you could try purging all caches (site admin > developer > purge all caches).

ResponsesInList.Title: Changes to course caching in 2.6 - get_fast_modinfo() and friends
ResponsesInList.Text: In 2.6 course modinfo cache is moved to MUC. This change: significantly reduces size of table 'course' increases performance, especially in DB operations very difficult to hit race conditions resulting with corrupt course cache course cache is purged together with other caches (for example on 'purge all caches' actions). This is the "Epic" issue for this change: MDL-34397 , it gives more details on what's going on. It is currently in integration and hopefully will be available for playing/testing very soon. Along with those changes class course_modinfo, cm_info and section_info were changed to NOT extend stdClass, have read-only properties and calculate conditional availability on demand only. This may require some changes to 3rd party plugins that used to be naughty and added extra properties to the instances of those classes. Comments are welcome.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Changes to course caching in 2.6 - get_fast_modinfo() and friends
ResponsesInList.Text: When you say that this change "increases performance", what evidence do you have for that statement? What measurements have you done? I would be particularly interested to hear about the tests you have done with large numbers of concurrent users in multi-web- server set-ups, with shared DB and shared cache back-ends.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Changes to course caching in 2.6 - get_fast_modinfo() and friends
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Tim, we will post the results of testing here. Increase in performance is not extremely significant. We can't do magic - there is still the same amount of information that is stored/retrieved, it has just changed the location. Also the "less DB queries" is a result of changes in classes cm_info and section_info (as I said above, they don't retrieve anymore data they don't need) rather than result of changing in caching. I would also expect that the performance may potentially go down if the environment is such when DB queries are faster than queries to filesystem. But this is the advantage of MUC - admin can choose which store to use for cache to make it the most efficient.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Changes to course caching in 2.6 - get_fast_modinfo() and friends
ResponsesInList.Text: This is what scares me. MUC was introduced to 'potentially' improve performance, but as we found in Moodle 2.4, it actually made things slower until people outside Moodle HQ fixed it. And now you continue to convert more of Moodle to rely on MUC before you are in a position to take meaningful measurements of the effects of your work. That is not engineering. (I know David Monllao is working on such testing and measuring). We had all better hope that your guesswork is right.
