ResponsesInList.Title: Installing Moodle on Subdomain
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi All, So, I know how to install moodle on a subdomain ( http://moodle.domain.com ), but I want to know how to install without using "moodle" in the destination URL . Is this possible? For example, see the University of Florida Moodle - http://online.education.ufl.edu/ Basically, I want to use the Moodle LMS but I don't want it in the URL. Any advice or tips is greatly appreciated. Thanks.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Installing Moodle on Subdomain
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Christopher, I'm by no means an expert at this but I think you need to configure the web server ( Apache 2?) httpd.conf file to point the URL, online.education.ufl.edu at the Moodle root directory, /home/ufl/public_html/ufl/education/moodle, or you can change the document root to /home/ufl/public_html/moodle and change the server directory to correspond to it if you wish. When the changes have taken (restart the web server, e.g. Apache), you can install Moodle from a web browser by going to online.education.ufl.edu or if you're changing an existing installation, just edit the /moodle/config.php file to match the new URL. Remember to make sure that the URLs, directories, and httpd.conf file match up. 
```text
</VirtualHost>

<VirtualHost *:80>
DocumentRoot /home/ufl/public_html/ufl/education/moodle
ServerName online.education.ufl.edu

# Other directives here

</VirtualHost>
```
 or 
```text
</VirtualHost>

<VirtualHost *:80>
DocumentRoot /home/ufl/public_html/moodle
ServerName online.education.ufl.edu

# Other directives here

</VirtualHost>
```
 I hope this helps!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to use get_user_field_value
ResponsesInList.Text: If you want the username for the current user, then it is $USER->username. get_user_field_value is for use with custom profile fields. If that is what you are trying to retrieve, then you need to get the relevant record from mdl_user_field_info - it would probably be worth looking at all the usage examples given in xref to see how to do this (and this only makes sense if you're doing something with the grades API, as that is where the function you pointed to exists).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to use get_user_field_value
ResponsesInList.Text: My code needs to be able to retrieve the username for a user id in the mdl_user table (I'm not writing it as a pure moodle plugin, just using moodle's login features and keeping my own separate database tables - mdl_user id field is the only link). Is there a different function I should be using? The title suggests it's the best fit...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to use get_user_field_value
ResponsesInList.Text: $username = $DB->get_field('user', 'username', array('id' => $userid)); // Just retrieve the username field. OR $user = $DB->get_record('user', array('id' => $userid)); // This loads the whole user record. $username = $user->username; As I mentioned in the original reply, 'get_user_field_values' is for retrieving custom profile fields (called 'user fields' in the database backend). If you have used the admin interface within Moodle to add custom fields to the user profile, then you could use this function to retrieve them (but again, it is part of the gradebook API, so I wouldn't suggest it was the best function to use). If you have not added custom profile fields or are not trying to retrieve them, just get the data directly from the user table.

(That conditional email feature is just a small add-on to the main functionality of this report, but it is useful for monitoring some things.) block_workflow : We use this at the OU to manage the production of courses. The main functionality is to track who is working on the site at a given time, and what they should do. However, it has the ability to execute some simple scripted actions when one person finishes one task, and the next person starts the next task. For example email the next person to tell them, or change an activity setting like automatically hiding or unhiding the activity. http://docs.moodle.org/26/en/The_OU_workflow_system#Automatic_script_actions http://docs.moodle.org/dev/Event_Monitor_specification : This is something that Moodle HQ is working on for Moodle 2.8. Automatically end out a message when certain conditions are met. I would not be surpirsed if either Remote Learner ELIS or MoodleRooms Joule had something in this area. It might also be worth looking at Moodle's web services. They provide a fairly 'safe' API into Moodle. Anyway, it would be great to see some sort of plugin to automate Moodle administration using a real scripting language like LUA. Certainly worth trying to make a proof of concept if you can.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Complex conditional rules
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Phil, Thanks for telling us about that scripting language which I'd never heard of before. Putting on my " grammar nazi " hat, may I point out that it should be spelled Lua, not LUA. From the Lua site: What's in a name? "Lua" (pronounced LOO-ah) means "Moon" in Portuguese. As such, it is neither an acronym nor an abbreviation, but a noun. More specifically, "Lua" is a name, the name of the Earth's moon and the name of the language. Like most names, it should be written in lower case with an initial capital, that is, "Lua". Please do not write it as "LUA", which is both ugly and confusing, because then it becomes an acronym with different meanings for different people. So, please, write "Lua" right! ATB, Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: moodle_database::update_record_raw() no fields found.
ResponsesInList.Text: The easiest way to fix this would be to step through the code in a debugger (xdebug + PHPStorm is my preference, but the free netbeans IDE also works with xdebug). If that's not an option, then try doing a 'print_object()' call on the params you are passing into 'update_record', then add some echo/print_object statements to see what happens to the values as they go through the 'update_record' function. On the other hand, you may want to consider using a custom profile field, instead of modifying the 'user' table, as that is likely to cause you all sorts of upgrade problems in the future ...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: moodle_database::update_record_raw() no fields found.
ResponsesInList.Text: What Davo says (I use xdebug and Eclipse), but you may also want to enable debugging on the site (Site administration - Development - Debugging).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: moodle_database::update_record_raw() no fields found.
ResponsesInList.Text: I know this is old, but I ran into a similar problem, and the key to the problem is  "  adding new fields to a table" To fix this, you would run "purge cache"  (Site Administration -> Development -> purge all caches) on your server,   one thing that will do, is re-create the cache of the fields in all database tables. the function update_records, has this code - public function update_record($table, $dataobject, $bulk=false) { $dataobject = (array)$dataobject; $columns = $this->get_columns($table); $cleaned = array(); Note that it gets the columns for the table, if it doesn't find the columns that you passed in as array elements, it will strip them.        A purge cache will re-create that cache.  I think in general this doesn't happen often, as most people don't add columns that often to tables. Steve

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to set cron function sequence?
ResponsesInList.Text: At present you can't do this. The order that "plugin" cron scripts is run is defined in code by Moodle at present (this may change in 2.8!!) So ALL block cron scripts are run before the course completion. Have a look at the the cronlib.php file there should be a run_cron() function which does all the sequencing. What you could do is try to find a type of plugin that has its cron run after the completion cron and implement your cron script as that type of plugin...but I'm not sure there is a type that runs after (off the top of my head). Michael

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to set cron function sequence?
ResponsesInList.Text: Sorry the function is called "cron_run()" not "run_cron" And it looks like this has changed between 2.6 and 2.7, so it'll depend on what you're targetting, but it's still time based so you can't force it to be after the course completion.

ResponsesInList.Title: Proposed change of mdl_user_preferences.value to TEXT
ResponsesInList.Text: See MDL-46739 . Other similar columns like mdl_config.value and mdl_config_plugins.value are TEXT, so it is surprising that this column is different, and that suprise has lead to bugs in the past (see linked issues of that tracker issue). Obviously a TEXT column will be fractionally slower than a VARCHAR on some databases, but I don't think it will be significant. (User preferences for the current user are cached in the session.) Anyway, just though I ought to publicise that proposed change. Comments welcome.

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi everyone!  I've been making SQL reports and cannot for the life of me make one that has a list of courses, their assignments, and the assignment due dates all by category. Can anyone help? Thanks for your time!  Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: [MYSQL Query]  Need Course, Assignment, and Assignment Due Date
ResponsesInList.Text: Can you provide a wireframe of your report grid with all the fields displayed?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: [MYSQL Query]  Need Course, Assignment, and Assignment Due Date
ResponsesInList.Text:
Something like this should get you started: 
```text
select mc.shortname "course_shortname", mcc.name "category" , ma.name "assignment_name", ma.duedate "assignment_duedate"
from m_course mc
join m_course_categories mcc on mcc.id = mc.category
join m_course_modules mcm on mc.id = mcm.course
join m_modules mm on mm.id = mcm.module
join m_assign ma on mcm.instance = ma.id
```
 That's from our PostgreSQL database but the SQL used is fairly generic so should work in MySQL too. Also update the m_ to mdl_ if that's what prefix you're using. Add more where clauses, group by's etc to suit as needed.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: redirect
ResponsesInList.Text: No. This is not really a Moodle, or even a PHP question. This is about HTTP. What these methods do is to send a 302 redirect temporary response, with a Location header. Web browsers receive that, and do a GET request of the URL in the Location header. The only way to get a post is to do something with JavaScript (like LTI does).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Provincial field on sign-up form
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Spencer - You really don't want to modify core Moodle code files if you don't have to. That just makes your installation difficult to maintain. You can add extra profile fields to users from the Moodle UI itself. From the "Admin" menu, go to "Users" / "Accounts" / "User profile fields". ResponsesInList.Title: What does Rebuild Course Cache do?
ResponsesInList.Text: I am working on a project where i have populated the moodle tables externally with the help of java programs.  Then i have to rebuild the course caches for the changes to be reflected on moodle. But i want to know what actually happens when i rebuild the course caches ? I have used a plugin -( https://moodle.org/plugins/pluginversion.php?id=2400 ) available on github to do so.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What does Rebuild Course Cache do?
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hello Pushkar. First of all, since 2.6 course cache is moved from course table to MUC and is automatically purged on "purge all caches". This is probably why this plugin is no longer needed. Course modinfo cache contains: the list of sections and modules in the course, some of their attributes including 'name' (this is especially important since it is stored in different db table). Also it contains availability conditions. Also each module can implement callback xxx_get_coursemodule_info() to specify what else should be cached. Course modinfo cache exists on application level so it does not contain any user-specific information, it is calculated on request (such as $cm->uservisible, etc.). Course modinfo cache was introduced initially to make as few as possible queries on course view page to increase performance. Now we try to use it more often in other situations, for example, on /my/ page for multiple courses, etc. In the past there were cases when course modinfo cache became corrupted as a result of simultaneous actions of two users (usually if one user edits and another views). MDL-36789 introduced additional cache validation that would re-build cache in some extremely dangerous corruption cases. Again, since 2.6 there is more proper cache validation (it required additional DB field which was impossible in stable versions bug fix). The meta issue for all 2.6 changes is MDL-41436 To retrieve course cache call: 
```text
$modinfo = get_fast_modinfo($courseorid);
```

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Custom user fields for Module
ResponsesInList.Text: If you are wanting to use the existing custom profile fields system within Moodle, instead of storing user data in a new table, then it is fairly straightforward to add them. Create a file db/install.php, within your plugin, with a function xmldb_mod_MYPLUGIN_install() and inside that use $DB->insert_record to add a suitable entry into the user_info_field table (it's fairly obvious what to do, if you look at the table structure). You can then retrieve the data you want by linking together the user_info_field and user_info_data tables (using the fieldid and userid fields). If your plugin is already installed, you can add an upgrade step in upgrade.php to add the user fields instead (or you can just ask the end user to create them manually, but automatic creation is much better!).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Running two Moodle on one database
ResponsesInList.Text: You need to have different prefixes for every moodle that is acessible by one person at the same time from the same address. For example, if you have two or more moodles on the same server , or two moodles on different servers. There has, AFAIK , been no formal convention, but the general rule has been that a prefix should be unique to every Moodle, an impossibility, I am sure you would agree if you are using two or three letters and/or numbers. What I have done on my test server where I run up to four Moodles, is to use the first three letters the site name. That is OK as long as I never have two Moodles that use the same three letters in their site name. If you use the same prefix, then you will be automatically logged out of the first Moodle you logged in to by the cookie of the second Moodle you logged in to. I often have my main employer's Moodle open, Moode.org, and one or two of my test sites as well as one or the other of the private sites I support. This is OK most of the time, but would be impossible if they used the same prefix.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Running two Moodle on one database
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Colin, From what I can ascertain from the OP , he has two moodle installs which are both using the same database, but without using different database prefixes. This would mean (if this is indeed how the two installs are setup!) that there was one user table in the database being accessed by both moodles. Each time a new course was made in one moodle, it would also exist in the second moodle; as there would only be one course table... and so on... I can not see when this would ever be a setup that someone would really want, and by the sounds of it, this is not the setup the OP has. He states that users who access from URL 1 can not login if they visit URL 2. If this is the case then there must be two user tables, one for each URL; and therefore two databases... In terms of the major difficulties I was hinting at, consider this: one database with two moodles using a different database prefix (in essence two databases!) but sharing the same moodledata folder. How does the database distinguish which files belong to which Moodle? This is perhaps less of an issue with the Moodle 2 data directory but would have resulted in course files being shared in incorrect courses using the Moodle 1.9 data directory method... Anyway, none of this really helps the OP, and unless Alan can provide a little more detail to how he has his two Moodles set up, I think we will continue to struggle to help! I would hazard a guess taht what we are looking at here is a need to migrate users from one Moodle to another a perhaps backup and restore courses from one to another too. Jon

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Running two Moodle on one database
ResponsesInList.Text: We have run a Moodle 2 cluster with automatic failover for 2 years. Theoretically you could use this technique to synchronize two servers in two buildings, but out of the box one is the master-server and one is the slave-server that is synchronized all the time. But you want to synchronize in both directions... so maybe you need three servers: the master server and two slaves you synchronize from the master-server so that the two slaves are acting only as front-end servers to the backend-master-server (in this scenario the back-end-server could only host the sql-database and the two front-ends only apache and Moodle-Php-Code). I guess MNet is still the out of the box solution here. And if bandwidth is the problem, you could synchronize only during night idle time. Our two servers were in the same room and on a fast network. Maybe they were even connected through a dedicated cable for failover-clusters but we lost a lot of performance. Rosario

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: duplicating a module
ResponsesInList.Text: Whenever I do this, I make the following changes: rename the main directory (/mod/oldname => /mod/newname) rename the language file (/mod/newname/lang/en/oldname.php => /mod/newname/lang/en/newname.php) search and replace all references to the original name throughout the code (preserving the original case, to make the comments read a bit better). This step can be more difficult if the module name is also used in other contexts, e.g. with the ' URL ' module, you need to be careful to not rename all 'moodle_url' references. Tweak the version.php file to reference today's date (optional). Step 3 should manage to fix the names of the database tables, plus all references to them. Theoretically, you might be able to get away without renaming some of the functions. However, most functions in /mod/newname/lib.php must match the name of the module, otherwise Moodle won't be able to find the function it needs to call. Also, you should assume that (at the very least) the lib.php, version.php and settings.php files for all modules will sometimes be in memory at the same time, so any functions with the same names in those files will cause problems. In practice, this means that using your IDE's 'search and replace in multiple files' function is the best way to proceed.

ResponsesInList.Title: JSmol issues with Moodle JavaScript
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi folks I'm looking for some guidance/answers to issues I'm encountering getting JSmol, the JavaScript version of Jmol (for interactive display of 3D chemical structures) to work nicely with Moodle (via the Jmol/JSmol filter). In the filter, the Jmol/JSmol libraries as wrapped-up as a YUI module and loaded into the page header using: 
```text
$page->requires->js_module ();
```
 and individual instances of JSmol, generated by the filter, are called within a 
```text
Y.on('load', function () {});
```
 See latest master version of the Jmol/JSmol filter on GitHub In general, this works nicely in Moodle (2.6, 2.7 alpha) in both normal or page edit mode. If MathJax (JavaScript rendering of equations, particularly useful in a chemical context when extended with mhchem ) is used as well, a collision between MathJax and JSmol is avoided by further wrapping the JSmol instances in a 
```text
 MathJax.Hub.Queue(function () {};
```
 This delays JSmol display until after MathJax has finished rendering any equations on the page. So far so good However, I have recently noticed couple of issues with some other Moodle JavaScript/ AJAX functions. 1. If a JSmol instance is displayed, I can no longer dock a Block. I only recently noticed this as I usually use a Bootstrap-based theme that doesn't use Block-docking anyway. Firebug reports: TypeError: M.core.dock.loader.delegationEvents[n].detach is not a function linking to: http://path/to/moodle/theme/yui_combo?rollup/~1/mcore-min.js. 2. With Glossary auto-linking enabled on the same page as JSmol, if I select a glossary link the popup displays "alert" as the title, and the sole text is "confirm" (rather than the glossary entry). I have tried a few things, without success, and am really at a loss as to how to further debug and fix this. Any JavaScript gurus with advice/suggestions? Thanks Further background information links JSmol JavaScript compatibility Jmol/JSmol Filter in Plugins directory

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: JSmol issues with Moodle JavaScript
ResponsesInList.Text:
I can try and take a look at this when I have some spare time, but it looks like JSMol does some incredibly nasty stuff. From reading their front page , it looks like JSMol is really JMol passed through a bastardised version java2javascript. Amongst other things: standard JavaScript classes that have been extended by Java2Script to be compatible with java .lang classes of the same name: 
```text
Array Boolean Character Date Error Number String
```
 Because they're always a valid reason for modifying core data types... So for starters that could get unpleasant. They also note: Note that Java2Script had to be extensively augmented to work with Jmol. Therefore JSmol will be incompatible with other Java2Script applications using the default implementations of Clazz. Which doesn't inspire me with confidence either. Looking at your plugin, it also looks like you're using JSMol.min.js, which includes jQuery. JSMol also ships with version which does not ship it's own jQuery (JSMol.min.nojq.js) which you should probably use instead - if you re-include jQuery on the page, then things tend to get unhappy and broken. Moodle now includes a way of including jQuery and jQuery plugins once, and once only so you may wish to look into these too, though I don't think that they will help in this case. Without breaking out the debugger, I'm not sure off the top of my head why other code on the page will be broken. I can only imagine that something is breaking the initialisation of the other code somehow - perhaps something to do with those data type changes. The code you've pulled out is called once in the dock loader - we loop through the elements of an array which was only just set up, and detach the events on it. The array is created using = [] rather than new Array so it shouldn't be affected by the changes I mentioned above. However, something in the event delegation code *could* be using named data types. Andrew

ResponsesInList.Title: A faster means to backup a course
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi everyone, Its project week here at HQ and one of the things I've chosen to quickly look at is speeding up the backup user interface so that you don't need to step through several stages in order to produce a backup..
I've opened a new issue MDL-46481 to do this and have put a solution up for peer-review.
The solution I am purposing adds a quick backup button to the first backup screen and collapses the backup settings on that screen by default.
When you click the button the backup gets immediately created using the system default settings. If this is something that interests you please let me/us know, vote on the issue etc etc to ensure it gets in. Many thanks Sam

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: A faster means to backup a course
ResponsesInList.Text: I would vote for it too. But as I started commenting here https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=263587 the whole thing could later be put into a major context : Moodle admins (and teachers) need facilities to revert back in case they delete a little portion out of their courses, the whole courses, categories or a whole tree of nested categories, etc. to avoid restoring and reverting back the whole system. In old Moodle 1.9 days course-backups could help recover atomic data (whole courses or parts of it on a testserver or on the production server where you would have restored the course backup-file from tape). But as Moodle 2 file system is much more complex and data is becoming bigger and bigger, course-backup-files might not be the good solution in the future. We need other facilities, complementary procedures. Not to be confused with the overall system backup, the one you need in case of a whole system loss. In the best case and long term development, sort of do-and-undo history could be integrated in the courses and on the whole Moodle system. The do-and-undo history should be available to all teachers/managers/siteAdmins of a course. The do-and-undo history of the whole Moodle system should be available only to site-Admins. In a compromise and short term development, every "destructive" action inside a course, i.e. changing any bit in it should trigger a course-backup on the fly. No do-and-undo history for the moment, but sort of snapshots BEFORE teachers modify anything. This would be session-based, so as not to trigger more than one backup of the course even if a teacher modifies/edits several sections / activities /resources during one session. If teachers log out and come back to the course for modifications, another backup is triggered. In a long term solution, nothing should be deleted from the database , only marked as deleted, so as to be able to implement a do-and-undo history. With that the need to create big course-file-backups should disappear, except to export and import Moodle course files on other systems. Maybe instead of a zip-file a tar-file or any other solution might be better, including a very rudimentary directory-tree containing all the uploaded files of a course along with Moodle's xml -file describing the course contents and links to the files. The only difference being that nothing gets zipped as zipping big multimedia-files does not make sense anyway. The siteAdmin would then set up a retention-time for such "deleted" items as I can do it on my mail-server. "deleted" items could be transferred to a trash-database and files belonging to those items could go into the trashDir, from where everything could be "revived", moved into the production database again, without disrupting anything. And, on the other side, could be safely hard-deleted after the retention period. Again, this is meant to give facilities on high load servers with lots of courses, data and teachers in which case the server admin has no chance of rewinding back the whole system if a teacher loses a bit in his course. Rosario

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: A faster means to backup a course

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: A faster means to backup a course
ResponsesInList.Text: Although an "undo" command could be quite useful, I don't think that automatic backups as you describe would be a good interim measure.  The two major issues which spring to mind would be: It'd use a lot of disk space very quickly, as you'd need to retain more than one backup for each course to keep sufficient "undo levels"; I know that "disk space is cheap", but especially on Moodles with large courses, storage usage would balloon - which IT departments in some places may not be happy with / may not allow to happen It'd be slow.  If you prevented the user from making changes until the backup completed, nobody would ever update their courses for fear of having to wait for the backup to complete first; if you didn't hold them back, they'd be able to make changes before the backup had been generated - which could result in inconsistencies and/or the changes being included in the backup That said, with the proposed "quick backup" feature, if a teacher is worried that some major change they're wanting to make might break something, they can fire off a "quick backup" before they start (and then hopefully remove it when they're satisfied that they didn't break anything).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: A faster means to backup a course
ResponsesInList.Text: I fully agree, course-versioning or course-snapshots, you may call it as you like. I like the idea, but the technical solution will be hard to realize. And you are right, course-backups are not the long term solution anyway with >5000 courses and > 1 or 2 TB data.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: A faster means to backup a course
ResponsesInList.Text: <Edit>Of course we must take in consideration that new virtualization technologies like WMware ESX are offering new compelling possibilities. ResponsesInList.Title: Need of overriding time() function?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I'm struggling upon time() php native function, timezones and Moodle. Our local timezone is UTC+2 and we set up Moodle according with this. The matter concerns the time() php native function which is used by the system to compare dates (course ending date, self-enrolment start and ending dates and so on..). For example: I set up the enrolment ending date tomorrow at 00:00. This date/time will be compared to time() in order to keep the enrolment open or to close it. Unfortunately time() native function will return, in the comparison, the "today 22:00 / 10pm" date. Due that, the comparison will fail because of timezones difference and will give 2 hours offset. We're thinking about overriding native time() function in order to use our timezone. Thanks for helping.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Need of overriding time() function?
ResponsesInList.Text: That doesn't sound like the right solution, all the forms built in to Moodle should automatically convert the user-specified time into a server -timezone time, which is then saved into the database . The timestamp should also be automatically re-converted back into the user's timezone if it needs displaying anywhere. So, if your user timezone is UTC+2, then a time specified as midnight in your timezone, will be converted to match the server's timezone giving 10pm in server time (assuming the server is running UTC). This will end the enrolment at 10pm server time, which would still be midnight in the local time (and any user with their timezone set to UTC+2 would see the time displayed as midnight, anywhere the time was output). If this is not working, then you need to check what time the server is set to and what timezone the users are set to and, if necessary, debug the timezone handling in the place where it is going wrong (if there is only one place where it is broken).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Git and moodle code
ResponsesInList.Text: Are you trying to fix a core bug, propose a new feature for Moodle, or create a plugin to share with others? If it's one of the first two, then you should make sure that this has been reported via tracker.moodle.org, before you start preparing a fix. You should then: take a fork of the Moodle current code (most people do this in github) pull this to your local computer create a new branch (named after the issue number of the tracker issue) commit your fix to that branch push the branch back to github post a link in the tracker issue for your patch. Alternatively, just prepare a patch file (off the very latest Moodle development code, in the 'master' branch) and post it onto the tracker issue. If it is a plugin, then (ideally) create a github (or similar) repo with just the plugin code (not the rest of Moodle), then go to the plugins database and add it as a new contribution (you can either upload a zip file there, or pull directly from the github repo).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Git and moodle code
ResponsesInList.Text: New features are only added to the latest development version of Moodle (that would be Moodle 2.8, at the current moment). Bug fixes can be submitted for all supported versions (2.6, 2.7, at the moment) - if it is a security issue, it can be submitted for one version further back (2.5, 2.6, 2.7) - for full details, see http://docs.moodle.org/dev/Releases (which lists the end of support dates for all versions). What you are proposing sounds like an 'improvement' rather than a 'bug fix'. However, it may be better as part of the discussion going on about rewriting the gradebook for Moodle 2.8 ( http://docs.moodle.org/dev/Grader_report_2014 ). Listen in to the general developer meeting ( http://docs.moodle.org/dev/Developer_meeting_July_2014 ) for more info about this.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Git and moodle code
ResponsesInList.Text: why not create pull requests on github that reference the issue in the tracker so they can be merged automatically? That is the way version/branch/patch management works best usually.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Git and moodle code
ResponsesInList.Text: Because the main Moodle git repository is not hosted on github - so pulling in to the github clone of the Moodle repository wouldn't get the code into Moodle core. Plus the github clone is a copy of the development repo, not the integration repo - patches submitted via tracker are peer reviewed, then put forward to integration by a component lead, then given an integration review, before being pulled into the integration repo; there they are tested and, all being well, added into the development repo and cloned back to the github repo. See http://docs.moodle.org/dev/Process for more details. Github pull requests are great for smaller projects, but don't cover all the review steps required by the current Moodle patch process.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Git and moodle code
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi David, As Davo suggests, we request that you do not create pull requests on github, and pull requests opened on github will be closed with a comment to open an issue in the tracker - they will not be merged automatically. From my own experience, the github pull request system isn't that great - especially when you're working on anything resembling a midscale to large project. I use it for several projects and it is far from clear or understandable, additionally it is not suited to multi-user systems (it's not possible to submit a patch against an existing issue without being the owner of that issue or being an administrator, and using the API for example), and it is not suited to projects with more than one stable branch (it doesn't handle merging to multiple places clearly). I use GitHub on some small projects (e.g. my own Moodle plugins ), and am a contributor on the YUI library. In both situations I find it largely unsuitable. The bugtracker is also not great. You'll find that most Moodle developers do use Github, but then paste the URLs into the tracker. You'll also find an increasing number of Moodle developers using the MDK toolset that one of our HQ developers wrote and maintains. Best wishes, Andrew

There is a way to target divs using javascript to modify the contents. I'm not sure whether any javascript created in your HTML block code would work correctly though. You could however modify your links so that instead of being regular links they have an onclick attribute. Each click would then run the piece of javascript to refresh and substitute the div contents. That might let you target the central portion but I'm not certain whether any javascript would run like that within Moodle. I changed our Moodle so that it has a graphical interface and included the javascript code into the new front page as a whole, even then it is not targeting the central portion of the screen but self created divs because I found that some of the Moodle divs are named using a dynamic yui-3 based name. Hope this is of some help to you. John Gifford

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: framename of central part of moodle page?
ResponsesInList.Text: Thank you John Gifford . I was able to target the region-main div which holds the central part of page. Here is how I did it: In <head> part I put: <script type="text/javascript"> function resizeIframe(obj) { obj.style.height = obj.contentWindow.document.body.scrollHeight + 'px'; } function url2div(url,target){ parent.document.getElementById(target).innerHTML = '<iframe style="width:100%;" scrolling="no" frameborder="0" onload="javascript:resizeIframe(this); javascript:parent.scrollTo(0,0);" src="' + url + '" />'; } </script> and I used this url2div function later in onclick attribute of my <a href...>: onclick="url2div('http://something/test.php', 'region-main')" (In my case I had to use ' instead of  those single quotes because single quotes was used in echo part of php)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: how to get a course with Moodle API
ResponsesInList.Text: Programming and learning to program the Moodle API is a steep curve. If you want to deal with courses - after having studied  the whole developer documentation - you could start with my uploadusersandcourses.php which is meant to create new courses and enroll people at the same time, either through the Web-GUI of Moodle either as nightly cron job. You may also look at everything you can find in Moodle's php directories, especially in /course/ directory Best thing is always to search for existing code, either in Moodle's php directories or in the modules & plugins database here. Sometimes you will find code examples also in these forums. Then use that existing code and modify it step by step to make it do what you want to do yourself. Starting from scratch is hardly possible. Rosario

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: how to get a course with Moodle API
ResponsesInList.Text: Then please have a look at the "useful sql queries" posts here: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=153059 Using these sql queries you can display first the data you want to collect and see in your phpMyAdmin or any other Database -Management-Tool of the database you use. Once this works, you can start to program it in php. But at this point, if you want to integrate it in the Moodle Web-GUI, you will have different options: you put your php-file in the yourMoodlePhpDir/admin and protect it with the necessary Moodle-API-functions so that only site admins can execute it. See as example search.php in that directory. In such a php-file you can use any desired HTML output and any Moodle-API-sql-query-functions you develop a block in which you can display your output you develop a special module you can place in yourMoodlePhpDir/local. See for reference my uploadusersandcourses.php and use only the header lines and all needed files to create your own module. Then insert the lines of code you need to make your query and display your output Rosario

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: how to get a course with Moodle API

Here is a crossreference site if you prefer browsing on the web instead of your own Moodle-Php-Dir: http://www.sourcexref.com/xref/moodle/nav.html?_functions/index.html (Moodle 2.4) http://xref-diff.mukudu-dev.net/moodle26 (Moodle 2.6) I still am not sure what you intend to do exactly. If you want to create a list of courses, e.g. for navigation purposes, you can use my sitenavigation block. You will find it in the modules&plugins database. It is a block to display categories and courses in nested folders. There are a lot of Admin options to set up that block. If you need navigation, you could use it as is. If you need something else, you could study the code in there and take what you need. Rosario

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Specifying the language for format_string()
Re: Specifying the language for format_string()
ResponsesInList.Text:
The following seems to work for me though I have to admit that I haven't tested it with caching yet: 
```text
// Retrieve string in French.
$currentlanguage = current_language(); // Save current language.
$SESSION->lang = 'fr'; // Set to alternate language.
$notification = format_string('notification'); // Retrieve string in alternate language.
$SESSION->lang = $currentlanguage; // Restore original language
```
 Naturally you should have the appropriate language pack installed before attempting this. Best regards, Michael Milette

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Specifying the language for format_string()
ResponsesInList.Text: Technically, that solution could end up overriding a user's default language with the course's language, for the duration of their login: 'current_language' will return the course's language as the first option, then the user's session language (selected from the drop-down at the top of the front page ), then their profile language (if the previous two were not set); writing this value back to the session language could be wrong (if the course language was set). Unfortunately, if the course language was set, this would also prevent the 'format_string' from working too, but this is probably less of an issue than accidentally switching someone to a courses language for the rest of their session ...

ResponsesInList.Title: Recommendations for Moodle core developers
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear all, The Sussex University e-learning team is passionate about education and supporting student learning through online tools. We really want Moodle to be an industry standard product that can meet the needs of educational institutions such as ours. We believe it has some way to go, but that it can yet achieve its goals. These are our recommendation s for Moodle HQ: 1. You don't need more PHP developers you need more designers 2. Follow the Market leaders of social media 3. Focus on Moodle core functionality 4. Consider Moodle courses as a bespoke textbook 5. Navigation needs to be clear and clean 6. Stop the proliferation of configuration variables 7. Moodle course administration needs to be improved 8. Make it easy to make content 9. Have notifications 10. Create a Moodle Lite For an explanation of these suggestions please visit our blog . Please leave comments on it or discuss below. Best wishes, Paolo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Recommendations for Moodle core developers
ResponsesInList.Text:
Thanks for sharing Paolo. I agree with many of the points you made. However... Re: " 4. Consider Moodle courses as a bespoke textbook At all levels of education, teachers refer to textbooks. The strength
of systems like Moodle is that the non-technical teachers can create
their own online textbooks, specifically for the curriculum they intend
to cover. Textbooks usually include activities to complete at the end of the
chapter. In VLEs like Moodle, the activities they set can be varied,
social and dynamic - more so than activities in a traditional textbook." And following on from Joseph's comment, "No. Online teaching and learning is much more than a textbook." I've read and heard many curriculum development theorists and practitioners warn against the "text book" approach, e.g. Barbara Gross-Davis. My personal reasoning is that it constrains curriculum developers and teachers to a particular approach to learning and teaching, which is the tradtional view of "knowledge transmission", AKA "present->practise->produce". To me, this represents a particularly narrow view of learning and teaching theory and practice. Moodle is founded on a social constructivist view of learning and teaching (See: http://docs.moodle.org/26/en/Pedagogy ) which makes a sharp departure from the traditional view and is based on alternative theories of developmental psychology (Vygotsky, Piaget, Bruner, et al). Declaring that an LMS should be more like a bespoke text book, encourages us to exclude and marginalise/or learning and teaching practices that are adaptive, emergentist, complex, socially oriented, self-directed, learner-centred, etc. (See: Malguzzi, Knowles, Schon, Gibbs, Brookfield, et al). A greatly simplified abstract explanation of this would be to say that, based on learners' backgrounds, previous learning experiences, and needs, curricula are co-created by (all) the course participants, as a course progresses, towards broadly defined learning outcomes in relation to central/core/essential questions of the discipline/subject matter. In order for this to happen, the power relationships between teachers/curriculum developers and learners (and administration) have to change. Academics, who are professional researchers and not necessarily professional teachers, are often required to teach and may or may not be well informed in learning and teaching theory and practice (or be particularly happy about having to teach). The way that status, positions, and salaries are awarded in academia also reinforces a certain degree of indifference to teaching. Faculty who are interested enough to dedicate sufficient time and effort to develop broader, more informed views of learning and teaching, in my experience (across a number of universities in a range of countries), are in a small minority (They do it for personal interest alone since there's little or no recognition or status awarded for such efforts). The research I read and the conferences I attend appear to support this view. There are exceptions and maybe mainstream views are changing, and hopefully Moodle's core philosophy is helping to change that and inspiring more institutions to embrace more coherent efforts towards developing their teachers and teaching, e.g. http://research.moodle.net/mod/data/view.php?id=1 So yes, you can create online text books with Moodle if you wish, but this isn't it's primary philosophical goal, as far as I understand Martin Dougiamas' intentions.

I just came back from 4 days of (climate change) activism training and the facilitation technique used is more like the social constructionist approach. Nearly everything were activities. They taught us a bit then with that little knowledge we did an activity and we kept on building on top of that and practising everything. We did brainstorming (mindmaps, popcorn, lists, etc), pair-sharing, role-playing, etc, and energisers to stay at the optimum learning mindset. This type of learning can be moved online but it can be hard to facilitate activities when everyone is not online at once and trust can be hard to establish when you cannot see people. The company I work for are creating 'text book' resources for students to use and the classes are more to actively learn the material then for the teacher to say what is in the book. For us Moodle is to be used as a delivery system for the resources. Hopefully in the future when we finalise the resources and classes, then we can make Moodle more of an active learning experience. But at the moment it is just a text book

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Recommendations for Moodle core developers
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Derek, Yes, the difference between cultivating social presence (i.e. getting learners to perceive each other as human beings that they can trust and learn from) in face-to-face vs. online contexts isn't as great as many people seem to think. However, I'd say that effectively implementing social constructivist oriented methods and cultivating the (pre-requisite?) climate of collaborative learning among cohorts of learners in both face-to-face and online contexts is far from easy. It takes a lot of awareness and skills that even professional teachers aren't usually trained in or necessarily develop in their careers. Everyone knows and understands "spray and pray" teaching (love that expression BTW ) but far fewer are as well versed in collaborative learning and the underlying principles that make the difference between mixed and mediocre results vs. consistent success in terms of learning outcomes. I think it makes little difference if courses are online or face-to-face, at least in higher and adult education. In other words, teachers need to know what they're doing and why.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Recommendations for Moodle core developers
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, Paolo. Thanks for your suggestions and opinions. I found your blog interesting reading and I encourage you to continue investigating, experimenting and contributing results to the community. First let me start by saying that, while Moodle HQ has a leading role, your suggestions should be referred to the whole community. As an HQ employee don't say that to dodge blame, but to state that if change is needed, the community has to drive it there. I thought it was worth, for my own benenfit, reflecting on each of your suggestions, so here I go. 1. You don't need more PHP developers you need more designers We have a quite a few designers in the community now, and I think the recent changes to Moodle, moodle.org and other community sites show that. I would also like to see more input from user interface and accessibility experts. See my post about the shift from a feature focus to an interface focus. We always need more developers; there's no escaping that. 2. Follow the Market leaders of social media There's good ideas in social media sites. Some of those are influencing Moodle's interface (eg Bootstrap). I do think there still needs to be a distinction between the functions of Moodle and activities that are primarily social, though there is some overlap. 3. Focus on Moodle core functionality Moodle is a system that has to work within an educational "ecosystem". Withdrawing into itself won't help education progress. In saying that, we have been making hard decisions that have removed some plugins from the standard distribution so that we can focus on the more important bits. I suggest you look into " technical debt ". 4. Consider Moodle courses as a bespoke textbook I don't see why you can't achieve this, if that is what you want. I personally prefer a mix of chunked learning and activity in courses I teach. 5. Navigation needs to be clear and clean People are experimenting with navigation right now, with a focus on responsive design and use on different devices. One hope is to do away with the navigation block altogether. I do like your point about the default number of sections . It reminds me of Parkinson's law. Would one section be enough to demonstrate to new users that they could add more sections? That sounds like a good UI investigation question. 6. Stop the proliferation of configuration variables There is a tendency among developers to offer every possible configuration option they can think of. There is also a lot of suggestions from users on more options still. I think the challenge is expose the essential options and bury the other options. Recent form improvements have worked towards this. 7. Moodle course administration needs to be improved Your dashboard sounds interesting. If there ways to get rid of the Administration block, that would be embraced, I would say. There is still a need for contextual administration at various levels, including at above and below the course level. 8. Make it easy to make content Your policy of course layout is not a bad one. I'd been interested to see evidence that this approach works better than alternatives. I have seen policies that have been almost the opposite to yours, with content on the course page being very simple and underlying activities/resources being the target for richness. It's good to know that Moodle can achieve both ends of the spectrum and the space in between. What I'm more interested in at this stage are the generation of content and the implementation of curricula in new ways. Imagine a block that allows you to drag activities/resources onto a course page in a sort of "course designer" mode. How about a map that allows you to create pathways through a course, with transitions controlled by activity restrictions, with additional alternatives offered to students who didn't "get it" the first time. We need to move towards tools that take education to places it hasn't been able to go before. 9. Have notifications The new events framework is in place and people are starting to capitalise on that functionality. Proactive prompting of students, teachers and decision makers is now possible. One project underway currently is a system that notifies users when certain events occur with a certain frequency in a specified time window. For example, when discussion on a forum gets hot, teachers should be told about it. When a new activity is added to a course, students could be notified about it. 10. Create a Moodle Lite (sic) Not a bad idea. Perhaps, when a site is installed, a light option could be offered and the list of default plugins and components could be set accordingly. That was what Moodle Flavours was working towards, but it could be even simpler.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Recommendations for Moodle core developers
ResponsesInList.Text:
A general response I wanted to write Paolo (but couldn't find the right way of expressing it, so I'll write it here): We do have these kind of conversations internally all the time. You'll see it on the tracker if you look hard enough - but there is much to learn and improve. Every day is a learning journey! 6. Stop the proliferation of configuration variables

There is a tendency among developers to offer every possible configuration option they can think of. This topic is something I feel strongly in agreement with Paolo about. I hate it. When we offer a choice we confuse new users, we double our testing load, we are not bold enough. But while I do agree its the natural tendency of developers to add configuration options, in Moodle I don't think its the primary cause of the proliferation of options. Often it comes from the fact we have an established community of users and don't want to break their use case, or if we are bold - people shout to add an option to allow the previous behaviour.. I've mellowed about this over the years though, it strikes me that the configurability of Moodle is key to its success across sectors. So my conclusion is really in agreement with Michael - the best way we can play to Moodle's strengths is to work to limit the exposure of configuration options as much as possible. For example - if we add a 'legacy' backwards compatibility option - don't let new users get exposed to it ever! We should choose what is best and enforce that, test against that. Put all our effort into making decisions that make Moodle easy and intuitive to use.

ResponsesInList.Text:
Re: "6. Stop the proliferation of configuration variables
There is a tendency among developers to offer every possible configuration option they can think of." To counter this argument/give the other side, I think it's important to take into consideration those who want to cultivate more autonomous, responsible learners and give them more control over their learning environment. Particularly with capabilities/permissions, it's nice to be able to create detailed profiles to give learners exactly the levels of autonomy and control they need to work collaboratively and responsibly. Also, with grading and feedback; there are so many different theories/approaches to formative and summative assessment that educators need as much flexibility as they can get in order to serve learners' needs. In some contexts you may need rather traditional, conservative grading systems but in others you may need to allow learners to grade themselves and each other. For example, John Hattie's research has identified self-grading as one of the strongest strategies for increasing learning gains. Should we have options that give learners access to edit part or all of their course grade book? Probably. But yes, there are some things that more than likely don't need to be options and probably should be managed in other ways. The thing is not to ignore educators and practitioners on the margins who may not have as loud a voice as the more conservative traditionalists. Just my €0.02

One, tutors appreciate having a reference to something they are familiar so they know what they are creating. Two, textbooks include activities. Three, those activities can involve (and expect) social engagement." My main problem is the "should be considered", not the "a bespoke text book". This makes an assertion that this is the *only* way (or the "best" way) that a Moodle course should be used, which may be true for your institution (based on valid assumptions on ability, available skills, pedagogy), but conversely it's only valid for *some* of our courses, which primarily use the Moodle class as a forum for discussion (say) However to paraphase Jonny Ive, the words that you use constrain the thoughts that people have, so "text" and "book" also instantly narrow down people's ideas on how they may use, in this case, a general purpose package. The ability to derive new forms *does* have to be balanced against familiarity, but neither should familiarity be chosen for the sake of it being familiar and comforting. Finally: I agree that the advanced button isn't great, I like having lots of settings (as an institutional admin) but it would be nice to not have to show them to users if I had to. So the "lock" option on a setting could(should?) actually hide the display of the setting that is locked (e.g. Assignment settings)

And the closest physical metaphor for the Moodle course a teacher is creating is a bespoke textbook, hopefully with cool activities. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Recommendations for Moodle core developers
ResponsesInList.Text: @Dawn Hi... "bespoke textbook" is a metaphor - not a template, plugin, course format, pdf (@jez). The metaphor allows us to understand a Moodle course in relation to a well-establish historical, culturally embedded, of-this-world, familiar object. We know what we are dealing with and, if well used, includes activities made possible through the internet that are not possible through a textbook, pdf, or wor d . Moodle ideally harnesses the power of the web - highlighting and promoting interaction - and encouraging engagement in the learning topics. A metaphor is something related but not the same as - and the textbook metaphor is useful for those who are unfamiliar or need inspiration about how to use Moodle (like some of our tutors) or for developers who need to prioritise what is most important on the development plan. Notifications - yes - social media, blogs, twitter, facebook - tell us about the latest activity - or most active activity - or most relevant activity to your interests. And they are usually the most obvious in your display - at the top of your list. This is how web systems feel dynamic, exciting - the sort of site you want to log on to. This is not like a textbook, no - oh! the contradiction. But that is because you want, and can have, both. We want our students to log on and engage with their curricula activities - often and with enthusiasm so we want our system to be appealing to use. It does this by feeling dynamic and personal. Large images and faces attract further interaction so if you can put a face next to a forum post, activity or assessment feedback then so much the better. That's it for now - have a nice weekend

ResponsesInList.Text: After posting, I suspected it was the 'public' that had made the difference (but didn't have time to test any further. Note, the reasons for leaving out the closing tag is that: PHP automatically assumes a closing tag at the end of the file If you put a closing tag, then it is very easy to put some spaces / tabs / newline characters after this without noticing. Usually this isn't a problem, but if you are serving a binary file (such as an image or a spreadsheet), then the extra, unwanted white space can end up added to the start of the file (or cause PHP to send the HTTP headers early, then complain when you try to send the correct headers). The comment about the closing tag was meant as an aside, rather than being the cause of your existing problem.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Which tables are safe to be truncated ?
ResponsesInList.Text: AFAIR there is a possible condition race when deleting the files, so it may happen that a file is in trashdir while it is still in use - so it's not 100% reliable to just ignore trashdir. It's pretty unlikely though this will affect you if you do the backup when the site is not used (e.g. at night). I think that localcache and temp should be safe to ignore. Weren't overriden strings stored under moodledata/lang? In such a case this one *should* be backed up. Tomek

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Which tables are safe to be truncated ?
ResponsesInList.Text: Correct, `moodledata/lang/*_local` should be included in the backup. All non-local ones are typically fetched from http://download.moodle.org/langpack/ .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Flash embedded question
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Mitesh, Can I assume that you're developing custom Flash activity/quiz generators that pull their data from XML files and possibly other multimedia (i.e. images, audio, video, animations)? If so, repackaging your learning interactions as SCORM packages is likely to be a long, difficult, frustrating process and maybe longer and more expensive than another option (which I'll mention next). I wrote an article on the pros and cons of SCORM here: http://blog.matbury.com/2009/02/16/scorm-the-pros-and-cons/ tl;dr, SCORM's great if you want to make individual, one-off learning interactions and presentations using dedicated SCORM authoring software, e.g. Captivate, Camtasia, Raptivity, or Articulate, but developing and managing large numbers of SCORM packages can become time consuming, tedious, manual labour, and if you want to do something that such SCORM authoring software doesn't provide templates for (they're simply template assembly systems), you're usually stuck (Captivate is more flexible and allows you to edit code and develop apps within SCORM packages if you use Flash Pro). With Moodle 2 onwards and its new file management system, you can no longer upload XML and media files to Moodle in any normal, logical way. Any files that are uploaded and not directly linked to via a Moodle activity or resource will be deleted from the server . This makes multimedia apps particularly difficult to deploy in Moodle. Fortunately, I've been working with these issues for a few years and getting multimedia apps to work in Moodle without SCORM headaches and getting around Moodle file management issues. The SWF Activity Module is designed for custom developed Flash learning activities and integrates Flash apps and Moodle seamlessly. You'll need to add some ActionScript 3.0 code to send user data to Moodle's grade book and you have a lot of flexibility with what data you can store and unlike Moodle's Quiz module, you can also record duration, i.e. time taken on task. SWF Activity Module: https://moodle.org/plugins/view.php?plugin=mod_swf Using a web standard XML schema for learning interactions can make life a
lot easier too. Personally, I like SMIL: http://blog.matbury.com/2011/10/23/whats-smil-and-why-should-we-use-it/ If you want to deploy to HTML only platforms, i.e. ARM CPU devices such as iOS and Android, apps written in ActionScript 3.0 are relatively easy to convert to Javascript (many of the popular 2D, 3D, and mutlimedia JS libraries were ported directly from ActionScript 3.0, e.g. http://createjs.com/#!/CreateJS ). The most recent versions of Adobe Flash Pro have CreateJS built in and can cross-compile to Javascript apps. I hope this helps!

ResponsesInList.Title: Plugins depending on other plugins
ResponsesInList.Text: Long introduction Generally, in Moodle, we like different plugins to be completely independent and self contained. This is nice and simple, but not always possible, and there are various ways plugins can depend on other things. For example: Well, to start with, no plugin is independent, becuase they all depend on Moodle core, and this is completely fine. Then, again, when you have sub-plugins, like Quiz access rules, or Assignment submission types, which necessarily depend on the parent plugins like Quiz or Assignment module. Again, this is to be expected. Now we start to get to more messy scenarios Sometimes, you have an add-on that only makes sense if another add-on in installed. For example Two of my add-ons. Report workflow is only useful if Block workflow is installed. auth_cas requires auth_ldap to be installed, becase CAS extends the functionality provided by LDAP . filter_glossary requires mod_glossary, again this makes sense. A few years ago we introduced $plugin->dependencies in plugin version.php files, to make this explicit, and so that the Moodle install system could make sure that you did not install an add-on without the other required add-ons. This case is now pretty well supported. The final scenario is in the other directly. What if other plugins need to provide some code to work with this plug-in, if it is present. The topical example is Report builder, which they are planning to add to Moodle 2.8. The rest of this post is about this case, which is not currently well supported by Moodle. Further summary of the problem So here are some examples of the problem: The new report-builder tool requires each plugin to describe its data, if data from that plugin is to be included in Report-builder reports. This is done by a class in mod_choice that makes the required information available. This class has to extend a base class in tool_reportbuilder. I have an add-on, report_editdates, which lets you edit all the date settings in your course on a single page. This requires a class for each activity that we want to support, like report_editdates_mod_forum_date_extractor . At the moment we store all those classes inside report/editdates, but that is not extensible. It would be more flexible those classes could be stored inside each separate module. (Though we might still want to keep the classes for core mods inside report_editdates.) Another similar example is the Combined question type, one of the OU question-type add-ons. This lets you build one question out of several other, like qtype_multianswer/Cloze, but better. One way that it is better is that it is extensible. Another qtype can make itself addable to qtype_combined by defining some classes in a folder like question/type/myqtype/combinable, for example in pattern-match . That last issues shows, that really we don't need anything special in Moodle core. You can just get on and do this, by making up your own rules. The point is that it is better for Moodle if we can come up with a standard way to do this for all similar situations. The other point is, we now have a system of automatic class-loading, and we want to work with that. There were recently some rules defined about that, and we should fit in with those rules. I don't think the integrators have written up what was agreed in MDLSITE-2549 yet, so let me summarise. Classes go in a path/to/my/plugin/classes folder. (For plugin with Frankenstyle name type_plugin.) Classes can just go in the root of that folder, in which case the auto-loader will try to find the class type_plugn_class_name in the file path/to/my/plugin/classes/class_name.php. Alternatively, you can use PHP namespaces, in which case the class \type_plugin\sub1\sub2\class_name is looked for in path/to/my/plugin/sub1/sub2/class_name.php. In the name-space case, there are rules about what is allowed for sub1. Basically, you are only allowed to use the names of core components like event, backup, ... there, plus you can have sub1 == local, and inside local you can do whatever you like (so it is like the locallib.php file that a lot of plugins use). Proposed solution So, my proposed solution for the case where other add-ons want to optionally integrate with other plugins, is to extend the rules for what is allowed at leave sub1. Extend the rules so that you can use the frankenstyle name of another plugin there, just like you can refer to core APIs. So, the examples above the classes you would need to create to make the integration work are, for example \mod_choice\tool_reportbuilder\data_description (in mod/choice/classes/tool_reportbuilder/data_description.php) \mod_certificate\report_editdates\date_extractor \qtype_pmatch\qtype_combined\renderer.php and \qtype_pmatch\qtype_combined\combinable.php The plugin that looks for these classes would just find whether another plugin supports it with a class_exists call, and we already have ancore_component::get_plugin_list_with_class() API. Rather than doing this at the sub1 level of namspacing, we could instead declare a new sub1=plugin, and then put the name of the other plugin at sub2 level, like \mod_choice\plugin\tool_reportbuilder\data_description, but I think it is impossible for the Frankenstyle name of an add-on to be the same as the name of a core component, so I prefer the flatter structure. The other proposed solution The reason I make this long boring post now, is that earlier, the Integration team had a secret meeting and came up with their own proposed solution, which so far they have only publised in a comment on a tracker issue https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-30193?focusedCommentId=293371&page=com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.issuetabpanels:comment-tabpanel#comment-293371 . In short their solution is to define a new core API 'reporting' just for the use of plugin tool_reportbuilder. That is all very well for something like report-builder, which is going in to core, but it does not work for add-ons like Edit dates or Combined question types. One of the good trends in Moodle in recent years has been increase the power of what add-ons can do without requiring changes ot Moodle core. The decision the integrators just took seems like a backwards step to me. Please reconsider.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Plugins depending on other plugins
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, nice post, and not boring at all. Really useful to put everything in context . Thanks! Said, that, I can imagine my answer is going to be longer and more boring than your initial post, so here it's my sincerest apology in advance. Also, I'll be trying to split the information into "chapters", so everything gets more organized and readable. The secret meeting First of all, for the sake of transparency, let me share that we (the integration team - iTeam), after every major release, use to have a meeting, sort of retrospective, where we discuss about practically everything (in fact that discussion happened in the 5th session of the meeting, spread along the past 3 weeks, so you can imagine how long it is). While those meetings are happening, new points are added to the agenda and that’s how the discussion about inter-plugin communication landed there (last point, if I’m not wrong), in the context of the report builder and its integration into core. I think the context is pretty important, please, don’t forget it. The discussion was basically about clarifying some concepts of the report builder (that personally I haven’t “tasted” yet), and then, about which should be it’s ideal (in our opinion) way to land to core. Of course, constructive, looking-forward, open-minded (I think that term was exactly used) and not final. There is only one dictator in this Community, and the iTeam is not him. And then, yes, we communicated it wrongly. More explanations and details, a proposal for discussion… were needed. So all I can say is sorry and that we’ll try to do it better next time. In any case, that does not change much the opinion about how the report builder case should be integrated into core, let’s talk about that (at last!). Components, plugins, subsystems and APIs. Just to be sure that we are all taking the same language, I think it’s needed to briefly comment about all those concepts. While they are pretty simple (in theory), I see them continuously used/replaced wrongly here and there (for example the “event”, “backup”… in the initial post… are not components at all, but APIs). And that leads to confusion. Components , (covering both plugins and subsystems), are the original effort to organize Moodle into differentiated areas. That included some agreed naming schema (the famous Frankenstyle ) and some shared functionalities: support for own lang strings, (originally) support for own database schema, install & upgrade, prefixing all constants and functions, phpdocs @package, renderers support… and few more niceties. Plugins (and subplugins), for sure the most famous components. Easy to identify, they are grouped into plugin types (auth, enrol, blocks, activities, filters… and many, many more). They are physically confined within a directory and, as far as they support easy installation & upgrade really good for everybody wanting to add/extend functionality to Moodle. So, there it is. The Moodle plugins database . Worth commenting that, no matter they all are plugins… since some months ago it was agreed that we were going to call “plugins” to the plugins distributed with Moodle releases and “add-ons” to the plugins not distributed with Moodle. All them are plugins, just we call them differently. Subsystems , the 2nd type of components. I really don’t want to comment much about these ones, just imagine them as some sort of organization with some extra functionalities as commented above. My very-personal POV (unrelated to this discussion) is that, along the time, they should be phased out and just have plugins and APIs. But that’s another story to be written in the future. So keep them apart, please. For the rest of the post I’ll be using the “plugins” word exclusively. APIs , first of all, they are not components. Ignore if there is any overlapping with the Moodle subsystems (some of them are APIs really) and everything you know about components. APIs are the core-core or Moodle, and they define how everything else must work and interact. Of course, they are legion , because Moodle is a big-mammoth (that’s one of the best secrets revealed, the real meaning of the “M”, LOL). They define how things must work at all levels and provide the rest of Moodle (other APIs, plugins and add-ons) with a specification about how to perform a lot of tasks (install & upgrade, database access, files handling, langs support, logging, ws implementation, testing…) and also provide some functionality to be used where necessary (grades, comments, rating, rss…). Finally, worth note that those APIs are becoming more and more important (in detriment of the subsystems, I’d say), and we gave them a really prominent position into the Namespaces agreement , reserving the whole “level2” for them (plus “local” that was decided to be allowed for plugins own stuff at 3rd level). Basically the rule is that any namespaced class (apart from the “local” bits and bobs case commented) must, always, follow this simple scheme: component_name \[api_name\] class_name And this is all we need to know to continue… 95% of agreement Yes, no surprises. I can say, without a problem, that I agree with 95% of the contents of Tim’s initial post. Indeed: All plugins depend of core. Just let me add “and its APIs”. I suppose nobody will object. Subplugins depend of their parent plugins. Correct, nothing to object. A plugin is responsible to control its children. There may be “dependencies” between different plugins. Can be architectural ones (extension) or data-access ones. Note I’m not 100% happy with how we use to perform that “raw access” (database, files…) between them and IMO it should be more controlled but, for its simplicity, and being proved to work, it’s accepted. Plus we are able to control such dependencies at install/upgrade. Ok. A plugin provides some functionality to other plugins by its own (aka, bypassing, core). Beep, beep, disagreement! Indeed! I really hope that, at this moment, it’s clear for everybody that the 4th point is the controversy one and everything else, that already covers a lot of inter-plugin dependencies, are not a problem at all . Let’s elaborate about that point a bit more by commenting about your 3rd case in the “Further summary of the problem”: Another similar example is the Combined question type, one of the OU question-type add-ons. This lets you build one question out of several other, like qtype_multianswer/Cloze, but better. One way that it is better is that it is extensible. Another qtype can make itself addable to qtype_combined by defining some classes in a folder like question/type/myqtype/combinable, for example in pattern-match. Pretty interesting, because it defines a new case, not explicitly defined in the 1-4 list above, but being a particular case of the controversial 4 (or perhaps a new case of 3). A plugin of a plugin type (qtype), combining with another plugins of the same plugin type (qtype). For that, you can use 2 approaches. Or you implement such combination abilities by controlling it at plugin type level (sort of API within the constraints of the plugin type). Or you implement that ability between plugins, straight between them, bypassing completely that qtype commons API. Personally I’d prefer to bring the functionality to the (higher level) plugin-type level, so you can define there what is needed in order to allow that work for a given question type. But, no matter of that… still… I’d say. No objection there. As far as a given functionality is within the limits of a plugin type (qtype), dependencies can be implemented as you prefer. So let’s add that point to the list of agreements and forget about it: 4a. A plugin type, constrained within its limits, can implement inter-plugin dependencies without a problem. And, obviously, that keep us with the disagreement way more reduced : 4b. A plugin provides some functionality to any other, unrelated, plugin. Do we agree that’s the problematic one? Hope so. Ok, I’m going to sleep some good hours (05:00 AM here is really insane)… in the mean time it would be great if we all could: Erase any previous knowledge / experience you can have about / with the report builder. That’s my current situation. And IMO it’s the key to see the forest behind the plugin current incarnation (the trees). Have you been able? No? Try again, please. Thanks. Great! … to be continued… I warned it was going to be long, ciao
